definition_zh: 继承（物）；遗产；遗传；（文化）传承；继承权
definition_en: property or a right received from someone who has died, or the transmission of traits and traditions from one generation to the next
core_image: 一只旧木匣装着钥匙与地契，从一双手递到另一双手，匣盖上的封蜡已经裂开
scene: 老宅的钥匙和地契被装进同一个木匣，交到下一代手里。 The eldest daughter received the farm as her inheritance.
sceneCN: 这里 inheritance 指「从去世的亲人那里接下的财产」（第 1 个义项：继承所得的财物）；句意为长女把这座农场作为遗产接了下来。可辨识物件：木匣、黄铜钥匙、地契、裂开的封蜡。

forms.label: 复数（可用，但常作不可数）

senses.title: Property received after a death
senses.titleCN: 从逝者那里接下的财产
senses.definition: money or property passed to an heir after someone dies
senses.definitionCN: 某人去世后传给继承人的钱财或财产
senses.example: She used her inheritance to buy the workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 她用继承来的钱买下了那间作坊。
senses.why: The word names what is handed over at death, so the first sense is the concrete estate rather than the act of receiving it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指在死亡时被交出的东西，因此第一个义项是具体的遗产，而不是领取的动作。

senses.title: The act or right of inheriting
senses.definition: the legal act or right by which an heir receives an estate
senses.definitionCN: 继承人取得遗产的法定行为或权利
senses.example: The inheritance of the land was disputed for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地的继承权争了多年。
senses.why: Because the noun covers both the thing and the legal relation, English can speak of an inheritance and of the right of inheritance.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个名词同时涵盖财物与法律关系，英语既能说「一份遗产」，也能说「继承权」。

senses.title: Genetic transmission
senses.definition: the passing of traits from parents to offspring through genes
senses.definitionCN: 性状经基因由亲代传给子代
senses.example: Eye colour shows a simple pattern of inheritance.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛颜色呈现出简单的遗传模式。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century biology borrowed the legal word because traits seemed to be handed down like property.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪的生物学借用了这个法律词，因为性状看起来像财产一样被传下去。

senses.title: Cultural heritage
senses.definition: the traditions, language or art received from earlier generations
senses.definitionCN: 从更早世代接下的传统、语言或艺术
senses.example: The city claims the inheritance of three empires.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市自称承袭了三个帝国的遗产。
senses.why: The legal frame widened to anything received from the past, so a city can inherit an empire's habits of building.
senses.whyCN: 法律框架被拓宽到任何从过去接下的东西，因此一座城市可以继承一个帝国的建造习惯。

senses.title: A burden or condition passed on
senses.titleCN: 一并接下的负担或状况
senses.definition: a debt, problem or condition that comes with what is received
senses.definitionCN: 随所得之物一起到来的债务、问题或状况
senses.example: He carries an inheritance of debt from the previous owner.
senses.exampleCN: 他背上了前任业主留下的一身债务。
senses.why: What is inherited is not always a gift; the word can name the liabilities that arrive with the property.
senses.whyCN: 被继承的不总是礼物；这个词也能指随财产一起到来的负担。

senses.title: Class inheritance in computing
senses.definition: the mechanism by which one class or module takes properties from a parent
senses.definitionCN: 一个类或模块从父级取得属性的机制
senses.example: Class inheritance lets one module reuse another's methods.
senses.exampleCN: 类继承让一个模块可以复用另一个模块的方法。
senses.why: Programming borrowed the family metaphor: a child class receives behaviour from its parent, just as an heir receives property.
senses.whyCN: 编程借用了家庭隐喻：子类从父类取得行为，正如继承人取得财产。

senses.title: Inheritance tax and legal thresholds
senses.definition: the tax charged on an estate before or after it passes to heirs
senses.definitionCN: 遗产传给继承人之前或之后所征的税
senses.example: Inheritance tax applies above a fixed threshold.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产税适用于超过固定起征点的部分。
senses.why: Once the state began taxing transfers at death, the noun became fixed in the compound inheritance tax.
senses.whyCN: 当国家开始对死亡时的财产转移征税后，这个名词就固定于遗产税这一复合词中。

senses.title: A legacy of consequences
senses.definition: the lasting effects that one period or action leaves to those who follow
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期或行动留给后来者的持久影响
senses.example: The reform left an inheritance of distrust.
senses.exampleCN: 这场改革留下了一份不信任的遗产。
senses.why: The metaphor treats consequences as an estate: later people receive them whether they want them or not.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻把后果当作一份产业：后来者不管愿不愿意都得接收。

intro.en: Inheritance comes from Anglo-French enheritance, from enheriter 'to make an heir', from Late Latin inhereditare, built on heres (hered-) 'heir'.
intro.cn: inheritance 来自盎格鲁-法语 enheritance，源自动词 enheriter「立为继承人」，再上溯为晚期拉丁 inhereditare，其词干是 heres（hered-）「继承人」。

items.en: Heres (genitive heredis) meant 'heir'. Its deeper origin is not established; suggestions linking it to other Indo-European words are hypotheses, and any PIE form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: heres（属格 heredis）意为「继承人」。其更深来源未得到确证；把它与其他印欧语词联系起来的说法只是假说，凡为其给出的原始印欧语形式均属重构形式。

items.en: Hereditas 'inheritance, heirship' and hereditarius 'of an heir' were formed on the hered- stem.
items.cn: hereditas「继承、继承权」与 hereditarius「继承人的」都建立在 hered- 词干上。

items.en: In- 'in, into' plus hereditare 'to inherit' gave inhereditare 'to appoint as heir'.
items.cn: in-「进入」加 hereditare「继承」构成 inhereditare「立为继承人」。

items.en: Enheriter and its noun enheritance reached English in the fourteenth century; legal use came first, and the exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: enheriter 及其名词 enheritance 在 14 世纪进入英语；法律用法最先出现，确切的最早书证不确定。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the word was extended to the transmission of traits, alongside the new science of heredity.
items.cn: 19 世纪，随着遗传学兴起，这个词被扩展到性状传递。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): first dates for the biological sense are approximate, and the pre-Latin origin of heres remains uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：生物学义项的首见年代只是约数，heres 在拉丁语之前的来源仍不确定。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same hered- stem or that merely look similar; group two holds the legal and everyday words for what is left to heirs.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 hered- 词干或仅形近的词；第二组是法律与日常语境中表示「留给继承人的东西」的近义词。

entries.tag: same root what is handed down
entries.definition: The same Latin hered- stem, but heritage usually names cultural or family possessions rather than a legal share.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁 hered- 词干，但 heritage 通常指文化或家族传承物，而非法定份额。

entries.definition: The biological transmission of traits, not the property received; the two words split in the nineteenth century.
entries.definitionCN: 指性状的生物传递，而非所收财产；两个词在 19 世纪分化。

entries.definition: The person who receives, not the thing received; the suffix -or marks the agent.
entries.definitionCN: 指接收的人，而非所收之物；后缀 -or 标记施事者。

entries.definition: From inhaerere 'to stick in', not heres: the state of being inherent or built into something. The resemblance is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 inhaerere「黏附于内」，并非 heres：指内在于某物的状态。相似只是偶然。

entries.definition: A specific gift left in a will; inheritance can also mean the whole estate or the right to it.
entries.definitionCN: 遗嘱中留下的具体馈赠；inheritance 还可指全部遗产或继承权。

entries.definition: Property given by a will, usually personal items; narrower and more legal than inheritance.
entries.definitionCN: 遗嘱赠予的财产，通常为个人物品；比 inheritance 更窄、更法律化。

entries.definition: The total property a person leaves, before it is divided among heirs.
entries.definitionCN: 某人留下的全部财产，在分配给继承人之前。

entries.definition: Money or property given to an institution, often to produce income; it stresses the lasting gift rather than the heir.
entries.definitionCN: 捐给机构的钱或财产，常用来产生收益；强调持续的馈赠而非继承人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'in' + heres 'heir': being put into the heir's place.
normal.cn: in-「进入」+ heres「继承人」：被放进继承人的位置。

normal.en: The family runs inherit, inheritance, inheritor, inheritable, hereditary and heredity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 inherit、inheritance、inheritor、inheritable、hereditary 与 heredity。

normal.en: Legal use came first; the biological use is a nineteenth-century extension.
normal.cn: 法律用法最先出现，生物学用法是 19 世纪的扩展。

normal.en: In computing, inheritance means a subclass takes methods from its parent.
normal.cn: 在计算机中，inheritance 指子类从父类取得方法。

normal.en: Fixed phrase: inheritance tax.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：遗产税。

abstract.en: Picture a house key passed from hand to hand until the first hand is forgotten.
abstract.cn: 想象一把房门钥匙被一双手传一双手，直到最初那双手被遗忘。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe card whose stains are inherited along with the recipe.
abstract.cn: 想象一张食谱卡，油渍和做法一起被继承下来。

abstract.en: Picture a debt that arrives with the furniture and has no invoice.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔债务随家具一起到来，却没有账单。

examples.en: The inheritance was divided equally among the four children.
examples.cn: 遗产在四个孩子之间平均分配。

examples.en: Researchers traced the inheritance of the trait across five generations.
examples.cn: 研究者追踪了这一性状在五代人中的遗传。

examples.en: Class inheritance reduced the amount of code the team had to write.
examples.cn: 类继承减少了团队需要编写的代码量。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进入）+ herit（继承人）——进入继承人的位置 → 继承（物）；同根的 heritage 是「传承物」。

root: 拉丁 hereditas「继承、继承权」← heres（hered-）「继承人」；经古法语 enheritance 进入英语；heres 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one handover: a box passes at death and becomes property, a right, a biological trait, a culture, a burden, a piece of code, a tax and finally a set of consequences.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次交接展开：一只匣子在死亡时被递出，成为财产、权利、生物性状、文化、负担、代码、税，最后成为一整套后果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden box of keys and deeds passing from one hand to the next.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只装着钥匙与地契的木匣，从一双手递到另一双手。

branches.en: PROPERTY AND RIGHT: the estate itself and the legal power to receive it.
branches.cn: 财产与权利：遗产本身，以及取得它的法定资格。

branches.en: WHAT IS TRANSMITTED: a trait can arrive like property, and so can a debt.
branches.cn: 被传递之物：性状可以像财产一样到来，债务也可以。

branches.en: CULTURE: buildings, language and habits are received from earlier generations.
branches.cn: 文化：建筑、语言与习惯从更早世代接下。

branches.en: COMPUTING: a child class receives behaviour from its parent class.
branches.cn: 计算机：子类从父类取得行为。

branches.en: TAX AND CONSEQUENCE: the state takes a share, and later people receive the effects.
branches.cn: 税与后果：国家取走一份，后来者接收影响。

intro.en: Inheritance is built from a Latin prefix and the hered- stem, and the same pieces form a large legal and biological family.
intro.cn: inheritance 由拉丁前缀与 hered- 词干构成，这些成分组成了一个庞大的法律与生物词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres (hered-) gives hereditas, hereditarius, inherit and inheritance; in- adds the sense of entering a position.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 heres（hered-）衍生 hereditas、hereditarius、inherit 与 inheritance；in- 增添「进入某一位置」的意思。

items.example: The prefix places the receiver inside the heir's position.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把接收者放进继承人的位置。

items.example: The stem names the person who receives.

items.meaning: to inherit; to leave as an inheritance
items.example: Hereditare turned the heir into an action.
items.exampleCN: hereditare 把「继承人」变成了动作。

items.example: The Late Latin verb added the legal act of naming an heir.
items.exampleCN: 晚期拉丁动词增添了指定继承人的法律动作。

items.structure: English verb from Old French enheriter
items.example: She inherited the house from her aunt.
items.exampleCN: 她从姑妈那里继承了这所房子。

items.meaning: the estate or the act of receiving it
items.example: The inheritance was divided among the children.
items.exampleCN: 遗产在孩子们之间分配。
继承人在契据上签了字。

items.example: The trait is inheritable in a simple pattern.
items.exampleCN: 这一性状以简单模式可遗传。

items.meaning: to cut an heir out of a will
items.example: The old man disinherited his nephew.
items.exampleCN: 老人剥夺了侄子的继承权。
这座城市保护自己的文化遗产。

definition_zh: 遗传的；世袭的；继承的
definition_en: passed from parents to offspring through genes, or transmitted by legal succession from one generation to the next
core_image: 家族相册里，几代人的手形几乎一模一样，连指节的弯度都对得上
scene: 家族相册里，几代人的手形几乎一模一样。 A hereditary trait ran through every generation of the family.
sceneCN: 这里 hereditary 指「由上一代经遗传传下来的」（第 1 个义项：经基因传递的）；句意为一种遗传性状贯穿了这个家族的每一代。可辨识物件：相册、放大的手部照片、家谱线、铅笔标记。

derivatives.zh: 可继承的财产（法律用语）

senses.title: Passed through genes
senses.definition: transmitted from parents to offspring through genetic material
senses.definitionCN: 通过遗传物质由亲代传给子代
senses.example: Hereditary deafness runs in that family.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传性耳聋在那个家族中代代出现。
senses.why: The adjective describes a trait whose cause travels in the genes, so it names the route rather than the illness itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词描述病因随基因传递的性状，因此命名的是传递路径，而非疾病本身。

senses.title: Inherited from ancestors
senses.definition: received from an ancestor rather than acquired in one's own lifetime
senses.definitionCN: 从祖先处承接，而非在本人一生中获得
senses.example: The tendency is partly hereditary.
senses.exampleCN: 这种倾向有一部分是遗传的。
senses.why: The word can soften a claim: partly hereditary means ancestry contributes without settling the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以缓和断言：部分遗传意味着祖先有贡献，但并不决定结果。

senses.title: Transmitted by succession
senses.definition: passed down by legal or customary succession rather than election
senses.definitionCN: 按法律或习俗世袭传递，而非经选举
senses.example: The duke held a hereditary seat in the old assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 公爵在旧议会中拥有一个世袭席位。
senses.why: Law uses the same adjective for offices because a seat can pass to an heir just as an estate can.
senses.whyCN: 法律用同一个形容词描述职位，因为席位也能像产业一样传给继承人。

senses.title: Of hereditary monarchy
senses.definition: describing a system in which the head of state succeeds by birth
senses.definitionCN: 描述国家元首按出生顺序继位的制度
senses.example: The country replaced hereditary rule with elections.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家用选举取代了世袭统治。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to institutions, not only to bodies, when rule itself is handed down.
senses.whyCN: 当统治权本身被传下时，这个形容词也附着于制度，而不只是身体。

senses.title: Of hereditary material
senses.definition: relating to the material that carries genes from one cell to the next
senses.definitionCN: 与把基因从一代细胞带到下一代细胞的物质相关
senses.example: Hereditary material is copied into every cell.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传物质被复制进每一个细胞。
senses.why: In biology the adjective can modify the carrier as well as the trait, which is why hereditary material is a fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 在生物学中，这个形容词既能修饰性状，也能修饰载体，因此「遗传物质」成为固定搭配。

senses.title: Of a hereditary predisposition
senses.definition: describing an inherited tendency that raises risk without causing the condition alone
senses.definitionCN: 描述提高风险但并不单独致病的遗传倾向
senses.example: A hereditary predisposition does not guarantee illness.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传易感性并不保证一定患病。
senses.why: The word separates inheritance from inevitability: a predisposition is a loaded starting point, not a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「遗传」与「必然」分开：易感性是一个有负载的起点，而不是判决。

senses.title: Legally inheritable
senses.definition: able to pass to an heir under the law
senses.definitionCN: 依法可以传给继承人
senses.example: The estate was hereditary and could not be sold.
senses.exampleCN: 这份产业属于可继承财产，不能出售。
senses.why: Property law uses the adjective for land and rights that must descend rather than be traded freely.
senses.whyCN: 财产法用这个形容词描述必须下传、不能自由买卖的土地与权利。

senses.title: Carried down from the past
senses.definition: describing an attitude or conflict handed down so long that it seems inborn
senses.definitionCN: 描述传得太久、仿佛天生的态度或冲突
senses.example: The two villages were hereditary enemies.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个村子是世代相传的仇敌。
senses.why: The metaphor treats hostility as an estate: children receive a quarrel they never chose.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻把敌意当作产业：孩子们接收了一场他们从未选择的争吵。

intro.en: Hereditary comes from Latin hereditarius 'of an inheritance', from hereditas 'inheritance', from heres (hered-) 'heir'.
intro.cn: hereditary 来自拉丁 hereditarius「继承的」，再上溯 hereditas「继承」与 heres（hered-）「继承人」。

items.en: Heres (genitive heredis) meant 'heir'. Its deeper origin is not established; links to other Indo-European words are hypotheses, and any PIE form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: heres（属格 heredis）意为「继承人」。其更深来源未得到确证；与其他印欧语词的联系只是假说，任何原始印欧语形式均属重构。

items.en: Hereditarius 'of an inheritance' was formed from hereditas; the adjective suffix -arius marks belonging or relation.
items.cn: hereditarius「继承的」由 hereditas 构成；形容词后缀 -arius 表示归属或关系。

items.en: English took hereditary from Latin or French in the fifteenth or sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在 15 或 16 世纪从拉丁语或法语借入 hereditary；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The legal sense survives in hereditary titles and hereditary peers, where office passes by birth rather than election.
items.cn: 法律义残存于世袭头衔与世袭贵族，其职位按出生而非选举传递。

items.en: The biological sense developed in the nineteenth century, when heredity became a research subject and traits were traced through families.
items.cn: 生物学义在 19 世纪发展起来，当时遗传成为研究课题，性状被沿家族追踪。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): heres has no established pre-Latin etymology, and the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：heres 没有已确立的拉丁语之前词源，英语首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same hered- family that differ in grammar or nuance; group two holds adjectives that also describe what is present from birth or runs in families.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 hered- 词族、但语法角色或侧重不同的词；第二组是同样描述「出生即有」或「家族中常见」的形容词。

entries.definition: The process or system of transmission; hereditary is the adjective describing what is transmitted.
entries.definitionCN: 指传递过程或系统；hereditary 是描述被传递之物的形容词。

entries.definition: Able to be inherited, often used of traits or property; hereditary describes the actual transmission or legal status.
entries.definitionCN: 指能够被继承，常用于性状或财产；hereditary 描述实际的传递或法律地位。

entries.definition: A legal term for inheritable property; it is a noun of things, not a trait.
entries.definitionCN: 指可继承财产的法律术语；它是事物名词，不是性状。

entries.definition: The adverb form; it describes how something is transmitted rather than what it is.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式；描述传递方式，而非事物本身。

entries.definition: The ordinary participle from inherit; hereditary is the fixed adjective, especially in biology and law.
entries.definitionCN: inherit 的普通分词；hereditary 是固定形容词，尤用于生物学与法律。

entries.tag: present at birth not always geneti
entries.definition: Present at birth; a congenital condition may arise during development and need not be hereditary.
entries.definitionCN: 指出生时即存在；先天状况可能在发育中形成，未必是遗传的。

entries.definition: Occurring in a family more often than chance; familial does not prove a genetic cause.
entries.definitionCN: 指在家族中发生率高于偶然；familial 并不证明存在遗传原因。

entries.definition: The broad modern adjective; hereditary emphasises transmission from ancestors, genetic emphasises the genes themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 宽泛的现代形容词；hereditary 强调从祖先传递，genetic 强调基因本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: heres 'heir' + -ary: belonging to an inheritance.
normal.cn: heres「继承人」+ -ary：属于继承的。

normal.en: The family runs hereditary, heredity, hereditarily and hereditament.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 hereditary、heredity、hereditarily 与 hereditament。

normal.en: Law fixes hereditary peer and hereditary title; biology fixes hereditary disease.
normal.cn: 法律固定搭配世袭贵族、世袭头衔；生物学固定搭配遗传性疾病。

normal.en: Hereditary peer describes a seat, not a gene.
normal.cn: 世袭贵族描述的是席位，不是基因。

normal.en: A hereditary predisposition raises risk without deciding the outcome.
normal.cn: 遗传易感性提高风险，却不决定结果。

abstract.en: Picture a seal stamped on every generation of a document.
abstract.cn: 想象每一代文件上都盖着同一枚印章。

abstract.en: Picture a tune learned before birth and never questioned.
abstract.cn: 想象一支在出生前就学会、从不被质疑的曲子。

abstract.en: Picture a title that comes with the furniture, not with a vote.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头衔随家具而来，而不是随选票而来。

examples.en: The condition is hereditary, though not everyone who carries the gene falls ill.
examples.cn: 这种病是遗传的，但并非每个携带该基因的人都会发病。

examples.en: Hereditary peers lost their voting rights in the reform.
examples.cn: 世袭贵族在改革中失去了投票权。

examples.en: The museum refused to sell the hereditary collection.
examples.cn: 博物馆拒绝出售这批世袭收藏。

dict_mnemonic.text: hered（继承人）+ itary（形容词尾）——与继承人相关的 → 世袭的、遗传的。

root: 拉丁 hereditarius「继承的」← hereditas「继承」← heres（hered-）「继承人」；heres 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a stamp that keeps reappearing: in genes, in ancestry, in offices, in monarchy, in cellular material, in risk, in property law and finally in inherited hostility.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一枚反复出现的印章展开：出现在基因、祖先、职位、君主制、细胞物质、风险、财产法，最后出现在沿袭的敌意中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same hand shape appearing in photograph after photograph.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一手形在一张又一张照片中反复出现。

branches.en: GENETIC AND ANCESTRAL: a trait travels through genes and is received from ancestors.
branches.cn: 遗传与祖先：性状经基因传递，并从祖先处承接。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND RISK: the carrier itself, and an inherited tendency that only raises risk.
branches.cn: 物质与风险：载体本身，以及只提高风险的遗传倾向。

branches.en: OFFICE AND RULE: seats and crowns pass by birth rather than election.
branches.cn: 职位与统治：席位与王冠按出生而非选举传递。

branches.en: PROPERTY LAW: land and rights that must descend to heirs.
branches.cn: 财产法：必须下传给继承人的土地与权利。

branches.en: INHERITED HOSTILITY: an old quarrel arrives like an estate.
branches.cn: 沿袭的敌意：旧日争吵像产业一样被接收。

intro.en: Hereditary is an adjective built on the Latin hered- stem plus a suffix, and the same stem builds a legal and biological family.
intro.cn: hereditary 是由拉丁 hered- 词干加后缀构成的形容词，同一词干还构成法律与生物词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres (hered-) gives hereditas, hereditarius, hereditary, heredity and inherit; -arius marks belonging.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 heres（hered-）衍生 hereditas、hereditarius、hereditary、heredity 与 inherit；-arius 标记归属关系。

items.example: The stem names the person who receives.
Hereditas named the estate and the relation together.
items.exampleCN: hereditas 同时命名产业与关系。

items.example: The adjective added -arius to the stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在词干后加 -arius。

items.example: The suffix turns the stem into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词干变成描述词。
这一性状以遗传方式传递。
契据列明了每一项可继承财产。

items.example: The debate drew both hereditarians and environmentalists.
items.exampleCN: 这场争论吸引了遗传论者与环境论者。

definition_zh: 苦苦挣扎；焦虑不安；为（决定）反复纠结；忍受煎熬
definition_en: to spend a long time worrying about a decision or problem without reaching an answer; also to endure prolonged physical or mental pain
core_image: 在赛场上扭着身子较劲，久久分不出胜负
scene: 两份录取通知摊在桌上，她整晚翻来翻去。 She agonized over which offer to accept.
sceneCN: 这里 agonize 是「反复纠结、焦虑不安」（第 1 个义项：为某个决定长时间痛苦挣扎）；句意为她整晚为该接受哪份录取而纠结。核心画面是在赛场上扭着身子较劲，久久分不出胜负。

pos.zh: 苦苦挣扎；焦虑不安；久拖不决

derivatives.zh: 英式拼写，与 agonize 同义，义为「苦苦纠结」
现在分词作形容词，义为「令人痛苦煎熬的」
加 -ly 构成，义为「令人煎熬地；极其缓慢地」
同根名词，义为「极度痛苦；煎熬」

senses.title: To suffer over a choice
senses.definition: to spend a long time worrying about a decision or a problem, turning it over without reaching an answer
senses.definitionCN: 为某个决定或问题长时间担忧，反复思量却得不到答案
senses.example: He agonized over the wording of a two-line email.
senses.exampleCN: 他为一封两行邮件的措辞纠结了很久。
senses.why: Agon was a contest in which athletes strained against each other, so agonize keeps the picture of an inner match that neither side wins.
senses.whyCN: agon 是运动员彼此较力的竞赛，所以 agonize 保留了一场内心比赛的画面：双方谁也赢不了。

senses.title: To drag on in pain
senses.definition: to endure prolonged physical or mental pain, or to make a process painfully slow, the older and heavier sense
senses.definitionCN: 忍受长时间的身心痛苦，或使某个过程慢得令人难受，是更古老、更沉重的用法
senses.example: The injured runner agonized through the final lap.
senses.exampleCN: 受伤的跑者煎熬着跑完最后一圈。
senses.why: Here the contest is against pain itself rather than against a choice, which is exactly how the Greek word was first used.
senses.whyCN: 这里较劲的对手是痛苦本身，而不是某个选择，这正是该希腊词最初的用法。

intro.en: Agonize comes from the Greek games: agon was a contest, agonizesthai was to compete in it, and English turned that public struggle into a private one.
intro.cn: agonize 来自希腊的竞技：agon 是竞赛，agonizesthai 是在其中角逐，英语把这种公开的较劲变成了内心的挣扎。

items.en: Greek agon meant a gathering and then a contest, especially the athletic contests at the great games.
items.cn: 希腊语 agon 先指集会，后指竞赛，尤指大型运动会上的竞技。

items.en: From agon came agonia, the strain of competing, which already covered mental anguish.
items.cn: 由 agon 派生出 agonia，即角逐时的紧绷状态，已涵盖精神上的痛苦。

items.en: The verb agonizesthai meant to contend for a prize, to struggle in the arena.
items.cn: 动词 agonizesthai 意为「争夺奖赏」，即在竞技场上奋力拼搏。

items.en: Late Latin agonizare kept the sense of struggling, and was used of the last struggle before death.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 agonizare 保留「挣扎」之义，并用于指临终前的最后挣扎。

items.en: French agoniser meant to be at the point of death, a narrowing that English later widened again.
items.cn: 法语 agoniser 意为「濒死」，这一收窄后来又被英语重新拓宽。

items.en: English agonize now covers both physical suffering and the everyday torment of choosing, with agonise as the British spelling.
items.cn: 现代英语 agonize 既指身体上的痛苦，也指日常抉择的煎熬，英式拼写作 agonise。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the agon- family of contest and pain; the near-meaning group lists other verbs for worrying at length.
note.cn: 形近组留在表示「竞赛与痛苦」的 agon- 词族内；近义组列出其他表示「长时间担忧」的动词。

entries.definition: Extreme physical or mental suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 极度的身心痛苦。

entries.definition: Causing great pain or anxious delay.
entries.definitionCN: 令人极度痛苦或焦急拖延的。

entries.definition: A person who opposes or competes against another.
entries.definitionCN: 与他人对立或竞争的人。

entries.definition: The leading character in a story or contest.
entries.definitionCN: 故事或竞赛中的主角。

entries.definition: To worry continually about small things.
entries.definitionCN: 为小事不停地烦恼。

entries.definition: To think darkly and at length about something.
entries.definitionCN: 阴郁而长久地想着某事。

entries.definition: To hesitate, unable to decide.
entries.definitionCN: 犹豫不决，拿不定主意。

entries.definition: To struggle with a difficult problem.
entries.definitionCN: 与难题奋力搏斗。

normalIntro.en: Agonize is agon, contest, plus -ize, to act: to keep competing inside your own head.
normalIntro.cn: agonize 就是 agon「竞赛」加 -ize「做……」：在自己脑子里不停地比赛。

normal.en: Agony and agonize share agon, so wherever you see agon- think of a contest that hurts.
normal.cn: agony 与 agonize 共享 agon，所以见到 agon- 就想到一场让人难受的竞赛。

normal.en: Agonize over a choice, agonize about a situation: over points at the thing you must pick.
normal.cn: agonize over 后接要挑的东西，agonize about 后接让人担忧的处境。

normal.en: American spelling ends in -ize, British in -ise: agonize and agonise are the same verb.
normal.cn: 美式拼写以 -ize 结尾，英式以 -ise 结尾：agonize 与 agonise 是同一个动词。

normal.en: The -ing form works as an adjective, as in an agonizing wait.
normal.cn: -ing 形式可作形容词，如 an agonizing wait（煎熬的等待）。

normal.en: It is usually intransitive, so say agonize over it, not agonize it.
normal.cn: 它通常不及物，所以说 agonize over it，不说 agonize it。

abstract.en: Picture two wrestlers locked in your chest, neither able to pin the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两个摔跤手在你胸口僵持，谁也压不倒谁。

abstract.en: Imagine a stadium where the only event is deciding, and it never ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一座体育场，唯一的项目是「做决定」，而且永不结束。

abstract.en: Think of a clock whose hands move only while you worry.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，只有在你担忧时指针才走动。

examples.en: She agonized for weeks before handing in her resignation.
examples.cn: 她纠结了好几个星期才递交辞呈。

examples.en: Do not agonize over a sentence nobody will read twice.
examples.cn: 别为一个没人会读第二遍的句子反复纠结。

examples.en: The whole family agonized while the results were pending.
examples.cn: 结果未定的那段时间，全家人都在煎熬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱哥奈兹」——爱（a）哥（go）奈（n）兹（ize）：心里两个小人比赛，谁也不服谁，就是苦苦纠结、焦虑不安。

root: 希腊语 agon「集会、竞赛」派生出 agonia「角逐的紧绷」与 agonizesthai「争夺奖赏」，经晚期拉丁语 agonizare「挣扎」与法语 agoniser「濒死」进入英语，加动词后缀 -ize 构成 agonize，字面即「像竞技一样持续较劲」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are a contest that will not end: in one you wrestle with a choice, in the other with pain, and in each the struggle itself is the point.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是一场不肯结束的竞赛：一个与选择较劲，一个与痛苦较劲，两者都以「挣扎本身」为重点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an inner contest with no winner
core.cn: 核心意象：一场分不出胜负的内心竞赛

branches.en: Turning a choice over all night.
branches.cn: 整晚把一个选择翻来覆去地想。

branches.en: Rewriting one sentence again and again.
branches.cn: 把一句话改了一遍又一遍。

branches.en: Pushing through pain to finish.
branches.cn: 忍着痛苦坚持到结束。

branches.en: A wait that feels longer than the clock says.
branches.cn: 一段比钟表所示更漫长的等待。

branches.en: Both keep the struggle going without a result.
branches.cn: 两者都让挣扎持续而没有结果。

intro.en: Agonize belongs to the agon- family, where the root always names a contest and the suffix decides whether you get a noun, a verb or an adjective.
intro.cn: agonize 属于 agon- 词族，词根永远表示竞赛，后缀决定你得到的是名词、动词还是形容词。

latinIntro.en: Greek agon passed through late Latin agonizare and French agoniser before English added the verb suffix -ize.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 agon 经晚期拉丁语 agonizare 与法语 agoniser，再由英语加上动词后缀 -ize。

latinEntries.example: Agon is the root of the whole family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: agon 是整个词族的词根。
agonia 已表示痛苦。
agonizesthai 是 agonize 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Agonizare carried the word into Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: agonizare 把该词带入拉丁语。

definition_zh: 居中调解；斡旋；促成和解；作为中介传导；（形容词）间接的
definition_en: to stand between two sides and help them reach an agreement, or to be the middle layer through which something is carried or passed on
core_image: 长桌中间空着的一把椅子：两边的人都够不到对方，只有这把椅子能同时听见两边
scene: 这里指「居中调解」。 The union and the company had stopped talking, so a retired judge was asked to mediate.
sceneCN: 这里 mediate 是「居中调解」（第 2 个义项：站在两方之间斡旋，促成对话）；句意：工会与公司已经停止对话，于是请来一位退休法官居中调解。场景要点：一张长桌、两方各自抱臂坐着、中间空着的一把椅子。

pos.zh: 调解；斡旋；居中促成（争端、协议）
间接的；居中的（多用于哲学与医学语境）

derivatives.zh: 女调解人（较少用，源自拉丁语阴性形式）

senses.title: Stand in the middle
senses.titleCN: 站在中间：占据中间位置
senses.definition: to be or occupy a position between two things, points or extremes
senses.definitionCN: 处在两物、两点或两个极端之间的位置
senses.example: A narrow strip of neutral ground mediated between the two front lines.
senses.exampleCN: 一条狭窄的中立地带横在两道前线之间。
senses.why: Mediate comes from Latin medius, 'middle'. The earliest uses describe sheer position: something simply sits between two others, with no suggestion of speaking or settling anything.
senses.whyCN: mediate 来自拉丁语 medius“中间”。最早的用法只描述位置：某物就横在两物之间，并不含说话或调停的意思。

senses.title: Act as go-between
senses.titleCN: 充当中间人：在两方之间斡旋
senses.definition: to intervene between two parties in order to bring them together or reconcile them
senses.definitionCN: 在两方之间介入，使他们重新接触或和解
senses.example: She mediated between the landlord and the tenants for three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她在房东与租客之间斡旋了三个小时。
senses.why: Recorded from the 1610s, this sense turns the middle position into an action: the person who occupies the gap begins to carry words across it.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项自 17 世纪 10 年代有记录，把“处在中间”变成动作：占据空隙的人开始把话从一边带到另一边。

senses.title: Settle a dispute
senses.titleCN: 调解解决：把争端谈停下来
senses.definition: to help two sides reach an agreement, or to settle a dispute by acting as the middle party
senses.definitionCN: 帮助两方达成一致，或作为中间方把争端解决掉
senses.example: The panel mediated a settlement that both sides accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 调解小组促成了一个双方都接受的解决方案。
senses.why: The 1560s sense 'settle by mediation, harmonize' was probably back-formed from mediation or mediator. The space in the middle is now measured by its result: an agreement exists.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 60 年代“通过调解解决、使和谐”的义项，很可能是从 mediation 或 mediator 逆构而来。中间那块空间现在用结果来衡量：协议出现了。

senses.title: Be the medium
senses.titleCN: 作为介质：把力量或信号带过去
senses.definition: to serve as the substance or channel through which a force, signal or quality is carried
senses.definitionCN: 作为某种力量、信号或性质得以传递的介质或通道
senses.example: Sound is mediated by air before it reaches the ear.
senses.exampleCN: 声音在到达耳朵之前要经过空气的传导。
senses.why: This sense grows from medium, the same 'middle' root: an intervening substance through which something is conveyed, a meaning recorded in the 1590s.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项从 medium 长出来，仍是同一个“中间”词根：某种介于其间的物质把东西输送过去，这一含义在 16 世纪 90 年代已有记录。

senses.title: Convey indirectly
senses.titleCN: 间接传达：话经中间层才到
senses.definition: to pass on information or feeling through an intermediate person or thing rather than face to face
senses.definitionCN: 不直接面对面，而是经由中间的人或物传递信息或情感
senses.example: Her letters mediated the news that no one in the family could say aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 家里没人说得出口的消息，由她的信间接传达了出来。
senses.why: Whatever must pass through a middle layer arrives altered. The word therefore also names the softening or shaping that happens on the way.
senses.whyCN: 凡是要穿过中间层的东西，到达时都会发生变化。因此这个词也指传递途中发生的缓冲与变形。

senses.title: Adjective: not immediate
senses.titleCN: 形容词：间接的、非直接的
senses.definition: reached through an intermediate step or cause rather than directly
senses.definitionCN: 经由中间步骤或中间原因达到，而非直接达到
senses.example: A mediate cause is one that acts through something else.
senses.exampleCN: 间接原因是指要通过别的因素才起作用的原因。
senses.why: The adjective was recorded in the early 15th century as 'intermediate', from Medieval Latin mediatus. It marks distance between a cause and its effect.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在 15 世纪初以“中间的”这一义项被记录，来自中世纪拉丁语 mediatus。它标记的是原因与结果之间的距离。

senses.title: Mediated knowledge
senses.titleCN: 间接认识：知识经符号与工具抵达
senses.definition: knowledge or experience that reaches the mind through symbols, instruments or other people rather than directly
senses.definitionCN: 经由符号、仪器或他人抵达头脑的知识或经验，而非亲身直接获得
senses.example: What we know of the deep ocean is mediated knowledge, gathered by robots and charts.
senses.exampleCN: 我们对深海的了解是间接知识，由机器人和海图收集而来。
senses.why: Once the middle layer is acknowledged, philosophy asks what it does to what passes through. The word becomes a name for the gap between world and mind.
senses.whyCN: 一旦承认中间层的存在，哲学就要问它对穿过的东西做了什么。这个词于是成了世界与头脑之间那道缝隙的名字。

senses.title: Formal mediation
senses.titleCN: 正式调解：法律、劳资与外交程序
senses.definition: in law, labour relations and diplomacy, to conduct a formal process in which a third party helps the sides reach terms
senses.definitionCN: 在法律、劳资关系与外交中，主持一个由第三方帮助各方达成条件的正式程序
senses.example: The government asked the United Nations to mediate the ceasefire talks.
senses.exampleCN: 政府请联合国来调解停火谈判。
senses.why: Institutions take the private act and give it rules, a room and a record. Mediate then names a procedure rather than a personality.
senses.whyCN: 机构把这种私人行为接管过来，给它规则、房间和记录。此时 mediate 命名的是一套程序，而不是某个人的性情。

senses.title: Religious mediator
senses.titleCN: 宗教上的中保：在神与人之间
senses.definition: in theology, to stand between God and humanity and bring the two together
senses.definitionCN: 在神学中，站在神与人之间，使两者得以相连
senses.example: In Christian doctrine, Christ mediates between God and man.
senses.exampleCN: 在基督教教义中，基督在神与人之间作中保。
senses.why: The noun mediator was first applied to Christ, and the verb inherited that vertical picture: the middle position is not between equals but between heaven and earth.
senses.whyCN: 名词 mediator 最早用于基督，动词继承了这幅垂直的画面：中间的位置不在平等的两方之间，而在天与地之间。

intro.en: Mediate comes from Latin medius 'middle' through the verb mediare. The same root gives medium and media, so the modern 'go-between' sense and the modern 'channel' sense are two branches of one physical picture. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mediate 经由拉丁语动词 mediare 来自 medius“中间”。同一个词根也给出 medium 与 media，因此现代“中间人”义与“渠道”义是同一幅物理画面的两个分支。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'divide in two equal parts', a sense now obsolete. It comes from Latin mediatus, past participle of mediare 'to halve', later 'to be in the middle'.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 16 世纪 40 年代，意为“分成相等的两半”，此义今已废弃。它来自拉丁语 mediatus，即 mediare 的过去分词；mediare 意为“对半分”，后义为“处在中间”。

items.en: The sense 'settle by mediation, harmonize, reconcile' appears, perhaps as a back-formation from mediation or mediator rather than as a direct development of the Latin verb.
items.cn: 出现“通过调解解决、使和谐、使和解”的义项，这也许是从 mediation 或 mediator 逆构而来，而不是拉丁语动词的直接发展。

items.en: The central modern sense is recorded: 'act as a mediator, intervene for the purpose of reconciliation'. The person in the middle now speaks.
items.cn: 核心的现代义项有记录：“充当调解人，为促成和解而介入”。处在中间的那个人现在开口说话了。

items.en: The positional sense 'occupy a middle place or position' is recorded, keeping the literal picture of something that lies between two others.
items.cn: 记录到表示位置的义项“占据中间的位置”，保留了某物横在另两物之间的字面画面。

items.en: The adjective is recorded as 'intermediate', from Medieval Latin mediatus, the past-participle adjective of mediare. Mediately and immediate belong to the same family.
items.cn: 形容词以“中间的”这一义项记录于 15 世纪初，来自中世纪拉丁语 mediatus，即 mediare 的过去分词形容词。mediately 与 immediate 属于同一词族。

items.en: The root *medhyo- 'middle' also lies behind medium, media, immediate, intermediate, medieval and Mediterranean. It has nothing to do with Latin medicus 'physician', the source of medical: the shared medi- shape is coincidence.
items.cn: 词根 *medhyo-“中间”也是 medium、media、immediate、intermediate、medieval、Mediterranean 的来源。它与 medical 的来源拉丁语 medicus“医生”毫无关系：共同的 medi- 外形只是巧合。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin 'middle' root but splits into a plural, a channel, a process and a person. The second group compares the words for stepping between people, which differ in how much authority the middle party has.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语“中间”词根，但分成复数、渠道、过程与人四个身份。第二组比较“介入他人之间”的几个词，区别在于中间方握有多少裁决权。

entries.definition: the plural of medium, now used collectively for newspapers, broadcasting and online platforms. It is a set of channels, not an act of reconciling.
entries.definitionCN: medium 的复数，现集合指报纸、广播与网络平台。它是一组渠道，不是调解行为。

entries.definition: a substance or agency through which something is conveyed, or a middle size or degree. The noun keeps the literal 'middle layer' that mediate uses figuratively.
entries.definitionCN: 借以传递某物的介质或机构，也可指中等的尺寸或程度。这个名词保留了 mediate 用作比喻时那个字面上的“中间层”。

entries.definition: the process of intervening to help two sides reach agreement. It is the noun of the act, recorded in the late 14th century, older in English than the modern verb sense.
entries.definitionCN: 介入并帮助两方达成一致的过程。它是这一行为的名词，14 世纪末已有记录，在英语里比动词的现代义项更老。

entries.definition: a person who mediates, especially one who helps disputing parties reconcile. It names the occupant of the middle chair.
entries.definitionCN: 进行调解的人，尤指帮助争执双方和解的人。它命名的是中间那把椅子上的人。

entries.definition: to act as an umpire and give a binding decision. An arbitrator can impose an outcome; a mediator can only help the sides agree.
entries.definitionCN: 充当裁判并作出有约束力的裁决。仲裁者可以强加结果；调解者只能帮助双方自行达成一致。

entries.definition: to come between parties or events, often without being asked. Intervention may be hostile or helpful; mediation is always aimed at agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 介入双方或事件之间，常非受邀而为。介入可能是敌意的，也可能是善意的；调解则总是以达成一致为目标。

entries.definition: to plead on behalf of someone, especially to someone in authority. The intercessor speaks for one party, while a mediator must keep both at the table.
entries.definitionCN: 为某人向有权者求情。说情者为一方说话，而调解人必须把两方都留在桌边。

entries.definition: to discuss in order to reach an agreement. In negotiation the two sides speak for themselves; mediation adds a third person between them.
entries.definitionCN: 为达成协议而商谈。谈判时双方自己开口；调解则在两者之间再加一个人。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin medius 'middle', the verb mediare, and the family medium, media, mediation, mediator, immediate.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 medius“中间”、动词 mediare，以及 medium、media、mediation、mediator、immediate 这一族。

normal.en: medi- means 'middle'. To mediate is to put yourself in the middle, where both sides can reach you.
normal.cn: medi- 表示“中间”。mediate 就是把自己放到中间，让两边都够得着你。

normal.en: In Latin, mediare first meant 'to halve', then 'to be in the middle'. The English verb began as 'divide in two', which is now obsolete.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mediare 最初意为“对半分”，后来才是“处在中间”。英语动词最初也表示“分成两半”，此义今已废弃。

normal.en: The 1610s sense is the one to remember: 'act as a mediator'. The person in the middle starts to carry words across the gap.
normal.cn: 要记住的是 17 世纪 10 年代那个义项：“充当调解人”。处在中间的人开始把话带过空隙。

normal.en: medium and media come from the same medius: the middle layer becomes a channel, and a set of channels becomes the media.
normal.cn: medium 与 media 来自同一个 medius：中间层变成渠道，一组渠道就成了媒体。

normal.en: immediate is im- 'not' plus medi- 'middle': no middle, no delay. That contrast is the clearest proof that medi- means 'middle'.
normal.cn: immediate 是 im-“不”加 medi-“中间”：没有中间，也就没有延迟。这个对比最能证明 medi- 就是“中间”。

abstract.en: Picture two rooms with a thick wall and no door. The mediator is not the wall and not either room; the mediator is the door.
abstract.cn: 想象两个房间之间有一堵厚墙，没有门。调解人不是墙，也不属于任何一个房间；调解人就是那扇门。

abstract.en: A mediator holds no weapon and no vote. The only power in the middle chair is that both sides are still willing to hear the sentence spoken from it.
abstract.cn: 调解人手里没有武器，也没有投票权。中间那把椅子唯一的权力，是两边仍愿意听从这里说出的话。

abstract.en: The same word covers the bridge and the signal that crosses it: a middle layer can be a person, a substance, or a screen.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指桥，也指过桥的信号：中间层可以是人、是物质，也可以是一块屏幕。

examples.en: A former colonial judge was brought in to mediate the border dispute.
examples.cn: 一位前殖民地法官被请来调解这场边界争端。

examples.en: The two departments could not speak directly, so the director mediated.
examples.cn: 两个部门无法直接对话，于是由总监居中斡旋。

examples.en: Nothing reaches us unmediated: even the sky we see passes through instruments and models.
examples.cn: 没有什么是无中介地抵达我们的：连我们看见的天空也要穿过仪器与模型。

dict_mnemonic.text: “米迪埃特”——米迪站在两边之间，左手拉住一个、右手拉住一个 → mediate 居中调解（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 medius“中间”，经动词 mediare“处在中间”而来，核心是“把自己放到两方之间的空位上”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of mediate, all built on one position: a body placed in the middle, which first merely occupies the gap, then speaks across it, then becomes the channel through which anything at all must pass.
sensesIntro.cn: mediate 的九个义项都建立在同一个位置上：一个被放在中间的身体。它先是占据空隙，继而隔着空隙说话，最后成为任何东西都必须穿过的通道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chair placed between two parties who cannot reach each other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把椅子被放在两个够不到对方的阵营之间。

branches.en: POSITION: the oldest picture is spatial — something simply lies between two others.
branches.cn: 位置：最古老的画面是空间的——某物就横在另两物之间。

branches.en: RECONCILIATION: the middle person starts to speak, and the talking ends in a settlement.
branches.cn: 和解：中间的人开始说话，而这场谈话最终落到一份和解上。

branches.en: CHANNEL: the middle layer carries sound, news or feeling, and therefore alters what it carries.
branches.cn: 通道：中间层运送声音、消息或情感，因此也改变了它所运送的东西。

branches.en: INDIRECTION: in grammar and philosophy the same gap becomes 'not immediate' and 'known through something else'.
branches.cn: 间接性：在语法与哲学里，同一道空隙变成“非直接的”与“经由他物而知的”。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: law and diplomacy turn the act into a procedure, and theology turns the middle chair into a mediator between heaven and earth.
branches.cn: 制度：法律与外交把这一行为变成程序，神学则把中间那把椅子变成天地之间的中保。

intro.en: Mediate is a Latin verb borrowed whole: the stem medi- 'middle' plus the verb ending -ate. English then adds -ion, -or and un- to build the rest of the family.
intro.cn: mediate 是整体借入的拉丁语动词：词干 medi-“中间”加动词词尾 -ate。英语再以 -ion、-or 与 un- 构成其余词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin medius 'middle' gives the stem; mediare 'to halve, to be in the middle' gives the verb; mediatio and mediator give the nouns. The root goes back to PIE *medhyo-, also behind medium and media.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 medius“中间”提供词干；mediare“对半分、处在中间”提供动词；mediatio 与 mediator 提供名词。这个词根可追溯到原始印欧语 *medhyo-，medium 与 media 也来自它。

items.meaning: to be in the middle; to bring two sides together
items.meaningCN: 处在中间；使两方走到一起（medi- 中间 + -ate 动词词尾）
items.example: A neutral country offered to mediate the talks.
items.exampleCN: 一个中立国提出为谈判作调解。

items.meaning: the act or process of mediating
items.meaningCN: 调解；斡旋（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: The contract was saved by two weeks of mediation.
items.exampleCN: 合同靠两周的调解得以保全。

items.meaningCN: 调解人；中间人（-or 表示施动者）
items.example: The mediator met each side separately before the joint session.
items.exampleCN: 调解人在联席会议前分别见了双方。

items.meaningCN: 女调解人（-trix 为拉丁语阴性施动后缀）
items.example: The order honours the Virgin as mediatrix.

items.meaning: carried or reached through an intermediary
items.meaningCN: 经中介传递的；间接获得的（-ed 构成分词形容词）
items.example: The mediated version of the story was kinder than the original.
items.exampleCN: 经中介转述的版本比原话温和。

items.meaningCN: 无中介的；直接的（un- 表否定）
items.example: She wanted unmediated contact with the readers.
items.exampleCN: 她想要与读者直接接触，不要中间环节。

items.meaning: with no middle step or delay
items.meaningCN: 立即的；直接的（im- 不 + medi- 中间，即“没有中间”）

items.meaning: lying or occurring between two stages
items.meaningCN: 中间的；中级的（inter- 在……之间 + medi- 中间）
items.example: She joined an intermediate class after the placement test.
items.exampleCN: 分级测试后她进了中级班。

items.meaning: a middle layer; a channel of communication
items.meaningCN: 介质；媒介；中间物（-um 为中性名词词尾）
items.example: Water is a good medium for sound.

items.meaningCN: 媒体；传播渠道（-a 为中性复数词尾）
items.example: The media covered the talks from outside the building.
items.exampleCN: 媒体在大楼外报道了会谈。

items.meaningCN: 中世纪的（medi- 中间 + aevum 时代）
items.example: The town wall is a medieval survival.
items.exampleCN: 这道城墙是中世纪留下的。

items.meaning: the sea in the middle of the lands
items.meaningCN: 地中海（medi- 中间 + terra 陆地，即“陆地中间的海”）
items.example: The Mediterranean lies between three continents.
items.exampleCN: 地中海位于三大洲之间。

latinEntries.meaning: to halve; to be in the middle
a division in the middle; mediation

latinEntries.meaningCN: 在双方之间介入的人；调解人

definition_zh: 遗传上；从基因角度；以遗传方式；经基因改造地
definition_en: in a way that relates to genes or heredity, or by means of genetic material or genetic modification
core_image: 两批外观相同的种子被放进检测仪，屏幕上显示出内部不同的条带
scene: 两批种子外表相同，实验室却能测出内部的差异。 The two strains are genetically distinct although they look alike.
sceneCN: 这里 genetically 指「从基因角度看、在遗传上」（第 2 个义项：就基因而言）；句意为这两个菌株虽然外表相似，在遗传上却不同。可辨识物件：两盘种子、检测仪、条带屏幕、标签。

pos.zh: 以遗传方式；经基因改造地

collocations.zh: 转基因的；经基因改造的

senses.title: By genetic modification
senses.definition: by changing genetic material, especially through engineering
senses.definitionCN: 通过改变遗传物质，尤指通过工程手段
senses.example: The crop was genetically modified to resist insects.
senses.exampleCN: 这种作物经过基因改造以抵抗昆虫。
senses.why: The adverb marks the means, so genetically modified means changed at the level of the instructions rather than by breeding alone.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词标记手段，因此「经基因改造」指在指令层面被改变，而非仅靠育种。

senses.title: In genetic terms
senses.definition: as judged by genes rather than by appearance
senses.definitionCN: 以基因而非外表来评判
senses.example: The two strains are genetically distinct although they look alike.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个菌株外表相似，在遗传上却不同。
senses.why: Here the adverb sets the viewpoint: what is compared is the sequence, not the visible form.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个副词设定视角：比较的是序列，而非可见形态。

senses.title: As determined by inheritance
senses.definition: in a way that is influenced or fixed by inherited factors
senses.definitionCN: 受遗传因素影响或固定的方式
senses.example: Height is genetically influenced but not fixed.
senses.exampleCN: 身高受遗传影响，但并非固定不变。
senses.why: The adverb can soften causation: genetically influenced leaves room for environment, while genetically determined closes it.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词可以缓和因果关系：受遗传影响仍给环境留余地，而由遗传决定则不留。

senses.title: At the level of genetic material
senses.definition: by examining or acting on DNA or other hereditary material
senses.definitionCN: 通过检查或作用于遗传物质
senses.example: The samples were compared genetically.
senses.exampleCN: 这些样本在遗传层面做了比较。
senses.why: The adverb can describe a method as well as a cause: comparing genetically means using sequences as the evidence.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词既能描述方法也能描述原因：在遗传层面比较，就是用序列作证据。

senses.title: Through genetic transmission
senses.definition: by passing from parents to offspring through genes
senses.definitionCN: 通过基因由亲代传给子代
senses.example: The disorder is genetically transmitted.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疾病经遗传传递。
senses.why: The adverb attaches transmission to genes, so the route is explicitly biological rather than social.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把传递附着到基因上，因此路径明确是生物的，而非社会的。

senses.title: With respect to genetic makeup
senses.definition: in terms of the overall genetic constitution of a group
senses.definitionCN: 就一个群体的整体遗传构成而言
senses.example: Genetically, the island population is unusually uniform.
senses.exampleCN: 就遗传而言，这个岛屿群体异常一致。
senses.why: At the start of a clause, the adverb frames the whole statement as a genetic judgement.
senses.whyCN: 置于句首时，这个副词把整句框定为遗传判断。

senses.title: By genetic engineering
senses.definition: by deliberate insertion, deletion or editing of sequences
senses.definitionCN: 通过有意插入、删除或编辑序列
senses.example: The vaccine seed strain was genetically engineered.
senses.exampleCN: 疫苗种株经过基因工程改造。
senses.why: Engineering is the most deliberate form of the means sense: the change is designed, not selected from existing variation.
senses.whyCN: 工程是手段义中最有意的一种：改变是被设计出来的，而非从既有变异中选出的。

senses.title: In genetic classification
senses.definition: as grouped by shared genetic material rather than by visible traits
senses.definitionCN: 按共享遗传物质而非可见性状来归类
senses.example: Genetically, the two species belong to one genus.
senses.exampleCN: 从遗传分类看，这两个物种属于同一属。
senses.why: The adverb can qualify taxonomy itself, marking a classification that follows sequences instead of shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词能限定分类学本身，标记一种依据序列而非外形的分类。

intro.en: Genetically is genetic plus the adverbial ending -ally, from -al + -ly. The adjective goes back through French to Greek genetikos 'generative'.
intro.cn: genetically 是 genetic 加副词词尾 -ally 构成，后者来自 -al + -ly。形容词经法语上溯到希腊 genetikos「生殖的」。

items.en: Genos 'race, kind' belongs to the PIE family reconstructed as *ǵenh₁-, so the root form is a reconstruction; Latin genus is a cognate, not the source.
items.cn: genos「种族、种类」属于被重构为 *ǵenh₁- 的原始印欧语词族，因此该词根形式是重构；拉丁 genus 是同源词，并非来源。

items.en: Genetikos 'generative' was formed from genesis 'origin' with the suffix -ikos.
items.cn: genetikos「生殖的」由 genesis「起源」加后缀 -ikos 构成。

items.en: Genetic entered English in 1831 for 'pertaining to origin', and from the early twentieth century, often dated 1908, for genes; genetical was the older adjective form.
items.cn: genetic 在 1831 年以「关于起源的」义进入英语，20 世纪初（常定在 1908 年）起用于基因；genetical 是较早的形容词形式。

items.en: The adverb was built as genetic + -al + -ly, giving genetically; the older genetical now survives mainly in technical writing.
items.cn: 副词由 genetic + -al + -ly 构成，写作 genetically；较旧的 genetical 如今主要残存于技术文献。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adverb spread to modification, screening and classification: genetically modified, genetically screened, genetically distinct.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个副词扩展到改造、筛查与分类：转基因、经基因筛查、遗传上不同。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first recorded use of the adverb is not firmly dated, and no Latin derivative of genetikos exists, so latinEntries is empty.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个副词的最早书证没有确切年代，且 genetikos 没有拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空。

note.en: Group one separates genetically from look-alikes with other roots; group two separates it from adverbs that name inheritance, genotype or environment.
note.cn: 第一组把 genetically 与词根不同的形近词分开；第二组把它与表示遗传、基因型或环境的副词区分。

entries.definition: From Latin genialis 'festive, natural', connected with genius, not genos: in a cheerful and friendly way.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 genialis「节庆的、天生的」，与 genius 相关，而非 genos：指和蔼愉快地。

entries.definition: From general, built on Latin genus 'kind' but meaning 'in most cases'; it is not a genetic judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 general，虽建立在拉丁 genus「种类」上，但意为「通常」；不是遗传判断。

entries.definition: The most common collocation, naming an organism whose material has been deliberately altered.
entries.definitionCN: 最常见的搭配，指遗传物质被有意改造过的生物。

entries.definition: Sharing the same genetic material, as clones do; the adverb marks the level of identity.
entries.definitionCN: 共享相同遗传物质，如克隆体；副词标记同一性的层面。

entries.definition: It stresses transmission from ancestors, while genetically can also mean 'at the level of genes' without descent.
entries.definitionCN: 强调从祖先传递，而 genetically 也可仅指「在基因层面」，不涉及世系。

entries.definition: Relating to the inherited constitution at one or more loci, a narrower technical term.
entries.definitionCN: 与一个或多个位点的遗传组成相关，是更窄的技术词。

entries.definition: Relating to visible or measurable traits, the opposite angle from genetically.
entries.definitionCN: 与可见或可测性状相关，角度与 genetically 相反。

entries.definition: Relating to external conditions rather than genes; the usual contrast in nature-nurture debates.
entries.definitionCN: 与外部条件相关而非基因；是天性与教养争论中的常见对照。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: genetic + -al + -ly: in the manner of genes.
normal.cn: genetic + -al + -ly：以基因的方式。

normal.en: The family runs gene, genetic, genetically, genetics and geneticist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 gene、genetic、genetically、genetics 与 geneticist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: genetically modified, genetically distinct, genetically determined.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：转基因的、遗传上不同的、由遗传决定的。

normal.en: As a sentence opener, genetically frames the whole claim.
normal.cn: 作为句首状语，genetically 为整句断言设定框架。

normal.en: Genetically is not environmentally: the two adverbs split nature from nurture.
normal.cn: genetically 与 environmentally 相对：两个副词把天性从教养中分开。

abstract.en: Picture two jars with identical labels but different contents.
abstract.cn: 想象两个标签相同、内容不同的罐子。

abstract.en: Picture a barcode read while the package looks blank.
abstract.cn: 想象包装看似空白，条形码却已被读出。

abstract.en: Picture a family resemblance measured with a ruler instead of an eye.
abstract.cn: 想象用尺子而不是眼睛来测量家族相似。

examples.en: The tomatoes were genetically modified to ripen on schedule.
examples.cn: 这些番茄经过基因改造，可按计划成熟。

examples.en: Genetically, the two populations have been separate for centuries.
examples.cn: 从遗传上看，这两个群体已分离数百年。

examples.en: The rescued cubs are genetically diverse enough to breed.
examples.cn: 获救的幼兽遗传多样性足够，可以繁育。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one viewpoint: by modification, in genetic terms, by inheritance, at the material level, through transmission, as makeup, by engineering and in classification.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个视角展开：经改造、从基因角度、由遗传决定、在物质层面、经传递、就组成而言、经工程、在分类上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two trays of identical seeds, while a screen shows different internal bands.
core.cn: 核心意象：两盘外观相同的种子，屏幕却显示出不同的内部条带。

branches.en: BY MODIFICATION: the change is made deliberately at the level of the instructions.
branches.cn: 经改造：改变是在指令层面有意作出的。

branches.en: VIEWPOINT: the judgement is made by sequences rather than by appearance or shape.
branches.cn: 视角：判断依据序列而非外表或形态。

branches.en: CAUSE AND ROUTE: inherited influence, and transmission from parents to offspring.
branches.cn: 原因与路径：遗传影响，以及由亲代到子代的传递。

branches.en: MATERIAL LEVEL: the comparison or action occurs on the hereditary material itself.
branches.cn: 物质层面：比较或作用发生在遗传物质本身。

branches.en: MAKEUP: the adverb frames a statement about a group's overall constitution.
branches.cn: 组成：副词为关于群体整体构成的陈述设定框架。

intro.en: Genetically is a layered adverb: a Greek-derived stem, an adjective suffix, and a further adverbial ending.
intro.cn: genetically 是分层构成的副词：希腊来源词干、形容词后缀，再加副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek genos gives gene and genetic; -ic and -al form the adjective, and -ly forms the adverb. No Latin derivative of genetikos exists, so latinEntries is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 genos 衍生 gene 与 genetic；-ic 与 -al 构成形容词，-ly 构成副词。genetikos 没有拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空。

definition_zh: 遗传学；（某生物或群体的）遗传组成
definition_en: the branch of biology that studies heredity and genes, or the genetic makeup of an organism or group
core_image: 一块白板写满杂交组合与比例，旁边摆着一排标了代号的育苗盘
scene: 实验室的白板上写满杂交组合，研究生在计算下一代的性状比例。 Modern genetics explains how traits pass from parents to offspring.
sceneCN: 这里 genetics 指「研究遗传与基因的生物学科」（第 1 个义项：遗传学）；句意为现代遗传学解释了性状如何由亲代传给子代。可辨识物件：白板、粉笔、杂交组合表、育苗盘、计算器。

pos.zh: 遗传组成；遗传特征（作复数）

senses.title: The science of heredity
senses.definition: the branch of biology concerned with genes, heredity and variation
senses.definitionCN: 研究基因、遗传与变异的生物学分支
senses.example: Modern genetics explains how traits pass from parents to offspring.
senses.exampleCN: 现代遗传学解释了性状如何由亲代传给子代。
senses.why: The name was coined for a discipline, so genetics takes a singular verb even though it ends in -s.
senses.whyCN: 这个名称是为学科而造的，因此尽管以 -s 结尾，genetics 仍接单数动词。

senses.title: The genetic makeup of an organism
senses.definition: the total genetic constitution of an organism or group
senses.definitionCN: 一个生物或群体的全部遗传构成
senses.example: The genetics of this population differ from those of the mainland.
senses.exampleCN: 这个群体的遗传组成与大陆群体不同。
senses.why: Because the field studies variation, its name was transferred to the variation itself, especially in population studies.
senses.whyCN: 由于该领域研究变异，其名称被转用到变异本身，尤其在群体研究中。

senses.title: A branch or subfield
senses.definition: a specialized division of the science, such as medical or molecular genetics
senses.definitionCN: 该学科的一个专门分支，如医学遗传学或分子遗传学
senses.example: Medical genetics now guides many cancer treatments.
senses.exampleCN: 医学遗传学如今指导许多癌症治疗。
senses.why: Compound names such as medical genetics treat the word as a countable field, so one can speak of several genetics.
senses.whyCN: 医学遗传学这类复合名称把该词当作可数的领域，因此可以说有多个遗传学分支。

senses.title: Molecular genetics
senses.definition: the study of how genetic material is copied, expressed and repaired at the molecular level
senses.definitionCN: 在分子层面研究遗传物质如何复制、表达与修复
senses.example: Molecular genetics studies how sequences are copied and repaired.
senses.exampleCN: 分子遗传学研究序列如何被复制与修复。
senses.why: When the focus moves to molecules, the word pairs with an adjective that names the level rather than the organism.
senses.whyCN: 当焦点转向分子，这个词便与标明层次的形容词搭配，而非与生物体搭配。

senses.title: Population genetics
senses.definition: the study of allele frequencies and their changes in populations
senses.definitionCN: 研究群体中等位基因频率及其变化
senses.example: Population genetics tracks allele frequencies over time.
senses.exampleCN: 群体遗传学追踪等位基因频率随时间的变化。
senses.why: Once genes are counted across groups, genetics becomes a science of frequencies rather than of single families.
senses.whyCN: 一旦跨群体计数基因，遗传学就成为频率的科学，而非单个家族的科学。

senses.title: Genetics as a subject taught
senses.definition: the subject as taught or examined in a course
senses.definitionCN: 作为课程或考试科目的遗传学
senses.example: She teaches genetics to first-year biology students.
senses.exampleCN: 她给一年级生物学生教遗传学。
senses.why: The discipline name also names a course, which is why it appears with teach, study and examine.
senses.whyCN: 学科名同时也指一门课程，因此常与「教」「学」「考」搭配。

senses.title: Clinical genetics
senses.definition: the application of genetics to diagnosis and counselling in medicine
senses.definitionCN: 遗传学在医学诊断与咨询中的应用
senses.example: Clinical genetics offers testing for inherited conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 临床遗传学为遗传性疾病提供检测。
senses.why: The clinical compound marks the point where the science meets patients, testing and advice.
senses.whyCN: 临床复合词标记出这门科学与患者、检测与建议相接的地方。

senses.title: Genetics in agriculture
senses.definition: the use of genetic knowledge to improve crops and livestock
senses.definitionCN: 利用遗传知识改良作物与家畜
senses.example: Modern genetics produced wheat that tolerates drought.
senses.exampleCN: 现代遗传学培育出了耐旱小麦。
senses.why: Breeding was practiced long before the science existed, but genetics now explains and directs what breeders do.
senses.whyCN: 育种远在这门科学出现之前就已实践，但遗传学如今解释并指导育种者的工作。

intro.en: Genetics was coined from Greek genetikos 'generative', a derivative of genesis 'origin' and genos 'race, kind'. The English noun is usually credited to William Bateson, who proposed it in 1905 and published it in 1906; other reference works record an isolated use in 1872 and a related sense in 1891, so the first date is disputed.
intro.cn: genetics 由希腊 genetikos「生殖的、产生的」造出，后者源出 genesis「起源」与 genos「种族、种类」。英语名词通常归功于威廉·贝特森，他于 1905 年提出、1906 年发表；另有参考书记录 1872 年的一处孤立用法与 1891 年的相关义，因此首见年代存在争议。

items.en: Genos meant 'race, kind, birth'. It belongs to the PIE family reconstructed as *ǵenh₁-, so that root form is a reconstruction; Latin genus is a cognate, not the source of the English word.
items.cn: genos 意为「种族、种类、出生」。它属于被重构为 *ǵenh₁- 的原始印欧语词族，因此该词根形式是重构；拉丁 genus 是同源词，并非这个英语词的来源。

items.en: Genesis 'origin, generation' supplied the noun of coming into being that stands behind genetikos.
items.cn: genesis「起源、生成」提供了「进入存在」的名词，位于 genetikos 之后。

items.en: Genetikos 'generative, concerned with generation' was formed with the adjectival suffix -ikos.
items.cn: genetikos「生殖的、与生成有关的」由形容词后缀 -ikos 构成。

items.en: William Bateson proposed genetics in a letter of 1905 and used it in print in 1906; some reference works record an isolated 1872 use and a 'study of heredity' sense in 1891, so the exact first appearance is disputed rather than the root.
items.cn: 威廉·贝特森在 1905 年的一封信中提出 genetics，并于 1906 年用于印刷文本；有些参考书记录 1872 年的一处孤立用法与 1891 年的「遗传研究」义，因此存疑的是确切首见年代，而非词根。

items.en: During the twentieth century the field split into molecular, population and clinical branches, and the plural-looking name stayed grammatically singular.
items.cn: 20 世纪，该领域分化为分子、群体与临床分支，这个看似复数的名称在语法上仍保持单数。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the root in genetikos is not in doubt, but the first English appearance is disputed between an isolated 1872 use, an 1891 sense and Bateson's 1905-1906 coinage; no Latin derivative of genetikos exists, so latinEntries is empty, and the Latin cognate genus belongs to the same PIE family but is not the source.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：genetikos 的词根并无疑问，但英语首见年代在 1872 年孤立用法、1891 年义项与贝特森 1905—1906 年造词之间存在争议；genetikos 没有拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空；拉丁同源词 genus 属于同一原始印欧语词族，但并非来源。

note.en: Group one separates genetics from words built on the same Greek stem and from one accidental sound-alike; group two separates it from the neighbouring sciences and from the older word for transmission.
note.cn: 第一组把 genetics 与同一希腊词干构成的词及一个偶然音近词分开；第二组把它与邻近学科及更早的「传递」用词区分。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'relating to genes'; genetics is the discipline or the makeup it studies.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与基因有关的」的形容词；genetics 是学科或被研究的组成。

entries.definition: The study of whole genomes rather than single genes; it grew out of genetics but is not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 研究整个基因组而非单个基因的学科；由遗传学发展而来，但并非同义词。

entries.definition: The unit of heredity that genetics studies; the science and its object are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 遗传学所研究的遗传单位；学科与其对象不能互换。

entries.definition: From Greek gymnazein 'to train naked', not from genos: physical exercises. The resemblance is only in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 gymnazein「裸身训练」，并非 genos：指体操。相似仅在读音。

entries.definition: The transmission of traits; genetics is the science that explains it, not the transmission itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指性状传递；genetics 是解释它的科学，而非传递本身。

entries.definition: A broader word for property and biological transmission; genetics names the discipline, not an estate.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖财产与生物传递的较宽泛词；genetics 命名学科，而非产业。

entries.definition: The study of complete genomes; genetics often focuses on individual genes and their effects.
entries.definitionCN: 研究完整基因组的学科；genetics 常聚焦单个基因及其效应。

entries.definition: The wider study of biological molecules; genetics is one part of it, focused on heredity.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物大分子的更广领域；遗传学是其中专注遗传的一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek genos 'race, kind' + -etics: the study of how kind passes down.
normal.cn: 希腊 genos「种族、种类」+ 学科后缀：研究种类如何下传的学问。

normal.en: The family runs gene, genetic, genetically, genetics, geneticist and genomics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 gene、genetic、genetically、genetics、geneticist 与 genomics。

normal.en: The name ends in -s but takes a singular verb when it means the science.
normal.cn: 这个词以 -s 结尾，但指学科时接单数动词。

normal.en: Bateson proposed the term in 1905 and printed it in 1906.
normal.cn: 贝特森于 1905 年提出该术语，1906 年正式印行。

normal.en: Medical, molecular and population are its common branches.
normal.cn: 医学、分子与群体是其常见分支。

abstract.en: Picture a library that catalogues not books but the instructions for making them.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆不编目书籍，而编目造书的指令。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree redrawn as a table of frequencies.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵家谱树被重画成一张频率表。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe book whose pages are copied with occasional mistakes.
abstract.cn: 想象一本食谱，页面被复制时偶尔出错。

examples.en: Genetics has become central to conservation planning.
examples.cn: 遗传学已成为保护规划的核心。

examples.en: The genetics of the island population show a long isolation.
examples.cn: 这个岛屿群体的遗传组成显示出长期隔离。

examples.en: She switched from field biology to genetics after her first course.
examples.cn: 她在上完第一门课后从野外生物学转向遗传学。

dict_mnemonic.text: gene（基因）+ tics（学科）——研究基因的学科 → 遗传学；指学科时作单数。

root: 希腊 genetikos「生殖的」← genesis「起源」+ genos「种族、种类」；genos 出自原始印欧语 *ǵenh₁-（重构形式）；拉丁 genus 为同源词，非来源；英语词通常归功于贝特森 1905—1906 年，另有 1872/1891 年早期用法之说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one discipline as it spreads: the science, the makeup it describes, its branches, its molecular and population scales, its teaching, its clinical use and its agricultural use.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一门学科的外扩展开：学科本身、它所描述的组成、它的分支、分子与群体尺度、它的教学、临床用途与农业用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whiteboard of crosses and ratios beside trays of labelled seedlings.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块写满杂交与比例的白板，旁边是一排标了代号的育苗盘。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE: the science itself, including the course that teaches it.
branches.cn: 学科：科学本身，包括讲授它的课程。

branches.en: THE MAKEUP: the name transferred from the field to what the field measures.
branches.cn: 组成：名称从领域转用到领域所测量的对象。

branches.en: BRANCHES AND SCALES: medical, molecular and population divisions.
branches.cn: 分支与尺度：医学、分子与群体划分。

branches.en: CLINICAL USE: testing and counselling where the science meets patients.
branches.cn: 临床用途：科学与患者相接处的检测与咨询。

branches.en: AGRICULTURAL USE: breeding guided by genetic knowledge.
branches.cn: 农业用途：由遗传知识指导的育种。

intro.en: Genetics is a Greek-derived compound whose stem also builds the modern vocabulary of heredity; the suffixes mark an adjective, a science and a person.
intro.cn: genetics 是希腊语来源的复合词，其词干还构成现代遗传词汇；后缀分别标记形容词、学科与从业者。

latinIntro.en: Greek genos 'race, kind' gives gene, genetic, genetics and genomics; -ikos gives the adjective and -ics names the field. No Latin derivative of genetikos exists, so latinEntries is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 genos「种族、种类」衍生 gene、genetic、genetics 与 genomics；-ikos 构成形容词，-ics 命名学科。genetikos 没有拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.exampleCN: genesis 命名事物进入存在的过程。

items.example: The adjective described what produces or transmits.

definition_zh: 意识形态；观念体系；思想体系；（贬义）空想的教条
definition_en: a systematic set of ideas and beliefs through which a group interprets the world and justifies its actions
core_image: 把散落的想法收进一张图，排成能解释整个世界的骨架
scene: 桌上摊着一份宣言，第一页写着几条原则，后面所有条款都向它对齐。 The party's manifesto opened with a page of principles, and every later policy had to fit that ideology.
sceneCN: 这里 ideology 是「政治意识形态」（第 1 个义项：解释并规范社会的一套系统观念）；句意：该党的宣言以一页原则开篇，后来的每项政策都必须符合这套意识形态。

senses.title: Political ideology: a map for society
senses.titleCN: 政治意识形态：解释社会的一张图
senses.definition: a connected set of political ideas that explains how a society should be ordered and what its institutions should aim at
senses.definitionCN: 一套彼此关联的政治观念，解释社会应如何安排、制度应追求什么
senses.example: The two parties differ less in policy than in ideology.
senses.exampleCN: 两党的差别不在具体政策，而在意识形态。
senses.why: Ideology began as a 'science of ideas' and later came to mean the system through which a group reads the world. A political ideology is that system applied to the ordering of society.
senses.whyCN: ideology 起初意为“观念的科学”，后来指一个群体借以解读世界的体系。政治意识形态就是把这套体系用于社会安排。

senses.title: Belief system of a group
senses.definition: the shared body of assumptions and values by which any group, not only a party, makes sense of its world
senses.definitionCN: 任何群体（不只是政党）借以理解自身处境的共同预设与价值
senses.example: The profession's ideology treats long hours as proof of commitment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个行业的观念体系把长时间工作当作敬业的证明。
senses.why: Once ideology is a system of ideas rather than a party programme, every group that shares assumptions has one, including professions, clubs, and families.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 ideology 指观念体系而非政党纲领，任何共享预设的群体都有了一套，包括行业、社团与家庭。

senses.title: Derogatory: a doctrine out of touch
senses.definition: in a hostile use, a rigid set of ideas held regardless of evidence, or theory with no practical use
senses.definitionCN: 在敌意用法中，指不顾证据的僵硬观念，或没有实际用途的空论
senses.example: Critics dismissed the reform as ideology dressed up as science.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把这项改革斥为披着科学外衣的教条。
senses.why: The word's scientific origin promised proof; when a system of ideas refuses proof, the same word becomes an accusation of blindness.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的科学出身曾承诺证明；当一套观念拒绝证明时，同一个词就变成了“盲目”的指控。

senses.title: Original sense: the science of ideas
senses.definition: the original sense coined in 1796, a philosophy of the mind that derives knowledge from the senses
senses.definitionCN: 1796 年造出的本义，指从感官经验推导知识的意识哲学
senses.example: The French philosopher called his project a science of ideas, set against metaphysics.
senses.exampleCN: 那位法国哲学家把自己的工作称为“观念的科学”，与形而上学相对。
senses.why: Destutt de Tracy joined Greek idea 'form, look' to -logy 'study of' to name a new discipline. The literal meaning is a study of ideas, not a set of beliefs.
senses.whyCN: 德斯蒂·德·特拉西把希腊语 idea“形相、外观”与 -logy“学科”组合，命名一门新学问。字面义是“对观念的研究”，而不是一套信念。

senses.title: Hidden framework behind neutral practice
senses.definition: the unstated assumptions built into a practice, technology, or institution that looks neutral
senses.definitionCN: 被嵌进某种看似中立的做法、技术或制度中的未言明预设
senses.example: The claim that data speak for themselves is itself an ideology.
senses.exampleCN: “数据自己会说话”这一说法本身就是一种意识形态。
senses.why: A map is most powerful when it looks like the territory. The same system of ideas becomes ideology when its assumptions stop being noticed.
senses.whyCN: 一张地图最有力的时候，是它看起来像地面本身。当一套观念的预设不再被人注意到，它就成了意识形态。

senses.title: Corporate ideology: values as a script
senses.titleCN: 企业意识形态：价值变成话术
senses.definition: the set of values and slogans through which a company explains itself and asks its staff to behave
senses.definitionCN: 一个公司借以解释自身并要求员工照此行事的一套价值与口号
senses.example: The company's ideology praises speed and quietly punishes caution.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的观念体系赞美速度，却在暗中惩罚谨慎。
senses.why: When a set of beliefs is used to organise a workplace, the political map becomes an internal one: it marks what counts as a good employee.
senses.whyCN: 当一套信念被用来组织工作场所，政治地图就变成了内部地图：它标出什么样的人才算好员工。

senses.title: Religious or moral system
senses.definition: a religious or moral framework that explains suffering, duty, and the proper order of life
senses.definitionCN: 解释苦难、义务与生活应有秩序的一套宗教或道德框架
senses.example: The movement combined a strict moral ideology with practical charity.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动把严格的道德观念体系与实际慈善结合在一起。
senses.why: The same architecture of ideas can hold gods instead of parties. Whenever a group explains why the world is as it is, it is drawing this kind of map.
senses.whyCN: 同一套观念架构也可以装神明而非政党。只要一个群体解释世界为何如此，它就在画这类地图。

senses.title: The -ism label: a political programme
senses.titleCN: 以“主义”命名的政治纲领
senses.definition: a named political programme such as socialism, liberalism, or fascism, treated as a single package
senses.definitionCN: 以社会主义、自由主义、法西斯主义等命名的成套政治纲领
senses.example: By 1918 the word was used of socialism and communism themselves.
senses.exampleCN: 到 1918 年，这个词已被直接用来指社会主义与共产主义。
senses.why: English usage from 1907 first tied the term to socialist and communist writing; from 1918 the ideas and the movements merged into one label.
senses.whyCN: 英语用法从 1907 年起先把这个词与社会主义、共产主义写作绑在一起；从 1918 年起，观念与运动合并成了同一个标签。

senses.title: Dogmatic purity: ideas that cannot bend
senses.titleCN: 教条化的纯粹：不肯弯曲的观念
senses.definition: the state in which a set of ideas is defended so strictly that evidence and compromise are treated as betrayal
senses.definitionCN: 一套观念被捍卫得极其严格，以致证据与妥协都被视为背叛的状态
senses.example: The purge was justified in the name of ideological purity.
senses.exampleCN: 那场清洗以意识形态纯洁性的名义被正当化。
senses.why: A map that refuses correction stops being a guide and becomes a test of loyalty. Here ideology turns from a system of ideas into a border.
senses.whyCN: 一张拒绝修正的地图不再是指南，而变成了忠诚的检验。此时意识形态从观念体系变成了一条边界。

intro.en: Ideology is a modern coinage from two Greek pieces, idea 'form, look' and -logy 'study of'. It began as a name for a science and ended as a name for the beliefs people cannot examine. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ideology 是用两个希腊成分造的现代新词：idea“形相、外观”与 -logy“学科”。它起初是一门科学的名称，最后成了人们无法审视的信念的名称。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Coined as French idéologie, 'science of ideas', by Destutt de Tracy, for a philosophy of the mind that derives knowledge from the senses, as opposed to metaphysics.
items.cn: 由德斯蒂·德·特拉西造出法语 idéologie，意为“观念的科学”，指一种从感官经验推导知识的意识哲学，与形而上学相对。

items.en: The coinage joins idéo- 'of ideas', from Greek idea 'form, the look of a thing', with -logie, from Greek -logia 'a speaking, discourse, science', from legein 'to speak'.
items.cn: 这个新词把 idéo-“观念的”、来自希腊语 idea“形相、事物的外观”，与 -logie 结合，后者来自希腊语 -logia“言说、论述、学科”，再上溯 legein“说”。

items.en: Greek idea comes from idein 'to see', from PIE *weid- 'to see'. An idea was first a visible form, then a form held in the mind.
items.cn: 希腊语 idea 来自 idein“看见”，再上溯原始印欧语 *weid-“看见”。观念最初是可见的形相，后来成为心中的形相。

items.en: Destutt published his Eléments d'idéologie in these years, fixing the word in its learned, neutral sense.
items.cn: 德斯蒂在这一时期出版《观念学原理》，把这个词固定在学术性的中立义上。

items.en: The sense 'systematic set of ideas, doctrines through which the world is interpreted' appears in English by 1907, earliest in socialist and communist writing; from 1918 it names socialism and communism themselves, and later fascism.
items.cn: “借以解释世界的系统观念与学说”这一义项在 1907 年前后进入英语，最早见于社会主义与共产主义写作；从 1918 年起，它直接指社会主义与共产主义本身，后来又指法西斯主义。

items.en: The term became omnipresent only after Marx's The German Ideology and Mannheim's Ideology and Utopia appeared between the world wars. Ideological is recorded from 1797, and ideologue names the person who lives inside the map.
items.cn: 这个词要到马克思《德意志意识形态》与曼海姆《意识形态与乌托邦》在两次世界大战之间问世之后才无处不在。ideological 从 1797 年起有记录，ideologue 则指住在这张地图里的人。

note.en: The first group separates idea, ideal, the adjective, and the person from ideology; the second group compares other names for sets of beliefs.
note.cn: 第一组把 idea、ideal、形容词与“人”同 ideology 分开；第二组比较其他表示“信念集合”的说法。

entries.definition: a thought, concept, or plan in the mind. It is one unit; ideology is the system that arranges many such units into a world picture.
entries.definitionCN: 心中的一个想法、概念或计划。它是一个单位；ideology 则是把许多这样的单位排成世界图景的体系。

entries.definition: a standard of perfection, or the best possible form of something. An ideal is what a belief aims at; an ideology is the whole frame that contains both the aim and its justification.
entries.definitionCN: 完美的标准，或某物可能达到的最佳形态。ideal 是信念所指向的目标；ideology 是同时容纳目标与理由的整个框架。

entries.definition: relating to an ideology. It describes how something is driven by a set of ideas, as in an ideological dispute, rather than naming the set itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与意识形态有关的。它描述某事如何由一套观念驱动，如意识形态争论，而不是命名这套观念本身。

entries.definition: a person who holds a doctrine rigidly and defends it. It is usually hostile: the ideologue is the one who will not look outside the map.
entries.definitionCN: 僵硬坚持并捍卫一套学说的人。它通常带敌意：意识形态者就是不肯往地图外面看的那个人。

entries.definition: a set of principles taught or officially held, often by a church or a state. Doctrine stresses authority and instruction; ideology stresses the whole way of seeing the world.
entries.definitionCN: 被教授或官方持有的一套原则，常属教会或国家。doctrine 强调权威与教导；ideology 强调整套看世界的方式。

entries.definition: the connected beliefs a person or group holds. It is the plain, neutral phrase; ideology is the academic and often political word for the same architecture.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或群体所持的相互关联的信念。它是朴素中性的说法；ideology 是同一架构的学术用词，且常带政治色彩。

entries.definition: the overall way a person or culture sees existence. A worldview may be private and philosophical; an ideology is more organised, shared, and acted upon.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或文化看待存在的整体方式。worldview 可以是私人的、哲学的；ideology 则更有组织、更共享、更被付诸行动。

entries.definition: a principle laid down as unquestionably true. Dogma is one brick; ideology is the building, and calling it dogma is already the hostile sense.
entries.definitionCN: 被规定为不容置疑的原则。dogma 是一块砖；ideology 是整座建筑，而把它称为 dogma 时，已经用上了贬义。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Greek idea 'form, look' plus -logy 'study of', and the family ideological / ideologue / ideologist.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：希腊语 idea“形相、外观”加 -logy“学科”，以及 ideological／ideologue／ideologist 词族。

normal.en: idea means 'form or look' and -logy means 'study of'. Ideology was literally the study of ideas before it became the ideas themselves.
normal.cn: idea 表示“形相或外观”，-logy 表示“对……的研究”。ideology 字面上是“对观念的研究”，后来才变成观念本身。

normal.en: The -logy ending also builds biology, psychology and theology, so ideology belongs to the same family of 'named fields of study'.
normal.cn: -logy 也构成 biology、psychology、theology，所以 ideology 属于同一类“被命名的学问领域”。

normal.en: Ideological is the adjective, ideologue is the person, and ideologist is the person who studies the system.
normal.cn: ideological 是形容词，ideologue 是信奉者，ideologist 是研究这套体系的人。

normal.en: Do not confuse ideal with idea: an ideal is the perfect standard, an idea is one thought, and an ideology is the frame that holds many thoughts together.
normal.cn: 不要把 ideal 与 idea 混同：ideal 是完美标准，idea 是一个想法，ideology 是把许多想法收在一起的那个框架。

normal.en: The word was coined in 1796 as a neutral science, and only after 1907 did it become the name of political belief systems.
normal.cn: 这个词 1796 年被造出时是一门中立科学，直到 1907 年之后才成为政治信念体系的名称。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of loose notes. Ideology is the moment someone draws a frame around them and says: these belong together and explain everything.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠散乱的笔记。ideology 就是有人给它们画上一个框，并说：这些属于同一体，能解释一切的那一刻。

abstract.en: The frame can hold a party, a profession, a company, or a church. Whatever it holds, its power comes from being mistaken for the world itself.
abstract.cn: 这个框可以装一个政党、一个行业、一家公司或一座教堂。不论装什么，它的力量都来自被误当成世界本身。

abstract.en: A frame that can be revised stays a map. A frame that cannot be revised becomes a border, and crossing it is treated as betrayal.
abstract.cn: 可以修改的框仍是地图；不能修改的框变成边界，越过它就被当成背叛。

examples.en: The textbook presents its own assumptions as neutral method, which is how ideology usually hides.
examples.cn: 这本教科书把自己的预设呈现为中立的方法，意识形态通常就是这样藏起来的。

examples.en: She studied how colonial ideology shaped the maps children were given.
examples.cn: 她研究殖民意识形态如何塑造发给孩子们的地图。

examples.en: Calling every conviction an ideology makes it impossible to argue with any of them.
examples.cn: 把一切信念都称为意识形态，会让人无法与其中任何一种辩论。

dict_mnemonic.text: “爱迪欧乐吉”——爱迪欧（ideo）把一堆想法收进一个乐（logy）高音喇叭，对着全世界广播 → ideology 意识形态、观念体系

root: 源自希腊语 idea“形相、外观”+ -logia“言说、学科”，1796 年由法语 idéologie 造出，核心是“把零散观念收成一套能解释世界的体系”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of ideology, all grown from one structure: scattered ideas are gathered into a frame, and that frame is then used to read the world, justify action, or shut out doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: ideology 的九个义项都从同一个结构长出来：零散的想法被收进一个框架，这个框架随后被用来解读世界、为行动辩护，或把怀疑关在门外。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a frame drawn around many ideas so that they explain a whole world.
core.cn: 核心意象：给许多想法画上一个框，使它们能解释整个世界。

chain: A WAY TO READ THE WORLD

branches.en: POLITICS: the frame becomes a party programme, and the programme acquires an -ism label.
branches.cn: 政治：框架变成政党纲领，纲领再获得一个“主义”标签。

branches.en: GROUP LIFE: professions, companies, and religions each read their world through their own frame.
branches.cn: 群体生活：行业、公司与宗教各自用自己的一套框架解读世界。

branches.en: RIGIDITY: when the frame refuses evidence and compromise, it turns from doctrine into an accusation and then into a border.
branches.cn: 僵硬：当框架拒绝证据与妥协，它就从学说变成指控，再变成边界。

branches.en: ORIGIN: the coined sense was a neutral study of ideas, not a set of beliefs.
branches.cn: 起源：造词时的义项是对观念的中立研究，而不是一套信念。

branches.en: HIDDEN FRAME: the system works best when its assumptions pass unnoticed, like a map mistaken for ground.
branches.cn: 隐藏的框架：当预设不被人注意时，这套体系最有效，就像地图被当成地面。

intro.en: Ideology is a modern compound of two Greek elements: idea 'form, look' and -logy 'study or discourse'. English adds -ical, -ly, -logue, and -ist to build the rest of the family.
intro.cn: ideology 是由两个希腊成分构成的现代复合词：idea“形相、外观”与 -logy“研究或论述”。英语再加上 -ical、-ly、-logue、-ist 构成整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin idea was borrowed from Greek idea 'form, look', and Medieval Latin -logia came from Greek -logia, from logos 'word, speech'. The elements are Greek, but they reached modern European languages through Latin and French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 idea 借自希腊语 idea“形相、外观”，中世纪拉丁语 -logia 来自希腊语 -logia，再上溯 logos“词、言说”。成分是希腊的，但它们是经拉丁语与法语进入现代欧洲语言的。
