items.meaning: a system of ideas through which the world is interpreted
items.meaningCN: 解释世界的观念体系（ideo- 观念的 + -logy 学科）
items.example: The film examines the ideology behind urban planning.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片审视城市规划背后的意识形态。

items.meaning: more than one system of ideas
items.meaningCN: 多套观念体系（辅音加 y 结尾变 y 为 i 加 -es）
items.example: Competing ideologies shaped the new constitution.
items.exampleCN: 彼此竞争的各种意识形态塑造了新宪法。

items.meaning: driven by or belonging to an ideology
items.meaningCN: 意识形态的；由观念体系驱动的（-ical 构成形容词）
items.example: The split was personal before it became ideological.
items.exampleCN: 这场分裂先是人际的，后来才变成意识形态的。

items.meaning: from the standpoint of an ideology
items.meaningCN: 从意识形态立场上（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two proposals are ideologically opposed but practically similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两项提案在观念上对立，在实际操作上却相似。

items.meaning: a rigid defender of a doctrine
items.meaningCN: 教条捍卫者；意识形态者（-logue 表示说话者）
items.example: He was a party ideologue who never met a compromise he liked.
items.exampleCN: 他是个党的意识形态者，从不喜欢任何妥协。

items.meaning: one who studies or formulates ideologies
items.meaningCN: 研究或制定思想体系的人（-ist 表示人）
items.example: The regime relied on ideologists to rewrite the textbooks.
items.exampleCN: 该政权依靠意识形态专家改写教科书。

items.structure: Greek idea 'form, look', from idein 'to see'
items.meaning: a thought or concept in the mind
items.meaningCN: 心中的想法或概念（希腊语“形相、外观”）
items.example: The idea came to her on the bus.
items.exampleCN: 这个想法是她在公交车上想到的。

items.meaningCN: 理想；完美标准（-al 构成形容词与名词）
items.example: The plan was an ideal rather than a schedule.
items.exampleCN: 这个方案更像一种理想，而不是一份日程。

items.meaningCN: 把某物理想化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The memoir idealizes a childhood it barely describes.
items.exampleCN: 这本回忆录把它几乎没怎么描述的童年理想化了。

items.meaningCN: 生物学（bio- 生命 + -logy 学科）
items.example: She took biology as her second subject.
items.exampleCN: 她把生物学选为第二专业。

items.meaning: the study of the mind and behaviour
items.meaningCN: 心理学（psycho- 心灵 + -logy 学科）
items.example: Psychology was once taught as part of philosophy.
items.exampleCN: 心理学曾作为哲学的一部分被教授。

items.meaning: the study of religion and divine things
items.example: He studied theology before turning to law.
items.exampleCN: 他先学神学，后来转学法律。

latinEntries.structure: Greek idea 'form, look' from idein 'to see'
latinEntries.meaning: a form, a visible shape; a concept in the mind
latinEntries.meaningCN: 形相、可见的形状；心中的概念（拉丁语借自希腊语）
言说、论述、论著、学科（中世纪拉丁语 -logia）

latinEntries.structure: Greek logos, from legein 'to speak, gather'

definition_zh: 有偿付能力的；有溶解力的；溶剂（能溶解其他物质的液体）
definition_en: able to pay one's debts, or having the power to dissolve something; a substance that dissolves another
core_image: 一只玻璃瓶里透明液体正把糖块化开，瓶身贴着一张「已结清」的标签
scene: 检验员把一块树脂放进溶剂，几分钟后它完全化开。 The inspector dropped a piece of resin into the solvent and watched it dissolve within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里指「能溶解其他物质的液体」（第 2 个义项：作为溶剂的物质）；句意为检验员把一块树脂放进溶剂，几分钟后它完全化开。可辨识物件：玻璃瓶、糖块、结清标签、量勺。

pos.zh: 有偿付能力的；有溶解力的

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词加名词后缀，表性质 → 偿付能力
否定前缀加基础形容词 → 无力偿付的
同源动词加名词后缀 → 溶液；解法
拉丁「解开」词干加形容词后缀，义为「可被……」→ 可溶的
表示「分开」的前缀加同源动词 → 溶解
表示「离开」的前缀加同源动词 → 赦免；免除

senses.title: Financially able to pay debts
senses.titleCN: 财务上有能力清偿债务
senses.definition: describing a person or firm whose assets exceed liabilities and which can meet its obligations
senses.definitionCN: 描述资产超过负债、能够履行义务的个人或企业
senses.example: The company stayed solvent through the downturn by selling a division.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司靠出售一个部门在低迷期保持偿付能力。
senses.why: the adjective is the present participle of the Latin verb for loosening: one who can untie a debt is solvent.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词是拉丁语「松开」动词的现在分词：能解开债务的人就是有偿付能力的。

senses.title: A liquid that dissolves another substance
senses.titleCN: 能把另一种物质溶开的液体
senses.definition: in chemistry, the component of a mixture that does the dissolving, usually the larger part
senses.definitionCN: 化学中混合物里执行溶解的那个组分，通常占较大部分
senses.example: Water is the solvent in most biological reactions.
senses.exampleCN: 在多数生物反应中，水是溶剂。
senses.why: in a mixture one component must do the dissolving, and the larger, more mobile part is usually it.
senses.whyCN: 混合物中必须有一个组分执行溶解，通常就是占得更多、更易移动的那一部分。

senses.title: Having the power to dissolve
senses.definition: describing a substance or agent that can break another material into a solution
senses.definitionCN: 描述能把另一种材料化为溶液的物质或作用者
senses.example: The solvent power of the new cleaner surprised the lab.
senses.exampleCN: 这种新清洁剂的溶解力让实验室感到意外。
senses.why: the same participle can describe the agent instead of the mixture, which is why the word works as an adjective in chemistry too.
senses.whyCN: 同一分词也能描述起作用者而非混合物，因此这个词在化学里也作形容词。

senses.title: An industrial or household cleaning liquid
senses.definition: a volatile liquid used to remove grease, paint or resin in workshops and homes
senses.definitionCN: 在车间与家中用于去除油污、油漆或树脂的挥发性液体
senses.example: The workshop banned the old solvent after the ventilation report.
senses.exampleCN: 通风报告之后，车间禁用了那种旧溶剂。
senses.why: grease and resin will not wash away in water, so workshops need a stronger liquid to carry them off.
senses.whyCN: 油脂与树脂不能靠水洗掉，车间因此需要更强的液体把它们带走。

senses.title: Solvent abuse as inhalants
senses.titleCN: 作为吸入剂的溶剂滥用
senses.definition: the practice of inhaling fumes from glues and cleaners for a short-lived high
senses.definitionCN: 为获得短暂快感而吸入胶水或清洁剂蒸气的行为
senses.example: Solvent abuse among teenagers worried the school.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年吸食溶剂让学校担忧。
senses.why: the same volatile fumes that dissolve grease can be inhaled, which is why the word appears in warnings.
senses.whyCN: 溶开油脂的同一挥发性蒸气也能被吸入，因此这个词出现在警示语中。

senses.title: A solvent estate in law
senses.titleCN: 法律上足以清偿的遗产
senses.definition: an estate whose assets are enough to pay the deceased person's debts and gifts
senses.definitionCN: 资产足以支付死者债务与遗赠的遗产
senses.example: The executor confirmed that the estate was solvent.
senses.exampleCN: 遗嘱执行人确认这笔遗产足以清偿。
senses.why: the test for an estate is the same as for a firm: do the assets cover what must be paid out?
senses.whyCN: 对遗产的检验与对企业相同：资产是否覆盖必须付出的款项？

senses.title: Solvent extraction as a process
senses.definition: a method that uses a liquid to pull a wanted substance out of a solid or another liquid
senses.definitionCN: 用液体把目标物质从固体或另一液体中提取出来的方法
senses.example: Oil is often recovered by solvent extraction from crushed seed.
senses.exampleCN: 油常通过溶剂萃取从压碎的种子中提取。
senses.why: a liquid can carry a wanted substance out of a solid, which turns the chemical property into an industrial method.
senses.whyCN: 液体能把目标物质从固体中带出，这一化学性质于是变成工业方法。

senses.title: Solvent-free products
senses.definition: describing paints, glues or cleaners made without volatile organic liquids
senses.definitionCN: 描述不使用挥发性有机液体的油漆、胶水或清洁剂
senses.example: The builder switched to solvent-free adhesives for indoor work.
senses.exampleCN: 施工方在室内作业改用无溶剂胶黏剂。
senses.why: if the fumes are the problem, the simplest fix is to make the product without any solvent at all.
senses.whyCN: 如果问题出在蒸气，最简单的办法就是完全不用溶剂来制造产品。

intro.en: Solvent is the present participle of Latin solvere 'to loosen, pay'. English uses it for both paying and dissolving because the Latin verb covers both. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: solvent 是拉丁 solvere「松开、清偿」的现在分词。英语用它兼指偿付与溶解，因为拉丁动词本来就覆盖两义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Solvere meant 'to loosen, untie, dissolve, pay'. The two modern senses of solvent were both present in the Latin verb, one as untying a debt and one as loosening a substance.
items.cn: solvere 意为「松开、解开、溶解、清偿」。solvent 的两个现代义在拉丁动词中都已存在，一是解开债务，一是溶开物质。

items.en: The present participle solvens meant 'loosening, paying', and English took the form directly rather than through a noun.
items.cn: 现在分词 solvens 意为「正在松开、正在清偿」，英语直接吸收这一形式，而非经由名词。

items.en: Alchemists and later chemists used solvent for the liquid that dissolves a solid, a sense recorded in English from the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 炼金术士与后来的化学家用 solvent 指溶解固体的液体，这一义自 17 世纪见于英语。

items.en: The financial sense, able to pay what one owes, is also recorded in the seventeenth century and rests on the paying half of the Latin verb.
items.cn: 「能够清偿所欠」的财务义同样见于 17 世纪，依据的是拉丁动词中「清偿」的那一半。

items.en: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries made solvents ordinary industrial materials, and the word spread to cleaning, painting and extraction.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪使溶剂成为寻常工业材料，这个词扩展到清洁、涂装与萃取。

items.en: Late in the twentieth century, concern about fumes produced the compound solvent-free and a new sense of the word.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期对蒸气的担忧产生了「无溶剂」这一复合词与该词的新义。

note.en: Group one holds words from the loosening root or the same chemical field; group two holds financial adjectives that are often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「松开」词根或同属化学领域的词；第二组是常与它混淆的财务形容词。

entries.tag: the dissolved thing not the liquid
entries.definition: The substance that is dissolved; the solvent is what does the dissolving, so the two are opposites in a mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 指被溶解的物质；溶剂是执行溶解的一方，二者在混合物中相对。

entries.definition: The resulting mixture of solute and solvent, or an answer to a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 指溶质与溶剂形成的混合物，或问题的解答。

entries.definition: Describing the solute that can go into a solvent; it does not describe the liquid itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述能进入溶剂的溶质；并不描述液体本身。

entries.tag: the noun of the financial sense
entries.definition: The ability to pay debts; the adjective for that ability is solvent.
entries.definitionCN: 指偿债能力；表示该能力的形容词正是 solvent。

entries.definition: Judged safe to lend to; a firm can be solvent yet judged uncreditworthy.
entries.definitionCN: 指被认为可以安全放贷；企业可以有偿付能力却仍被认为不宜放贷。

entries.definition: Able to turn assets into cash quickly; solvency concerns totals, not speed.
entries.definitionCN: 指能迅速把资产变成现金；偿付能力关乎总额，而非速度。

entries.tag: a rare synonym for the chemical no
entries.definition: A dissolving agent, used in technical writing; solvent is the common form.
entries.definitionCN: 指起溶解作用之物，用于技术写作；solvent 是常见形式。

entries.definition: Describing an amount that must be paid; solvent describes the one who can pay it.
entries.definitionCN: 描述应支付的款项；solvent 描述有能力支付的人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: One Latin verb, two jobs: untie a debt and loosen a solid, so solvent means both able to pay and able to dissolve.
normal.cn: 一个拉丁动词干两件事：解开债务与溶开固体，所以这个词既指能清偿，也指能溶解。

normal.en: The family runs solve, solution, soluble, solvent, solvency, insolvent, dissolve.
normal.cn: 同族词包括解决、溶液、可溶的、溶剂、偿付能力、无力偿付的、溶解。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the uses: organic solvent, solvent extraction, solvent abuse, remain solvent.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分出用法：有机溶剂、溶剂萃取、吸食溶剂、保持偿付能力。

normal.en: In a mixture the solvent is the liquid, the solute is what disappears into it.
normal.cn: 在混合物中，溶剂是液体，溶质是溶进其中的东西。

normal.en: Solvent-free paint is a modern label made by putting the old word in front of free.
normal.cn: 无溶剂油漆是把旧词放在「无」前面造出的现代标签。

abstract.en: Picture a clear liquid eating a sugar lump while a settled bill hangs on the bottle.
abstract.cn: 想象一瓶透明液体正在化开糖块，瓶上挂着已结清的账单。

abstract.en: Picture a knot coming undone with no knife, only patience.
abstract.cn: 想象一个绳结在没有刀的情况下慢慢解开，只靠耐心。

abstract.en: Picture two faces of one coin: one reads able to pay, the other reads able to dissolve.
abstract.cn: 想象同一枚硬币的两面：一面写「能清偿」，一面写「能溶解」。

examples.en: The firm remained solvent even after the loss, because its property was worth more than its debt.
examples.cn: 即使出现亏损，这家企业仍有偿付能力，因为其房产价值高于债务。

examples.en: Use the solvent outdoors; the fumes are heavier than air.
examples.cn: 要在户外使用这种溶剂，其蒸气比空气重。

examples.en: The estate was solvent, so every creditor was paid in full.
examples.cn: 这笔遗产足以清偿，因此每位债权人都获得全额支付。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「解开」的词根加表示「……的」的后缀——能解开债务的是有偿付能力的，能解开物质的则成了溶剂

root: 拉丁 solvere「松开、解开、溶解、清偿」的现在分词 solvens 直接进入英语；同一动词的过去分词与名词形式给出 solution、solvency，同根还有 dissolve、absolve。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses use one participle in two fields: a payer who can untie debts, and a liquid that unties solids, then the cleaning trade, inhalant misuse, estates, extraction and products made without it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个分词用在两个领域：能解开债务的清偿者，能溶开固体的液体，随后是清洁行业、吸入滥用、遗产、萃取，以及不含它的产品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear liquid eating a sugar lump, with a settled bill hanging on the bottle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一瓶透明液体正在化开糖块，瓶上挂着已结清的账单。

branches.en: THE PAYER: a person, a firm or an estate that can untie what it owes.
branches.cn: 清偿者：能解开所欠之债的个人、企业或遗产。

branches.en: THE LIQUID AND ITS POWER: the dissolving component, and the strength it brings.
branches.cn: 液体与力量：执行溶解的组分，以及它所带的溶解力。

branches.en: THE TRADE: cleaning fluids and extraction methods turn the chemical sense into work.
branches.cn: 行业：清洁液与萃取方法把化学义变成工作。

branches.en: MISUSE: the same fumes that clean metal can be inhaled.
branches.cn: 滥用：清洁金属的同一蒸气也可被吸入。

branches.en: THE NEGATIVE FORM: modern products are labelled by the absence of the solvent.
branches.cn: 否定形式：现代产品以「不含溶剂」来标注。

intro.en: Solvent is one Latin participle serving two English fields; the root also gives solve, solution, soluble and dissolve.
intro.cn: solvent 是一个拉丁分词，服务于两个英语领域；同一词根还给出 solve、solution、soluble 与 dissolve。

latinIntro.en: Latin solvere and solvens stand behind the whole family, from solution to insolvency.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 solvere 与 solvens 支撑整个词族，从 solution 到 insolvency。

items.exampleCN: 这个动词覆盖两个领域。

items.example: The participle became an English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词变成了英语词。

items.example: They solved the shortage by importing.
items.exampleCN: 他们靠进口解决了短缺。

items.example: The court absolved him of blame.

definition_zh: 迁移；迁徙；移居；（数据、系统）迁移；（细胞）移动
definition_en: to move from one place, habitat or system to another, especially over a distance and often for a season or a new life
core_image: 一群身影越过旧地平线，走向另一条尚未抵达的地平线
scene: 这里指「迁移」。 Every October the birds migrate south along the coast.
sceneCN: 这里 migrate 是「迁徙」（第 1 个义项：动物随季节从一处栖息地移到另一处）；句意：每年十月，鸟群沿着海岸向南迁徙。场景要点：一条海岸线、排成人字的鸟群、地平线上尚未到达的南方。

pos.zh: 迁移；迁徙；移居（常与 from、to 连用）
（信息技术）迁移（数据、系统、账户）

collocations.zh: 在两个地方之间来回迁移

senses.title: Animals on the move
senses.titleCN: 动物迁徙：随季节换一片栖息地
senses.definition: of animals, to move from one habitat or region to another at a distance, usually with the seasons
senses.definitionCN: 指动物远距离地从一处栖息地或地区移到另一处，通常随季节而行
senses.example: Every October the birds migrate south along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 每年十月，鸟群沿着海岸向南迁徙。
senses.why: The animal sense is recorded from 1753. Latin migrare already meant 'to move from one place to another', and birds made the word's clearest picture.
senses.whyCN: 动物义项自 1753 年有记录。拉丁语 migrare 本就意为“从一处移到另一处”，而鸟群给这个词提供了最清晰的画面。

senses.title: People settle elsewhere
senses.definition: of people, to move from one place of residence to another at a distance, especially to another country
senses.definitionCN: 指人远距离地从一处居住地迁到另一处，尤指迁往另一个国家
senses.example: Her grandparents migrated to the coast in the 1950s.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖父母在 20 世纪 50 年代移居到了海边。
senses.why: The sense for persons is recorded by 1770. The same movement now carries a household, a language and a future, not only a body.
senses.whyCN: 指人的义项在 1770 年已有记录。同一种移动现在承载的是一个家庭、一门语言和一种未来，而不只是一具身体。

senses.title: Move from place to place
senses.titleCN: 一般移动：只说到从一处到另一处
senses.definition: to pass from one place or position to another, without stressing either departure or arrival
senses.definitionCN: 从一处或一个位置移到另一处，既不强调离开，也不强调抵达
senses.example: The infection migrated from the skin to the joint.
senses.exampleCN: 感染从皮肤转移到了关节。
senses.why: This is the word's first English sense, recorded in the 1690s: 'to pass from one place to another'. It is the plain trunk from which the other senses branch.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词在英语里的第一个义项，1690 年代有记录：“从一处移到另一处”。它是其他义项分叉出来的那根主干。

senses.title: Data and systems
senses.titleCN: 数据与系统迁移：换一个平台继续运行
senses.definition: in computing, to move data, programs or services from one system or platform to another
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，把数据、程序或服务从一个系统或平台移到另一个
senses.example: The company will migrate its accounts to the new platform in June.
senses.exampleCN: 公司将在六月把账户迁移到新平台。
senses.why: The old picture fits exactly: something alive in one place is picked up and set down in another, and must keep working after the move.
senses.whyCN: 旧画面严丝合缝：在一个地方运行着的东西被拿起、放到另一个地方，而且搬完之后还得继续运行。

senses.title: Cells and substances
senses.definition: in biology and medicine, of cells or substances, to move within the body or from one tissue to another
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学与医学中，指细胞或物质在体内移动，或从一种组织移到另一种
senses.example: These cells migrate to the wound and begin repairing it.
senses.exampleCN: 这些细胞迁移到伤口处并开始修复。
senses.why: The distance shrinks to millimetres, but the verb keeps its shape: a body leaves one site and arrives at another.
senses.whyCN: 距离缩短到毫米级，但动词的形状没变：一个个体离开一处，抵达另一处。

senses.title: Labour on the move
senses.titleCN: 劳动力流动：为生计迁往别处
senses.definition: of workers or populations, to move from one region to another in search of work or better conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指工人或人群为寻找工作或更好的条件而从一地区迁往另一地区
senses.example: Whole villages migrated to the cities when the factories opened.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂开工后，整村整村的人迁往城市。
senses.why: When migration is driven by wages, the word stops describing nature and starts describing economics.
senses.whyCN: 当迁徙由工资驱动时，这个词就不再描述自然，而开始描述经济。

senses.title: Switch to a new way
senses.titleCN: 比喻：转向新的做法或平台
senses.definition: figuratively, to change from one practice, model or system to another
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法：从一种做法、模式或制度转到另一种
senses.example: Many readers have migrated from print to podcasts.
senses.exampleCN: 许多读者已经从纸媒转向播客。
senses.why: The journey no longer has geography, only a before and an after. The verb survives because the feeling of relocation survives.
senses.whyCN: 这趟旅程不再有地理，只剩下“之前”与“之后”。动词之所以还活着，是因为那种搬迁的感觉还活着。

senses.title: Round trip
senses.titleCN: 循环迁徙：去了还会回来
senses.definition: to move regularly between two places, as migratory birds or pastoral families do
senses.definitionCN: 像候鸟或游牧家庭那样，在两处之间规律地往返
senses.example: The herders migrate between the lowlands in winter and the high pastures in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 牧民冬天迁到低地，夏天迁往高山牧场。
senses.why: Not every migration is one-way. The word covers the round trip as easily as the exodus, because it names the moving, not the staying.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有迁徙都是单向的。这个词既能指一去不返的大迁徙，也能指往返循环，因为它命名的是“移动”，而不是“留下”。

senses.title: Direction left open
senses.titleCN: 用法分界：不指明移出还是移入
senses.definition: used without specifying whether one is leaving a place or arriving at one, unlike emigrate and immigrate
senses.definitionCN: 使用时不明说自己是离开某地还是抵达某地，这与 emigrate 和 immigrate 不同
senses.example: The report says people migrate for work, without asking which border they cross.
senses.exampleCN: 报告说人们为工作而迁移，并不追问他们越过的是哪一道边界。
senses.why: The Century Dictionary put it plainly in 1897: migrate stresses the change itself, not the place of departure or of stopping. Emigrate looks back, immigrate looks forward.
senses.whyCN: 《世纪词典》1897 年说得很清楚：migrate 强调变化本身，而不强调出发地或落脚地。emigrate 回头看，immigrate 向前看。

intro.en: Migrate comes from Latin migrare 'to move from one place to another', probably from PIE *(e)meigw- 'to change'. Its English life began with the plain sense 'pass from one place to another' and later specialised into animals, people and machines. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: migrate 来自拉丁语 migrare“从一处移到另一处”，可能源自原始印欧语 *(e)meigw-“改变”。它在英语里先有“从一处到另一处”的平实义，后来才分化出动物、人与机器诸义。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'to pass from one place to another', from Latin migratus, past participle of migrare 'to move from one place to another'.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 17 世纪 90 年代，意为“从一处移到另一处”，来自拉丁语 migratus，即 migrare“从一处移到另一处”的过去分词。

items.en: Latin migrare is probably originally *migwros, from PIE *(e)meigw- 'to change', an extended form of the root *mei- (1) 'to change, go, move'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 migrare 最初大概是 *migwros，来自原始印欧语 *(e)meigw-“改变”，而这是词根 *mei-（第一支）“改变、走、移动”的扩展形式。

items.en: Of animals, 'to remove from one habitat to another at a distance' is recorded. The word's most familiar picture, a flock crossing a season, is fixed here.
items.cn: 记录到指动物的“远距离地从一处栖息地移到另一处”。这个词最熟悉的画面——一群鸟越过一个季节——在这里固定下来。

items.en: Of persons, 'to pass or remove from one place of residence to another at a distance' is recorded, especially from one country to another.
items.cn: 记录到指人的“远距离地从一处居住地迁到另一处”，尤指从一个国家到另一个国家。

items.en: The Century Dictionary draws the line still taught today: migrate stresses the change, not the departure or the stopping place; emigrate views the person leaving, immigrate views the person arriving.
items.cn: 《世纪词典》划出了今天仍在教的界线：migrate 强调变化，而不强调出发地或落脚地；emigrate 着眼于离开的人，immigrate 着眼于抵达的人。

items.en: The computing sense, to move data or services to another system, extends the old picture into machines. The family keeps its bearings: migration (1610s), migrant (1760), emigrate (1778), immigrate (1620s).
items.cn: 计算机义“把数据或服务迁到另一系统”把旧画面延伸到机器上。这个词族的方向感仍在：migration（17 世纪 10 年代）、migrant（1760）、emigrate（1778）、immigrate（17 世纪 20 年代）。

note.en: The first group is the family built on migrate: the process, the person or animal, and the adjective. The second group separates the words that name a move with a direction, which migrate deliberately leaves out.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在 migrate 上的词族：过程、人（或动物）、形容词。第二组区分那些带方向的“迁移”词，而 migrate 恰恰有意不指明方向。

entries.definition: the act or process of migrating, or a group of people or animals doing it. It is the noun of the event, not a synonym of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 迁移的行为或过程，或正在迁移的一群人或动物。它是这一事件的名词，不是动词的同义词。

entries.definition: a person or animal that migrates, or an adjective meaning 'migratory'. It names the mover, while migrate names the moving.
entries.definitionCN: 迁移的人或动物，也可作形容词表示“迁徙的”。它命名的是移动者，而 migrate 命名的是移动本身。

entries.definition: having the habit of migrating, as a species or a way of life. It describes the pattern, not a single journey.
entries.definitionCN: 有迁徙习性的，如某个物种或某种生活方式。它描述的是模式，而不是某一趟旅程。

entries.definition: relating to migration. It is rare and mostly replaced by migratory, but it keeps the noun's abstract frame.
entries.definitionCN: 与迁移有关的。它很少用，多半被 migratory 取代，但仍保留名词的抽象框架。

entries.definition: to leave one's own country and settle elsewhere. The prefix e- is Latin ex- 'out': it views the person from the place left behind.
entries.definitionCN: 离开本国到别处定居。前缀 e- 即拉丁语 ex-“向外”：它从被留下的那个地方看这个人。

entries.definition: to come into a country to settle there. The prefix im- is Latin in- 'into': it views the person from the place of arrival.
entries.definitionCN: 进入某国并在此定居。前缀 im- 即拉丁语 in-“进入”：它从抵达地看这个人。

entries.definition: to move to a new location, often with an employer or a company. It is more administrative than migrate and usually one-way and planned.
entries.definitionCN: 搬到新地点，常指随雇主或公司搬迁。它比 migrate 更带行政色彩，通常是单向且有计划的。

entries.definition: to migrate across or through something, and in religion to pass into another body after death. The prefix trans- 'across' adds a crossing.
entries.definitionCN: 跨越某地迁移；在宗教中也指死后灵魂转入另一具身体。前缀 trans-“横越”加了一层“穿过”的意思。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin migrare 'to move from one place to another', the PIE root *mei- 'to go, change', and the direction-marked family emigrate, immigrate, transmigrate.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 migrare“从一处移到另一处”、原始印欧语词根 *mei-“走、改变”，以及带方向标记的 emigrate、immigrate、transmigrate。

normal.en: migr- means 'move from one place to another'. Migrate is the bare movement, with no prefix telling you which way.
normal.cn: migr- 表示“从一处移到另一处”。migrate 是光秃秃的移动，没有前缀告诉你方向。

normal.en: emigrate has e- (ex-, 'out'): you leave. immigrate has im- (in-, 'into'): you arrive. The same journey looks different from each end.
normal.cn: emigrate 带 e-（ex-，“向外”）：你离开。immigrate 带 im-（in-，“进入”）：你抵达。同一趟旅程，从两端看不一样。

normal.en: migration is the event, migrant is the mover, migratory is the habit. Three forms, three jobs.
normal.cn: migration 是事件，migrant 是移动者，migratory 是习性。三个形式，三份工作。

normal.en: The root may be PIE *(e)meigw- 'to change', linked to *mei- 'to go, move'. Latin migrare is the branch that reached English.
normal.cn: 词根可能是原始印欧语 *(e)meigw-“改变”，与 *mei-“走、移动”相关。拉丁语 migrare 是抵达英语的那一支。

normal.en: Computing borrowed the bird: data migrate to a new platform the way flocks move to a new coast.
normal.cn: 计算机借用了鸟：数据迁到新平台，就像鸟群迁到一片新的海岸。

abstract.en: Picture a coastline at dusk and a line of wings crossing the last of the light. Nothing in the picture says whether they will come back.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏的海岸线，以及一排翅膀划过最后一点光。这幅画里没有任何东西说明它们会不会回来。

abstract.en: Migration is measured from the mover, not from the border. That is why the same person is an emigrant to one country and an immigrant to another.
abstract.cn: 迁徙是从移动者身上度量的，不是从边界度量的。所以同一个人对一国是移出者，对另一国是移入者。

abstract.en: The word travels as far as its picture: birds, workers, cells, files. Wherever something leaves one place and keeps living in another, migrate still fits.
abstract.cn: 这个词跟着它的画面走得一样远：鸟、工人、细胞、文件。只要某物离开一处并在另一处继续存活，migrate 就仍然适用。

examples.en: The whales migrate thousands of kilometres to breed in warmer water.
examples.cn: 鲸鱼迁徙数千公里，到更温暖的水域繁殖。

examples.en: Her family migrated from the north to the coast three generations ago.
examples.cn: 她家三代以前从北方迁到了海边。

examples.en: The archive will migrate to a new server over the weekend.
examples.cn: 档案库将在周末迁移到新的服务器上。

dict_mnemonic.text: “买格瑞特”——买张票，格瑞特就跨过边界去了另一片土地 → migrate 迁移、迁徙（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 migrare“从一处移到另一处”，核心是“离开一块地面，落到另一块地面”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of migrate, all from one motion: a body leaves one place and arrives at another. The word never says which end matters, which is why birds, workers, cells and files can all use it.
sensesIntro.cn: migrate 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：一个个体离开一处，抵达另一处。这个词从不说哪一端更重要，所以鸟、工人、细胞与文件都能用它。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group crossing from one horizon to another, with the departure and the arrival equally unnamed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群身影从一条地平线越向另一条，出发地与抵达地同样不被点名。

chain: THE MOVE ITSELF IS THE WORD

branches.en: SEASONS: animals and herders move on a rhythm, and the journey may be a round trip rather than an exit.
branches.cn: 季节：动物与牧民按节奏移动，这趟旅程可能是往返，而不是出走。

branches.en: HOUSEHOLDS: people move to settle or to work, and the move carries a family or a labour force.
branches.cn: 家庭：人为定居或为工作而移动，这一移动承载的是一个家庭或一支劳动力。

branches.en: PLAIN MOTION: the oldest sense describes movement without direction, which is exactly what separates it from emigrate and immigrate.
branches.cn: 平实移动：最老的义项描述无方向的移动，这正是它与 emigrate、immigrate 的分界。

branches.en: SYSTEMS: data and habits change platforms, and the old geography becomes a before and an after.
branches.cn: 系统：数据与习惯更换平台，旧的地理变成“之前”与“之后”。

branches.en: THE BODY: cells make the same journey at millimetre scale, from one tissue to another.
branches.cn: 身体：细胞以毫米尺度完成同一趟旅程，从一种组织到另一种。

intro.en: Migrate is Latin migr- 'move, shift' plus the verb ending -ate. Direction is added by prefixes: e- 'out', im- 'in', trans- 'across'. English also builds -ion, -ant and -ory nouns and adjectives.
intro.cn: migrate 是拉丁语 migr-“移动、迁徙”加动词词尾 -ate。方向由前缀补充：e-“向外”、im-“向内”、trans-“横越”。英语还用 -ion、-ant、-ory 构成名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin migrare 'to move from one place to another' gives the stem; migratio gives migration and migrans gives migrant. The family is Latin throughout, with no Greek element.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 migrare“从一处移到另一处”提供词干；migratio 给出 migration，migrans 给出 migrant。这个词族从头到尾都是拉丁语，没有希腊语成分。

items.meaning: to move from one place to another
items.meaningCN: 从一处移到另一处（migr- 移动 + -ate 动词词尾）
items.example: Some species migrate only once in a lifetime.
items.exampleCN: 有些物种一生只迁徙一次。

items.meaning: the act or process of moving to another place
items.meaningCN: 迁移；迁徙（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: The migration takes three generations to complete.
items.exampleCN: 这场迁徙要三代人才能完成。

items.meaningCN: 迁徙者；移民（-ant 表示施动者）
items.example: The camp houses migrant workers from four provinces.
items.exampleCN: 营地里住着来自四个省份的务工移民。

items.meaningCN: 有迁徙习性的；迁徙的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.example: The wetland is a stopover for migratory birds.
items.exampleCN: 这片湿地是候鸟的中转站。

items.meaning: to leave one's country and settle elsewhere
items.meaningCN: 移出；迁离本国（e- 向外 + migrate）
items.exampleCN: 他的父母在 1979 年移居国外。

items.meaning: to come into a country and settle
items.meaningCN: 移入；迁入定居（im- 向内 + migrate）
items.example: They immigrated with two suitcases and no English.
items.exampleCN: 他们带着两只箱子、一句英语也不会就迁了进来。

items.meaning: to pass across or into another body or place
items.meaningCN: 跨越迁移；灵魂转世（trans- 横越 + migrate）
items.example: The doctrine says the soul transmigrates after death.
items.exampleCN: 该教义说灵魂在死后转世。

items.meaning: a person who leaves a country
items.example: The ship carried emigrants to the south.
items.exampleCN: 这艘船把移出者载往南方。

items.meaning: a person who comes to settle in a country
items.example: The city grew fast on immigrant labour.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市靠移民劳动力迅速扩张。

items.meaning: the act of leaving one's country
items.meaningCN: 移出；迁离（e- 向外 + migration）
items.exampleCN: 人口迁出使高地村庄空了下来。

items.meaning: the act of entering and settling in a country
items.meaningCN: 移入；迁入定居（im- 向内 + migration）
items.example: Immigration rules changed again last spring.
items.exampleCN: 移民入境规定去年春天又变了。

items.meaning: a passing across, or the passing of a soul into another body
items.meaningCN: 跨越迁移；灵魂转世（trans- 横越 + migration）
items.example: Transmigration is central to the doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 转世之说在该教义中处于核心位置。

latinEntries.meaning: to move from one place to another

definition_zh: n. 阁楼；屋顶正下方的顶层房间或空间
definition_en: A room or space just under the roof of a house, often used for storage.
core_image: 屋顶斜面下那间要低头走的小屋
scene: 他们在屋顶下那间小屋里翻出一只旧箱子。 They found an old trunk in the attic under the sloping roof.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：attic 指屋顶正下方、常用来堆放杂物的顶层空间。

senses.title: The space under the roof
senses.definition: the room or unfinished area directly beneath the roof of a building
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物屋顶正下方的房间或未装修区域
senses.example: The cases were stacked along the attic wall.
senses.exampleCN: 箱子沿着阁楼的墙堆放。
senses.why: The word came from Attic architecture, where a low storey was set above the main cornice, so the top space took the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自阿提卡式建筑：主檐口之上再加一层矮层，于是顶层空间就沿用了这个名字。

senses.title: A place for stored things
senses.definition: by extension, the part of a house where old possessions are put out of the way
senses.definitionCN: 引申指家中把旧物挪开存放的那一部分
senses.example: Her letters had lain in the attic for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 她的信件在阁楼里躺了几十年。
senses.why: Because that space was cheap and awkward, it became the natural store, and the word carries the smell of dust and old boxes.
senses.whyCN: 因为那块空间廉价又不规整，它成了天然的储物处，这个词也带上了灰尘与旧箱子的气味。

intro.en: Attic is short for Attic storey, from Greek Attikos, of Attica, the region of Athens, whose builders set a small order above the main cornice.
intro.cn: attic 是 Attic storey「阿提卡层」的省略，出自希腊语 Attikos「阿提卡的」，即雅典所在地区，那里的工匠在主檐口之上再加一层小型柱式。

items.en: Attica was the district around Athens, and its name gave the adjective Attikos.
items.cn: 阿提卡是雅典周边地区，其名产生形容词 Attikos。

items.en: Attikos meant of Attica, and by extension elegant, since Athenian taste was the standard.
items.cn: Attikos 意为「阿提卡的」，并引申为「雅致的」，因为雅典品味被视为标准。

items.en: Latin took the word as Atticus, used for both Athenian style and a refined manner.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 Atticus，既指雅典风格，也指优雅的举止。

items.en: French architecture used attique for a low storey above the main cornice.
items.cn: 法国建筑用 attique 指主檐口之上的一层矮层。

items.en: English adopted attic storey in the eighteenth century, then shortened it to attic.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪采用 attic storey，随后缩略为 attic。

items.en: By the nineteenth century attic meant the whole room under the roof, not just the architectural feature.
items.cn: 到十九世纪 attic 指屋顶下的整个房间，而不再只指那个建筑构件。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps words that share the opening letters; the near-meaning group lists other names for the top space of a house.
note.cn: 形近组保留开头字母相同的词；近义组列出房屋顶层空间的其他名称。

entries.definition: A playful or absurd act.
entries.definitionCN: 滑稽荒唐的举动。

entries.definition: A diplomat on a mission staff.
entries.definitionCN: 使馆随员。

entries.definition: To act violently against.
entries.definitionCN: 攻击。

entries.definition: To declare that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某事为真。

entries.definition: An upper space under a roof.
entries.definitionCN: 屋顶下的上层空间。

entries.definition: A tiny room at the top of a house.
entries.definitionCN: 房屋顶层的小房间。

entries.definition: A roof whose slope holds rooms.
entries.definitionCN: 斜面内可设房间的屋顶。

entries.definition: A small loft just under the ridge.
entries.definitionCN: 紧靠屋脊的小阁楼。

normalIntro.en: Attic began as Attic storey, a top layer in Athenian style, and now means the room under any roof.
normalIntro.cn: attic 起初是 Attic storey「雅典式顶层」，如今泛指任何屋顶下的房间。

normal.en: Say in the attic, not on the attic.
normal.cn: 要说 in the attic，不说 on the attic。

normal.en: An attic conversion turns storage into a room.
normal.cn: attic conversion 把储物空间改成房间。

normal.en: A loft is often open; an attic is usually closed.
normal.cn: loft 常是开敞的，attic 通常是封闭的。

normal.en: A garret is a poor little attic.
normal.cn: garret 是穷困的小阁楼。

normal.en: Capital Attic means Athenian, lower case means the room.
normal.cn: 大写 Attic 指雅典的，小写指阁楼。

abstract.en: Picture a sloping ceiling you must duck under.
abstract.cn: 想象一片必须低头才能走的斜天花板。

abstract.en: Imagine dust hanging in a single window beam.
abstract.cn: 想象灰尘悬在一道窗光里。

abstract.en: Think of a trunk that has not moved in years.
abstract.cn: 想象一只多年未动的箱子。

examples.en: They slept in a narrow attic room.
examples.cn: 他们睡在一间狭窄的阁楼房里。

examples.en: The attic was full of broken chairs.
examples.cn: 阁楼里堆满破损的椅子。

examples.en: A ladder led up to the attic hatch.
examples.cn: 一架梯子通向阁楼的舱口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：Attic「雅典式的」+ storey「楼层」——雅典式建筑在主檐口上加的那层矮楼，就是 attic 阁楼。

root: 希腊语 Attikos「阿提卡的、雅典式的」经拉丁语 Atticus、法语 attique 进入建筑术语，指主檐口之上的矮层 attic storey；缩略为 attic 后转指屋顶下的整个房间。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses point to the same place: the architectural space beneath the roof, and that space used as the house store for old things.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项指向同一处地方：屋顶之下的建筑空间，以及被当作旧物仓库使用的那个空间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low room under a sloping roof where you must duck
core.cn: 核心意象：屋顶斜面下那间要低头走的小屋

branches.en: A room beneath the sloping roof.
branches.cn: 斜屋顶下的房间。

branches.en: A hatch reached by a ladder.
branches.cn: 靠梯子通达的舱口。

branches.en: Cases stacked along the wall.
branches.cn: 沿墙堆放的箱子。

branches.en: Letters lying untouched for decades.
branches.cn: 数十年无人翻动的信件。

branches.en: The same space, seen as room and as store.
branches.cn: 同一空间，既作房间也作仓库。

intro.en: Attic is a place adjective turned noun: Attic plus storey; the same clipping pattern gives basement and mezzanine their everyday use.
intro.cn: attic 是地名形容词转为名词：Attic 加 storey；同样的省略方式也让 basement 与 mezzanine 进入日常用法。

latinIntro.en: The layer is Greek rather than Latin: Attikos, of Attica, passed through Latin Atticus; Greek oikos, house, gives economy beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 这一层属希腊语而非拉丁语：Attikos「阿提卡的」经拉丁语 Atticus 传来；旁边的希腊语 oikos「房屋」产生 economy。

latinEntries.exampleCN: Attikos 指那种风格。
Atticus 把它带向北方。
oikos 产生 economy。

definition_zh: 好斗性；攻击性；（受称赞的）进取劲头
definition_en: the quality of being quick to attack or quarrel; also the bold, forceful drive to win or achieve, praised in sport and business
core_image: 一股向前扑的劲头
scene: 新教练要求球员逼抢更凶，可裁判也盯得更紧。 Aggressiveness wins the ball, not the argument.
sceneCN: 这里 aggressiveness 是「进取劲头」（第 2 个义项：主动向前、敢于争取的劲头）；句意为这种劲头能抢到球，却吵不赢架。核心画面是一股向前扑的劲头。

pos.zh: 好斗性；攻击性；进取劲头

forms.label: 不可数名词，无复数形式

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ness 的形容词，义为「好斗的；有进取心的」
aggressive 加 -ly，义为「咄咄逼人地；积极地」
同根名词，义为「侵略；攻击行为」
加 -or 构成，义为「侵略者；挑衅者」

senses.title: Readiness to attack or quarrel
senses.definition: the quality of being quick to attack, argue or force your way, so that others feel threatened
senses.definitionCN: 动辄攻击、争吵或强行推进的性质，使他人感到威胁
senses.example: His aggressiveness made every meeting feel like a fight.
senses.exampleCN: 他的好斗让每次开会都像在打架。
senses.why: Aggredi means to step toward someone, and when that step is hostile the -ness noun names a standing readiness to pick a fight.
senses.whyCN: aggredi 意为「朝某人迈步」，当这一步带着敌意时，加 -ness 的名词就表示一种随时准备挑事的常态。

senses.title: Bold drive to win or achieve
senses.definition: the quality of pushing forward confidently and refusing to wait, valued in sport, sales and negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 自信地向前推进、不肯等待的性质，在体育、销售与谈判中受到重视
senses.example: The team lacked the aggressiveness to close the game out.
senses.exampleCN: 这支球队缺少把比赛拿下的那股拼劲。
senses.why: The same forward step is read positively here: nothing changes in the image except whether the observer welcomes the push.
senses.whyCN: 同样是向前迈步，这里被正面解读：画面没有变，变的只是旁观者是否欢迎这一推。

intro.en: Aggressiveness is three layers stacked on a Latin step: ad-, toward, plus gradi, to step, gives aggredi, to approach; -ive turns it into an adjective and -ness into a quality.
intro.cn: aggressiveness 是在拉丁语「迈步」上叠起的三层：ad-「朝向」加 gradi「迈步」构成 aggredi「走近」；-ive 把它变成形容词，-ness 再变成性质名词。

items.en: Latin ad meant to or toward, and it doubles its d to g before a g, giving the spelling aggr-.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ad 意为「向、朝」，在 g 前把 d 同化为 g，于是拼作 aggr-。

items.en: Latin gradi meant to step or walk, the root behind grade, gradual, progress and congress.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gradi 意为「迈步、行走」，是 grade、gradual、progress 与 congress 背后的词根。

items.en: The deponent verb aggredi meant to approach or to attack, a step taken toward someone with intent.
items.cn: 异态动词 aggredi 意为「走近、攻击」，即带着意图朝某人迈出的一步。

items.en: Late Latin aggressivus described someone given to attacking, built on the past participle aggressus.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 aggressivus 描述动辄攻击的人，建立在过去分词 aggressus 之上。

items.en: English took aggressive in the seventeenth century, first of hostile nations and later of forceful salespeople.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 aggressive，先用于敌对国家，后来用于强势的推销员。

items.en: Adding the native suffix -ness produced aggressiveness, now used both of hostility and of praised competitive drive.
items.cn: 加上本族后缀 -ness 得到 aggressiveness，如今既指敌意，也指被称赞的竞争劲头。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the grad- family of stepping; the near-meaning group lists other nouns for a pushing, fighting temperament.
note.cn: 形近组留在表示「迈步」的 grad- 词族内；近义组列出其他表示「好推进、好斗气质」的名词。

entries.definition: Hostile or violent behaviour toward another.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人怀有敌意或暴力的行为。

entries.definition: Ready to attack, or pushing forward with force.
entries.definitionCN: 随时准备攻击，或强势向前推进。

entries.definition: Forward movement toward a better state.
entries.definitionCN: 朝更好状态的向前推进。

entries.definition: To go back to an earlier, worse state.
entries.definitionCN: 退回更早、更差的状态。

entries.definition: Confidence in stating what you want without attacking.
entries.definitionCN: 自信地说出诉求而不攻击他人。

entries.definition: Eager, openly hostile readiness to fight.
entries.definitionCN: 急切而公开敌对的开战意愿。

entries.definition: Unfriendly opposition or dislike.
entries.definitionCN: 不友好的对立或厌恶。

entries.definition: Energy and determination to get things done.
entries.definitionCN: 把事情做成的干劲与决心。

normalIntro.en: Aggressiveness is aggressive plus -ness: the quality of being aggressive, whether that means picking fights or chasing wins.
normalIntro.cn: aggressiveness 就是 aggressive 加 -ness：好斗或敢拼的那种性质，既可能指挑事，也可能指争胜。

normal.en: -ness turns any adjective into a quality: kind gives kindness, aggressive gives aggressiveness.
normal.cn: -ness 把形容词变成性质：kind 变 kindness，aggressive 变 aggressiveness。

normal.en: The double g is ad- meeting gradi, the same doubling you see in aggravate and aggregate.
normal.cn: 双写 g 是 ad- 遇上 gradi，与 aggravate、aggregate 中的双写相同。

normal.en: Aggression is the act; aggressiveness is the habit of doing it.
normal.cn: aggression 是那次行为，aggressiveness 是习惯性地这么做。

normal.en: In sport writing aggressiveness is praise; in a complaint letter it is blame.
normal.cn: 体育报道里 aggressiveness 是褒义，投诉信里则是贬义。

normal.en: It is uncountable, so say too much aggressiveness, not many aggressivenesses.
normal.cn: 它不可数，所以说 too much aggressiveness，不说 many aggressivenesses。

abstract.en: Picture a player who lunges at every loose ball before anyone else moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一个球员，每次球一松就抢在所有人之前扑上去。

abstract.en: Imagine two rams butting heads, then the same energy turned into a sales pitch.
abstract.cn: 想象两只公羊顶角，再把同一股劲头变成一段推销说辞。

abstract.en: Think of a spring compressed and ready to push whatever stands in front.
abstract.cn: 想象一根压紧的弹簧，随时准备推开挡在前面的一切。

examples.en: The coach praised the aggressiveness of his young defenders.
examples.cn: 教练称赞了年轻后卫的那股拼劲。

examples.en: Aggressiveness in the interview room can cost you the offer.
examples.cn: 面试时咄咄逼人可能让你丢掉这份工作。

examples.en: They mistook quiet confidence for a lack of aggressiveness.
examples.cn: 他们把沉着的自信误当成缺乏进取心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿哥瑞死我内思」——阿哥（ag-gres）扑过来要死磕（sive），心里（ness）憋着那股劲，就是好斗性、进取劲头。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「朝向」在 g 前同化为 ag-，加 gradi「迈步」构成 aggredi「走近、攻击」，其过去分词 aggressus 派生出晚期拉丁语 aggressivus，英语借为 aggressive，再加本族后缀 -ness 构成 aggressiveness，字面即「不断向前迈步的性质」。

sensesIntro.en: One forward push is read two ways: aimed at a person it is hostility, aimed at a goal it is praised drive, and the noun names whichever habit the speaker sees.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一股向前的推力有两种读法：对着人就是敌意，对着目标就是被称赞的干劲，这个名词指的就是说话人看到的那一种习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a force that keeps stepping forward
core.cn: 核心意象：一股不断向前迈步的劲

branches.en: Stepping toward someone to start a quarrel.
branches.cn: 朝某人迈步去挑起争执。

branches.en: A temper that others learn to avoid.
branches.cn: 让别人学会绕着走的脾气。

branches.en: Pressing forward to win a loose ball.
branches.cn: 向前逼抢去争一个松球。

branches.en: Refusing to wait for permission to act.
branches.cn: 不肯等着别人允许才行动。

branches.en: Both name a habit, not a single act.
branches.cn: 两者都指习惯，而非一次行为。

intro.en: Aggressiveness is built in clear layers: a prefix of direction, a root of stepping, an adjective suffix and a native noun suffix.
intro.cn: aggressiveness 的层次非常清楚：方向前缀、迈步词根、形容词后缀，再加本族名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad plus gradi gave aggredi and its participle aggressus; only the final -ness is English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad 加 gradi 构成 aggredi 及其分词 aggressus；只有最后的 -ness 是英语本族的。

latinEntries.example: Ad doubles to ag- before g.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ad 在 g 前双写为 ag-。
gradi 提供 grad- 与 gress-。

latinEntries.example: Aggredi is the source of aggress-.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aggredi 是 aggress- 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Aggressus carries the ss into English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aggressus 把 ss 带进英语。

definition_zh: 农用化学品（农药、除草剂、化肥等）；农化行业
definition_en: a manufactured chemical used on farmland, such as a pesticide, herbicide or fertiliser; also the industry that produces these substances
core_image: 从化工厂搬到田里的那一袋药
scene: 这片稻田过去靠人工除虫，如今一年要撒好几遍药。 Agrochemical use has doubled in ten years.
sceneCN: 这里 agrochemical 是「农用化学品」（第 1 个义项：用于农田的农药与化肥等化学制品）；句意为农用化学品的用量十年间翻了一倍。核心画面是从化工厂搬到田里的那一袋药。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 agro- 的部分，义为「化学品；化学制品」
agro- 的来源词，义为「农业」
agro- 加 chemistry，义为「农业化学」

senses.title: A chemical made for farm use
senses.definition: a manufactured chemical used on farmland, such as a pesticide, herbicide or fertiliser, to protect or feed crops
senses.definitionCN: 用于农田的人造化学制品，如杀虫剂、除草剂或肥料，用来保护或供养作物
senses.example: The co-op buys agrochemicals in bulk before planting.
senses.exampleCN: 合作社在播种前批量采购农用化学品。
senses.why: Agro- means field and chemical means a substance made by chemistry, so the word simply names chemistry carried out into the fields.
senses.whyCN: agro- 表示田地，chemical 表示化学制成的物质，所以这个词就是「把化学带到田里去」的东西。

senses.title: The farm chemical industry
senses.definition: the sector that produces and sells these substances, used as a mass noun in business and policy writing
senses.definitionCN: 生产与销售这些物质的行业，在商业与政策文本中作总称名词使用
senses.example: The agrochemical sector is dominated by a few global firms.
senses.exampleCN: 农化行业由少数几家全球企业主导。
senses.why: Here the same word shifts from counting bottles to naming the whole trade, exactly as pharmaceutical does in medicine.
senses.whyCN: 这里同一个词从「数瓶子」变成「指整个行业」，正如 pharmaceutical 在医药领域的用法。

intro.en: Agrochemical is a modern compound: the Greek agros, field, joined to chemical, which itself traces back to the old word for the art of metals and drugs.
intro.cn: agrochemical 是一个现代复合词：希腊语 agros「田地」加上 chemical，而 chemical 本身可追溯到表示金属与药物技艺的古老词。

items.en: Greek agros meant a field or open country, the same root that gives agriculture and agrarian.
items.cn: 希腊语 agros 意为田地或旷野，与 agriculture、agrarian 同根。

items.en: Latin ager carried the same meaning, and its stem agr- is what English borrowed as agro-.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ager 意义相同，其词干 agr- 正是英语借作 agro- 的形式。

items.en: Arabic al-kimiya named the art of transmuting substances, and reached Europe through medieval Latin.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 指物质转化的技艺，经中世纪拉丁语传入欧洲。

items.en: Scholarly Latin chemicus described someone practising that art, giving English chemical and chemistry.
items.cn: 学术拉丁语 chemicus 指从事该技艺的人，为英语提供 chemical 与 chemistry。

items.en: English joined agro- to chemical in the twentieth century, as industrial farming began to depend on manufactured inputs.
items.cn: 英语在二十世纪把 agro- 与 chemical 拼合，当时工业化农业开始依赖人造投入品。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the agro- and chem- pieces; the near-meaning group lists the specific products this word covers.
note.cn: 形近组保留 agro- 与 chem- 构件；近义组列出该词涵盖的具体产品。

entries.definition: The practice of farming crops and animals.
entries.definitionCN: 种植作物与饲养动物的生产活动。

entries.definition: Relating to land, farming or country life.
entries.definitionCN: 与土地、农耕或乡村生活有关的。

entries.definition: The science of substances and their reactions.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质及其反应的科学。

entries.definition: Relating to the chemistry of living things.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物体化学过程有关的。

entries.definition: A substance used to kill pests.
entries.definitionCN: 用来杀灭害虫的物质。

entries.definition: A substance used to kill unwanted plants.
entries.definitionCN: 用来杀灭杂草的物质。

entries.definition: A substance added to soil to help crops grow.
entries.definitionCN: 施入土壤帮助作物生长的物质。

entries.definition: A substance used to destroy fungi.
entries.definitionCN: 用来杀灭真菌的物质。

normalIntro.en: Agrochemical is agro, field, plus chemical: a chemical that works in the field.
normalIntro.cn: agrochemical 就是 agro「田地」加 chemical「化学品」：在田里干活的化学品。

normal.en: Agro- always points at farmland: agriculture, agrarian and agrochemical all start in the fields.
normal.cn: agro- 永远指向农田：agriculture、agrarian、agrochemical 都从田里出发。

normal.en: The word is countable when you mean a product, so say three agrochemicals.
normal.cn: 指具体产品时可数，所以说 three agrochemicals。

normal.en: It is uncountable when you mean the industry, so say the agrochemical sector.
normal.cn: 指行业时不可数，所以说 the agrochemical sector。

normal.en: Pesticide, herbicide and fertiliser are all kinds of agrochemical, not rivals to it.
normal.cn: pesticide、herbicide、fertiliser 都是 agrochemical 的种类，不是它的对立词。

normal.en: Stress falls on chem: agro-CHEM-ical, the same pattern as biochemical.
normal.cn: 重音落在 chem 上：agro-CHEM-ical，与 biochemical 的重音模式相同。

abstract.en: Picture a factory chimney standing at the edge of a rice paddy.
abstract.cn: 想象一根工厂烟囱立在稻田边上。

abstract.en: Imagine a sack labelled with a chemistry formula instead of a grain name.
abstract.cn: 想象一只麻袋，标签上写的是化学式而不是谷物名。

abstract.en: Think of rain washing a field medicine into the river below.
abstract.cn: 想象雨水把田里的药冲进下面的河。

examples.en: Runoff carries agrochemicals into the streams after heavy rain.
examples.cn: 大雨之后，径流把农用化学品带进溪流。

examples.en: The farm cut its agrochemical bill by rotating crops.
examples.cn: 这家农场通过轮作削减了农化开支。

examples.en: Agrochemical residues were found on a third of the samples.
examples.cn: 三分之一的样品检出了农化残留。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿格罗凯米扣」——阿格罗（agro）是田，凯米扣（chemical）是化学药：田里用的化学药，就是农用化学品。

root: 希腊语 agros「田地」经拉丁语 ager（词干 agr-）形成组合前缀 agro-，与源自阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 的 chemical 拼合，二十世纪构成 agrochemical，字面即「田地里用的化学品」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses name the same substances: one counts the products a farmer buys, the other names the industry that makes them, and neither leaves the field.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项指的是同一批物质：一个数农民买的产品，一个指生产这些产品的行业，两者都没有离开田地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: factory chemistry carried into the field
core.cn: 核心意象：把工厂里的化学搬进田里

branches.en: A spray that kills insects on the leaf.
branches.cn: 喷在叶面上杀虫的药剂。

branches.en: A granule that feeds the root.
branches.cn: 给根部供肥的颗粒。

branches.en: A handful of firms supplying whole regions.
branches.cn: 少数几家企业供应整个地区。

branches.en: Policy debates about farm inputs.
branches.cn: 关于农业投入品的政策争论。

branches.en: Both start with chemistry applied to land.
branches.cn: 两者都始于把化学用于土地。

intro.en: Agrochemical joins two productive pieces: agro- fixes the place, the field, and chemical fixes the kind of substance.
intro.cn: agrochemical 拼合了两个能产构件：agro- 确定地点「田地」，chemical 确定物质类别。

latinIntro.en: The field half is Latin ager with stem agr-; the chemical half reached Latin from Arabic al-kimiya.
latinIntro.cn: 「田地」这一半是拉丁语 ager，词干 agr-；「化学」这一半经阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 进入拉丁语。

latinEntries.exampleCN: ager 提供词干 agr-。
属格 agri 解释了 agriculture 的拼写。
chemicus 是 chemical 的来源。

definition_zh: 富裕；富足；（人、货物或水的）大量涌入
definition_en: the state of having a great deal of money and material comfort; in older use, an abundant inward flow of people, goods or water
core_image: 财富像水一样不断流进来
scene: 这条街十年前只有几家小店，如今橱窗一间接一间亮起来。 Affluence has reshaped the whole neighbourhood.
sceneCN: 这里 affluence 是「富裕」（第 1 个义项：财富充裕、生活舒适的状态）；句意为富裕改变了整个街区的面貌。核心画面是财富像水一样不断流进来。

forms.label: 不可数名词，无复数形式

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ence 换 -ent 的形容词，义为「富裕的；富足的」
affluent 加 -ly，义为「富足地；充裕地」
同根名词，义为「（人、物的）流入；汇集」

senses.title: A state of having plenty of money
senses.definition: the condition of having a great deal of money, property and material comfort
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大量金钱、财产与物质享受的状态
senses.example: Two decades of growth brought affluence to the coastal towns.
senses.exampleCN: 二十年的增长让沿海城镇富裕起来。
senses.why: Ad- means toward and fluere means to flow, so affluence is literally a flowing-toward: wealth keeps arriving instead of sitting still.
senses.whyCN: ad- 表示「朝向」，fluere 表示「流动」，所以 affluence 字面就是「朝……流来」：财富不断涌来，而不是静止不动。

senses.title: A large inward flow of people or things
senses.definition: an abundant incoming stream of people, goods or water, the older and more literal sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 人、货物或水大量流入的情形，是该词更古老、更字面的用法
senses.example: The affluence of visitors strained the little station.
senses.exampleCN: 游客的大量涌入让这个小车站不堪重负。
senses.why: This keeps the original river image intact: the word first described water flowing in, and money later borrowed that picture.
senses.whyCN: 这里保留了最初的河流意象：该词最早描述水的流入，后来金钱借用了这幅画面。

intro.en: Affluence is a river word that became a money word: Latin ad-, toward, plus fluere, to flow, gives a flowing-in, and English used it of water long before it used it of wealth.
intro.cn: affluence 是一个从河流变成金钱的词：拉丁语 ad-「朝向」加 fluere「流动」构成「流入」，英语先用于水，很久以后才用于财富。

items.en: Latin ad meant to or toward, and it assimilates to af- before an f, which is why the word is spelled with a double f.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ad 意为「向、朝」，在 f 前同化为 af-，这正是该词拼作双写 f 的原因。

items.en: Latin fluere meant to flow, the root behind fluent, fluid, influence and flush.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fluere 意为「流动」，是 fluent、fluid、influence 与 flush 背后的词根。

items.en: Combining the two gave affluere, to flow toward, used of rivers running into a larger body of water.
items.cn: 两者结合得到 affluere「朝……流来」，用于描述河流汇入更大的水体。

items.en: The noun affluentia named abundance and a plentiful inflow, already carrying the sense of plenty.
items.cn: 名词 affluentia 表示丰裕与大量流入，已经带有「充足」的意味。

items.en: Old French affluence kept both the flow and the abundance senses, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 affluence 同时保留「流动」与「丰裕」两义，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: By the twentieth century English affluence meant chiefly material wealth, and the phrase the affluent society made that meaning dominant.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，英语 affluence 主要指物质财富，the affluent society 这一说法让该义成为主流。

note.en: The look-alike group stays inside the flu- family of flowing; the near-meaning group lists other words for having plenty of money.
note.cn: 形近组留在表示「流动」的 flu- 词族内；近义组列出其他表示「有钱」的词。

entries.definition: Having a great deal of money and a comfortable standard of living.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有大量金钱与舒适生活水平的。

entries.definition: The power to shape what someone thinks or does.
entries.definitionCN: 影响他人想法或行为的力量。

entries.definition: The place where two rivers join and flow together.
entries.definitionCN: 两条河流汇合之处。

entries.definition: Liquid waste flowing out of a factory or works.
entries.definitionCN: 从工厂流出的液体废物。

entries.definition: A large amount of money and valuable possessions.
entries.definitionCN: 大量金钱与贵重财产。

entries.definition: The state of being successful, especially in making money.
entries.definitionCN: 成功兴旺的状态，尤指赚钱方面。

entries.definition: Great wealth shown off through expensive surroundings.
entries.definitionCN: 通过奢华环境显示出来的巨大财富。

entries.definition: A quantity that is more than enough.
entries.definitionCN: 多得用不完的数量。

normalIntro.en: Affluence is af-, toward, plus flu, flow, plus -ence, a state: the state of wealth flowing toward you.
normalIntro.cn: affluence 就是 af-「朝向」加 flu「流」加 -ence「状态」：财富朝你流来的状态。

normal.en: Flu means flow, so affluent, influence and confluence all keep something moving.
normal.cn: flu 表示流动，所以 affluent、influence、confluence 都让某物保持流动。

normal.en: The double f is ad- turning into af- before fluere, the same change as in afford and afflict.
normal.cn: 双写 f 是 ad- 在 fluere 前变成 af-，与 afford、afflict 中的变化相同。

normal.en: Money that flows in is affluence; money that flows out is expenditure.
normal.cn: 流进来的钱是 affluence，流出去的钱是 expenditure。

normal.en: -ence marks a state, as in silence and presence, so affluence is the state of flowing in.
normal.cn: -ence 表示状态，如 silence、presence，所以 affluence 就是「流入」的状态。

normal.en: Affluence is usually uncountable, so write growing affluence, not an affluence.
normal.cn: affluence 通常不可数，所以写 growing affluence，不写 an affluence。

abstract.en: Picture a river of coins running downhill into your courtyard and never stopping.
abstract.cn: 想象一条硬币的河顺坡流进你的院子，从不停下。

abstract.en: Imagine a tide that comes in but never goes out, leaving the shore deep in goods.
abstract.cn: 想象一道只涨不退的潮，把岸边堆满货物。

abstract.en: Think of a reservoir whose inflow pipe is wider than its outlet.
abstract.cn: 想象一座水库，进水管比出水管还粗。

examples.en: The report links rising affluence to longer life expectancy.
examples.cn: 报告把日益富裕与更长的预期寿命联系起来。

examples.en: Affluence did not reach every village in the valley.
examples.cn: 富裕并未惠及山谷里的每一个村庄。

examples.en: They grew up in affluence but learned to budget carefully.
examples.cn: 他们在富足中长大，却学会了精打细算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿福路恩思」——阿福（af）走的那条路（flu）上恩（ence）泽不断，钱像水一样流进来，就是富裕、富足。

root: 拉丁语前缀 ad-「朝向」在 f 前同化为 af-，加 fluere「流动」构成 affluere「朝……流来」，其名词 affluentia 经古法语 affluence 进入英语，字面即「不断流入的丰裕」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same inflow: the older one counts water and people arriving, the newer one counts money arriving, and in each case plenty keeps coming in.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种流入：较早的义项数的是流来的水与人，较新的义项数的是流来的钱，两者都是丰裕不断涌来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wealth flowing in like water
core.cn: 核心意象：财富像水一样流进来

branches.en: Money arriving year after year.
branches.cn: 金钱年复一年地涌来。

branches.en: Comfort that lasts because the inflow never stops.
branches.cn: 因为流入不停而长久留存的舒适。

branches.en: A crowd pouring into one small place.
branches.cn: 人群涌进一个小地方。

branches.en: Rivers running into a larger stream.
branches.cn: 河流汇入更大的水流。

branches.en: Both measure abundance by how much flows in.
branches.cn: 两者都用流入量来衡量丰裕。

intro.en: Affluence sits in the flu- family, where the root always means flow and the prefix decides which direction the flow takes.
intro.cn: affluence 属于 flu- 词族，词根永远表示流动，前缀决定流动的方向。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad plus fluere gave affluere and the noun affluentia, which French passed on to English almost unchanged.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad 加 fluere 构成 affluere 与名词 affluentia，法语几乎原样把它传给英语。

latinEntries.exampleCN: ad 在 f 前变为 af-。

latinEntries.example: Fluere gives flu- in many English words.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fluere 为许多英语词提供 flu-。

latinEntries.example: Affluere described rivers joining a larger water.
latinEntries.exampleCN: affluere 描述河流汇入更大的水体。

latinEntries.example: Affluentia is the direct source of affluence.
latinEntries.exampleCN: affluentia 是 affluence 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 城市化；城市人口比重上升；城市地域扩张；城市化程度；过度城市化
definition_en: the process by which a population becomes concentrated in cities and the countryside takes on city forms
core_image: 稻田中央竖起塔吊，水泥路把田埂切成整齐的方块，远处楼群一层层往上长
scene: 稻田中央新起了一片楼群，水泥路把田埂切成方块，远处塔吊还在转。 Rapid urbanization swallowed the rice fields within a decade.
sceneCN: 这里 urbanization 指「人口与土地持续向城市集中的过程」（第 1 个义项：乡村人口转为城市人口）；句意为快速城市化在十年内吞掉了这片稻田。可辨识物件：塔吊、楼群、水泥路、田埂。

pos.zh: 城市化；城市化过程与程度（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 urbanus「城市的」→ 由「城市」偏移为「属于城市或城市生活的」
urban + -ize（动词后缀）→ 偏移为「使某地转为城市形态」
urbanize + -ed（形容词化过去分词）→ 偏移为「已经城市化的」
urban + -ism（名词后缀，表体系或倾向）→ 偏移为「城市生活方式与规划理念」
urbanism + -ist（人名词后缀）→ 偏移为「研究或倡导城市生活的人」
sub-（在下、近旁）+ urban → 偏移为「城郊的」
ex-（向外）+ urban → 偏移为「城市远郊的」

senses.title: Movement of people into cities
senses.definition: the process by which people move from the countryside into cities and stay there
senses.definitionCN: 人们从乡村迁入城市并留下来的过程
senses.example: Rapid urbanization swallowed the rice fields within a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 快速城市化在十年内吞掉了这片稻田。
senses.why: urbanus meant 'of the city', and -ization names a process, so the word is literally the process of becoming city-like.
senses.whyCN: urbanus 意为「城市的」，-ization 表过程，因此这个词字面上就是「变成城市样子的过程」。

senses.title: A rising urban share
senses.definition: the increase in the proportion of a population that lives in urban areas
senses.definitionCN: 生活在城市地区的人口所占比例的上升
senses.example: The census recorded urbanization of four points in five years.
senses.exampleCN: 普查记录到五年内城市化率上升了四个百分点。
senses.why: the process can be measured, so the noun also names the number that measures it.
senses.whyCN: 这个过程可以被测量，因此这个名词也指测量它的那个数字。

senses.title: Expansion of built-up land
senses.definition: the spread of built-up land into formerly rural areas
senses.definitionCN: 建成区向原本的乡村地区铺开
senses.example: Urbanization pushed the edge of the city three kilometres outward.
senses.exampleCN: 城市化把城市边缘向外推了三公里。
senses.why: people need land as well as jobs, so population movement shows up on the map as spreading construction.
senses.whyCN: 人既需要工作也需要土地，因此人口迁移在地图上就表现为建筑的铺开。

senses.title: Diffusion of city ways
senses.definition: the spread of city habits, services and expectations into non-city places
senses.definitionCN: 城市习惯、服务与期待扩散到非城市地区
senses.example: Urbanization reached the village as piped water and evening buses.
senses.exampleCN: 城市化以自来水和夜班公交的形式抵达了这个村庄。
senses.why: the word covers ways of living, not only where people sleep, so it can arrive without a skyline.
senses.whyCN: 这个词覆盖的是生活方式，而不只是人睡在哪里，因此它可以在没有高楼天际线时也抵达。

senses.title: Degree of urbanization
senses.definition: how far a place has already become urban, expressed as a level or share
senses.definitionCN: 某地已经城市化的程度，用水平或比例表示
senses.example: Their level of urbanization differs sharply from the coastal provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的城市化程度与沿海省份差别很大。
senses.why: a process that can be measured can also be reported as a level, so the noun doubles as a score.
senses.whyCN: 一个可测量的过程也可以被报告为一个水平，因此这个名词兼作分数。

senses.title: Planning and infrastructure drive
senses.titleCN: 规划与基础设施推动的城市化
senses.definition: deliberate state building of roads, housing and services that turns land urban
senses.definitionCN: 国家有计划地修建道路、住房与服务，使土地转为城市
senses.example: State-led urbanization built the new district before anyone moved in.
senses.exampleCN: 国家主导的城市化在有人入住之前就把新区建好了。
senses.why: the process need not wait for migrants; when the state builds first, the noun names a policy, not a migration.
senses.whyCN: 这个过程不必等移民到来；当国家先建设时，这个名词指的就是政策，而不是迁移。

senses.title: Social change accompanying cities
senses.definition: the social shifts that follow dense living, such as smaller households and new work patterns
senses.definitionCN: 密集居住带来的社会变化，如家庭规模缩小与工作方式改变
senses.example: Urbanization loosened the hold of the extended family.
senses.exampleCN: 城市化松动了大家庭的约束。
senses.why: dense living changes who shares a roof and how work is timed, which is why the social effects take the same name.
senses.whyCN: 密集居住改变了谁与谁同住一个屋顶、工作如何排时间，因此这些社会后果也用同一个名字。

senses.title: Over-urbanization
senses.definition: city growth faster than the jobs, housing and services that could absorb it
senses.definitionCN: 城市增长快于就业、住房与服务的吸纳能力
senses.example: Over-urbanization left rows of unfinished towers beside open drains.
senses.exampleCN: 过度城市化在露天排水沟旁留下了一排排未完工的塔楼。
senses.why: the same process, pushed past the point that jobs and services can absorb, becomes a warning rather than a goal.
senses.whyCN: 同一个过程一旦被推过就业与服务能吸纳的界限，就从一个目标变成一个警示。

intro.en: Urbanization joins urbanus, Latin for 'of the city', to the suffix -ization, which names a process; the word belongs to nineteenth-century social description. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: urbanization 把拉丁语指「城市的」的 urbanus 与表过程的 -ization 组合起来；这个词属于十九世纪的社会描述。年代均为约数。

items.en: Urbs meant 'city', especially Rome. Its deeper origin is uncertain; no accepted Indo-European source has been shown.
items.cn: urbs 意为「城市」，尤指罗马城。其更早来源不确定，没有已获公认的印欧语来源。

items.en: Urbanus meant 'of the city', and carried a secondary tone of city manners, from which English gets both urban and urbane.
items.cn: urbanus 意为「城市的」，并带有「城市举止」的第二层色彩，英语的 urban 与 urbane 都由此而来。

items.en: French urbanisation was coined in the nineteenth century to describe the growth of city populations.
items.cn: 法语 urbanisation 在十九世纪被造出来，用以描述城市人口的增长。

items.en: The suffix -ization goes back to Greek -izein 'to make, to act' through Latin -izare and French -isation; it names a process rather than a state.
items.cn: 后缀 -ization 经拉丁 -izare 与法语 -isation 上溯至希腊 -izein「使、做」；它指过程，而非状态。

items.en: English adopted urbanization in the late nineteenth century, first as a description of population movement and later as a policy field.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪末采纳 urbanization，最初描述人口流动，后来成为一个政策领域。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of urbs before Latin is unsettled and the exact first English citation is unrecorded, so any earlier form proposed for urbs is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 来源不确定：urbs 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，英语首见的确切书证也没有记录，因此为 urbs 提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates urbanization from its own family, which shares the same stem; group two holds related demographic and economic processes.
note.cn: 第一组把 urbanization 与同一词干的自家人分开；第二组是相关的人口与经济过程。

entries.definition: The mode of life and set of values associated with cities; urbanization is the process of arriving at that mode.
entries.definitionCN: 与城市相连的生活方式与价值取向；城市化是抵达这种方式的进程。

entries.definition: To make an area or a population urban; it is the acting verb behind the process noun.
entries.definitionCN: 使某地或某人群城市化；它是这个进程名词背后的动词。

entries.definition: Of or in a city; the adjective describes a state, the noun describes movement into that state.
entries.definitionCN: 城市中的、城市的；形容词描述状态，名词描述进入该状态的过程。

entries.definition: The movement of city populations to the outskirts; it is a later phase of the same process, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 城市人口向郊区移动；它是同一进程的较晚阶段，并非同义词。

entries.definition: Movement away from large cities toward smaller settlements; it reverses the direction, so it cannot replace the term.
entries.definitionCN: 从大城市迁往较小居民点的移动；它反转了方向，因此不能替代本条术语。

entries.definition: Movement from one place to another; it is the general term, of which the rural-to-city flow is one case.
entries.definitionCN: 从一个地方到另一个地方的移动；它是一般术语，乡到城的流动只是其中一种情形。

entries.definition: The growth of factory production; it often drives urbanization but is a different process with a different measure.
entries.definitionCN: 工厂生产的增长；它常推动城市化，却是另一种进程，衡量方式也不同。

entries.definition: Broad adoption of modern technology and institutions; it is wider than urbanization and need not be urban.
entries.definitionCN: 对现代技术与制度的广泛采纳；比城市化更宽，也不必是城市的。

entries.definition: The spread of low-density development over open land; it is one physical result of urbanization, often criticized.
entries.definitionCN: 低密度开发在空地上的铺开；它是城市化的一个物理结果，常受批评。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin stem, the real process suffix and the real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词干、真实的过程后缀与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: urbs 'city' gives urban; add -ization and you get the process of becoming city.
normal.cn: urbs「城市」给出 urban；加上 -ization 就得到「变成城市」的过程。

normal.en: The family runs urban, urbanize, urbanized, urbanism, urbanist, suburban, exurban.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 urban、urbanize、urbanized、urbanism、urbanist、suburban、exurban。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the measured sense: urbanization rate, rapid urbanization, counter-urbanization.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出可测量的义项：城市化率、快速城市化、逆城市化。

normal.en: Latin had both urbanus 'of the city' and the sharper urbane 'city-mannered'; English kept the pair.
normal.cn: 拉丁语既有 urbanus「城市的」，也有更偏「城市举止」的 urbane；英语把这一对都留下了。

normal.en: -ization names a process in hundreds of words: industrialization, modernization, globalization.
normal.cn: -ization 在成百上千的词里表过程：工业化、现代化、全球化。

abstract.en: Picture a field where the footpaths are slowly replaced by kerbs without anyone deciding the whole plan.
abstract.cn: 想象一片田野，小路一点点被路缘石取代，却没有人定下整体规划。

abstract.en: Picture a village clock that begins to keep city hours.
abstract.cn: 想象一只村庄的钟，开始按城市的时间走。

abstract.en: Picture a map where the grey area grows like water spreading across paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，灰色区域像水在纸上蔓延一样扩大。

examples.en: Urbanization without sewers turns a growing city into a health crisis.
examples.cn: 没有下水道的城市化会把一座成长中的城市变成一场卫生危机。

examples.en: The country reached an urbanization rate of seventy per cent in one generation.
examples.cn: 这个国家在一代人之内达到七成的城市化率。

examples.en: Historians treat nineteenth-century urbanization as a rupture in everyday life.
examples.cn: 历史学者把十九世纪的城市化视为日常生活的一次断裂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「urban（城市的）+ ize（使成为）+ ation（过程）」——使地方变成城市的那一过程 → 城市化

root: 拉丁 urbs「城市」→ urbanus「城市的」+ -ization（经拉丁 -izare、希腊 -izein「使、做」，表过程）；urbs 更早来源不确定。英语 urbanization 为十九世纪社会描述用语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process: people move into cities, the measured share rises, built land spreads, city habits diffuse, a level is reached, the state builds, society reshapes, and growth can outrun what supports it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个进程展开：人迁入城市，可测的比重上升，建成区铺开，城市习惯扩散，达到某个水平，国家主动建设，社会随之变形，最后增长可以超出支撑能力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grey built-up area spreading across a map that was green only a generation ago.
core.cn: 核心意象：灰色的建成区在一张上一代人还是绿色的地图上蔓延。

branches.en: MOVEMENT AND MEASURE: the flow of people, and the percentage that records it.
branches.cn: 流动与度量：人的迁移，以及记录这一迁移的百分比。

branches.en: LAND AND SOCIETY: building spreads over fields, and dense living redraws households and work.
branches.cn: 土地与社会：建筑铺过田野，密集居住重画了家庭与工作。

branches.en: DIFFUSION AND LEVEL: city ways travel beyond the skyline, and the whole can be rated by how far it has gone.
branches.cn: 扩散与水平：城市方式越过天际线传播，整体也可按进展程度评级。

branches.en: DELIBERATE BUILDING: the state lays roads and housing first and waits for residents.
branches.cn: 有意的建设：国家先铺路建房，再等居民到来。

branches.en: GROWTH TOO FAST: when jobs and services lag, the same process produces overcrowding rather than opportunity.
branches.cn: 过快的增长：当就业与服务跟不上，同一进程产出的是拥挤，而非机会。

intro.en: Urbanization is a Latin stem plus a process suffix, and both parts build long families in English.
intro.cn: urbanization 是一个拉丁词干加一个表过程的后缀，两部分在英语里都建起了很长的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin urbs and urbanus supply the stem; -ization reaches Latin through -izare and Greek -izein.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 urbs 与 urbanus 提供词干；-ization 经拉丁 -izare 与希腊 -izein 上溯。

items.example: The Latin noun named the city as a walled place.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词把城市指为有城墙的地方。

items.example: The adjective described both place and manner.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词既描述地点，也描述举止。

items.example: The suffix turns a quality into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把性质变成动作。

items.example: The suffix names the whole process, not one act.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀指整个过程，而非单个动作。
城市学校面对不同的压力。

items.structure: urbanus, with the manner sense kept
items.example: His urbane reply avoided the question.
items.exampleCN: 他文雅的回答避开了那个问题。
铁路使这个山谷城市化了。

items.example: The urbanized strip follows the motorway.
items.exampleCN: 城市化的地带沿着高速公路展开。
城市生活方式改变了邻里的相遇方式。

items.meaning: one who studies or advocates city life
items.meaningCN: 研究或倡导城市生活的人
items.example: The urbanist argued for narrower streets.
items.exampleCN: 这位城市研究者主张把街道弄窄。

items.example: The prefix places the suburb just outside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把郊区放在城的近外。

items.example: The prefix pushes development beyond the edge.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把开发推到边缘之外。

definition_zh: 突变；使突变；改变形态；（语言学）发生元音换音
definition_en: to undergo or cause a genetic change, or more generally to change form or character
core_image: 病毒在宿主里复制出新的版本，外壳上的标记一次比一次略有不同
scene: 病毒在宿主里不断复制，每隔几代就出现新的版本。 Viruses mutate quickly enough to escape older vaccines.
sceneCN: 这里 mutate 指「发生遗传突变」（第 1 个义项：遗传物质发生改变）；句意为病毒突变得足够快，能逃过较旧的疫苗。可辨识物件：病毒示意球、宿主细胞、复制箭头、新旧外壳标记。

senses.title: Undergo a genetic change
senses.definition: to undergo a change in genetic material
senses.definitionCN: 遗传物质发生改变
senses.example: Viruses mutate quickly enough to escape older vaccines.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒突变得足够快，能逃过较旧的疫苗。
senses.why: The core sense is intransitive: the material changes itself, and no outside agent is named.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是不及物的：物质自身发生改变，不点明外部施事者。

senses.title: Cause a genetic change
senses.definition: to induce or create a change in genetic material
senses.definitionCN: 诱发或造成遗传物质的改变
senses.example: Researchers mutate one base to test its function.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者使一个碱基突变，以检验其功能。
senses.why: The transitive use adds an experimenter: the change is made on purpose, often one site at a time.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法加上实验者：改变是有意作出的，常常一次一个位点。

senses.title: Change form or appearance
senses.definition: to change in form, often gradually or beyond recognition
senses.definitionCN: 形态发生改变，常为逐渐或面目全非
senses.example: The story mutated with every retelling.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事每复述一次就变一次。
senses.why: The general sense treats form like sequence: small substitutions accumulate until the thing is recognizably different.
senses.whyCN: 一般义把形态当作序列：小的替换累积起来，直到事物明显不同。

senses.title: Change into something else
senses.definition: to develop into a different kind of thing
senses.definitionCN: 发展成另一种事物
senses.example: The protest mutated into a national movement.
senses.exampleCN: 这场抗议演变成全国性运动。
senses.why: With into, the verb names a threshold: what began as one thing now counts as another.
senses.whyCN: 与 into 连用时，这个动词命名一个门槛：起初是一回事，如今算作另一回事。

senses.title: Undergo vowel mutation
senses.definition: in historical linguistics, to change a vowel under the influence of a following sound
senses.definitionCN: 在历史语言学中，指元音在后接音影响下改变
senses.example: Old English mutated the vowel before a high front vowel.
senses.exampleCN: 古英语在高前元音前使元音发生换音。
senses.why: Philology used the verb for sound change before biology borrowed it, and the linguistic sense remains technical.
senses.whyCN: 语文学在生物学借用之前就用这个动词指语音变化，语言学义至今仍是技术性的。

senses.title: Mutate a pathogen deliberately
senses.definition: to alter a pathogen in the laboratory, often to weaken it
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室中改变病原体，常为削弱它
senses.example: Scientists mutate a strain to weaken it for a vaccine.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家使一个毒株突变，以削弱它用于疫苗。
senses.why: This sense is closer to engineering than to accident: the change is directed toward a goal.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项更接近工程而非偶然：改变被导向一个目标。

senses.title: Mutate rapidly or slowly
senses.definition: to change at a particular rate under given conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在特定条件下以某种速率改变
senses.example: These bacteria mutate faster under antibiotic pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 这些细菌在抗生素压力下突变得更快。
senses.why: Rate adverbs turn the verb into a measurable process, which is how mutation becomes a parameter.
senses.whyCN: 速率副词把这个动词变成可测量的过程，突变由此成为参数。

senses.title: Transform a plan or idea
senses.definition: to change a plan, idea or institution until it differs greatly from the original
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、观念或制度改变到与原初大不相同
senses.example: The plan mutated beyond recognition after the review.
senses.exampleCN: 计划在评审之后变得面目全非。
senses.why: The figurative use carries a warning: change without a clear limit can destroy the original purpose.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法带有警示：没有明确界限的改变可能毁掉原初目的。

intro.en: Mutate comes from Latin mutare 'to change'; English may have formed it from the past participle mutatus or as a back-formation from mutation, and both routes are hypotheses. It is first recorded in 1818 for general change, long before genetics.
intro.cn: mutate 来自拉丁 mutare「改变」；英语可能由过去分词 mutatus 构成，也可能是从 mutation 逆构，两条路径都属假说。这个词在 1818 年首次记录为一般变化义，远早于遗传学。

items.en: Mutare 'to change' is the source of mutation, mutable and mutate. Its deeper origin is not established beyond Latin, so any pre-Latin root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: mutare「改变」是 mutation、mutable 与 mutate 的来源。它在拉丁语之外的更深来源未得到确证，因此任何拉丁语之前的词根均属重构。

items.en: The past participle mutatus 'changed' supplied the stem behind the English verb pattern in -ate.
items.cn: 过去分词 mutatus「已改变的」提供了英语 -ate 动词模式背后的词干。

items.en: Mutate appeared in English in 1818 meaning 'to change'; the exact sense development is not fully documented, and the relationship to Latin mutatus is a hypothesis.
items.cn: mutate 在 1818 年以「改变」义出现在英语中；义项发展并无完整文献，且它与拉丁 mutatus 的关系属于假说。

items.en: The genetic sense is recorded from 1913 and twentieth-century genetics made 'undergo mutation' the dominant sense, first of organisms and later of viruses and cells.
items.cn: 遗传义从 1913 年起有记录；20 世纪的遗传学使「发生突变」成为主导义，先用于生物体，后用于病毒与细胞。

items.en: Philologists used mutate for vowel change before the biological sense spread, and the sense survives in historical grammar.
items.cn: 在生物学义传播之前，语文学家已用 mutate 指元音变化，这一义在历史语法中存留。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin and sense dates): mutare has no established deeper etymology, and the dates of the biological and linguistic senses are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（拉丁语之前词源与义项年代）：mutare 没有已确立的更深词源，生物学义与语言学义的年代都只是约数。

note.en: Group one separates mutate from its family and from a near sound-alike; group two separates it from verbs of changing and transforming.
note.cn: 第一组把 mutate 与其词族及一个音近词分开；第二组把它与「改变」「转变」类动词区分。

entries.definition: The change or the process; mutate is the act of undergoing or causing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指改变或过程；mutate 是发生或导致改变的动作。

entries.definition: An organism carrying a change; it names the result rather than the process.
entries.definitionCN: 携带改变的生物体；命名结果而非过程。

entries.definition: Able to change; the adjective describes a possibility, not an event.
entries.definitionCN: 能够改变；形容词描述可能性，而非事件。

entries.definition: From Latin mutus 'silent', not mutare: unable or unwilling to speak. The resemblance is only in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 mutus「沉默的」，并非 mutare：指不能或不愿说话。相似仅在读音。

entries.definition: The broad everyday verb; mutate is narrower and often implies form or sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 宽泛的日常动词；mutate 更窄，常暗示形态或序列。

entries.definition: To make a partial change, often deliberate; mutate can be unintended and can go further.
entries.definitionCN: 作部分改变，常为有意；mutate 可以无意，且程度可能更深。

entries.definition: To change form completely; mutate stresses repeated or gradual change, especially of sequences.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底改变形态；mutate 强调反复或逐渐的改变，尤指序列。

entries.definition: To develop gradually, especially by selection; mutate names the origin of variation, not the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐发展，尤经选择；mutate 命名变异来源，而非整个过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mutare 'to change' + -ate: to make or become changed.
normal.cn: mutare「改变」+ -ate：使改变或发生改变。

normal.en: The family runs mutate, mutation, mutant and mutable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mutate、mutation、mutant 与 mutable。

normal.en: Viruses mutate; researchers mutate a site; stories mutate in retelling.
normal.cn: 病毒会突变；研究者使位点突变；故事在复述中变形。

normal.en: Mutation is the noun; mutant is the carrier.
normal.cn: mutation 是名词；mutant 是携带者。

normal.en: Linguistic mutate refers to vowel change, an older sense.
normal.cn: 语言学中的 mutate 指元音换音，是更早的义项。

abstract.en: Picture a photocopier that never makes an exact copy.
abstract.cn: 想象一台永远不能完全准确复印的复印机。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour growing a new detail at every retelling.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻每复述一次就长出一个新细节。

abstract.en: Picture a path worn wider by feet until it becomes a road.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被踩得越来越宽、最终变成道路的小径。

examples.en: The virus mutates slowly enough for the vaccine to remain useful.
examples.cn: 这种病毒突变够慢，疫苗仍能发挥作用。

examples.en: The team mutated the binding site to see what changed.
examples.cn: 团队使结合位点突变，观察发生了什么变化。

examples.en: The old ceremony mutated into a street festival.
examples.cn: 这个古老仪式演变成了街头节日。

dict_mnemonic.text: mut（改变）+ ate（动词尾）——使改变 → 突变；名词是 mutation。

root: 拉丁 mutare「改变」← 过去分词 mutatus；mutare 在拉丁语之外的更深来源不确定，相关原始印欧语词根均属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a changing copy: genetic change, induced change, changed form, change into another kind, vowel shift, weakened pathogen, measurable rate and a transformed plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一份不断改变的副本展开：遗传改变、诱发改变、形态改变、变成另一类、元音换音、被削弱的病原体、可测速率与变形的计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a virus copying itself, each shell slightly different from the last.
core.cn: 核心意象：病毒不断复制自身，外壳一次比一次略有不同。

branches.en: GENETIC CHANGE AT A RATE: the material changes itself, fast or slow.
branches.cn: 以某速率发生的遗传改变：物质自身改变，可快可慢。

branches.en: INDUCED CHANGE: an experimenter or vaccine maker directs the change.
branches.cn: 诱发改变：实验者或疫苗制作者引导改变。

branches.en: FORM AND THRESHOLD: appearance shifts, and a thing becomes another kind.
branches.cn: 形态与门槛：外观移动，事物成为另一类。

branches.en: VOWEL SHIFT: historical grammar uses the verb for sound change.
branches.cn: 元音换音：历史语法用这个动词指语音变化。

branches.en: BEYOND RECOGNITION: a plan or idea changes until its purpose is lost.
branches.cn: 面目全非：计划或观念改变到失去原初目的。

intro.en: Mutate is a Latin verb whose stem also builds the noun, the carrier and the adjective; prefixes extend the same root to exchange and unchangeability.
intro.cn: mutate 是拉丁动词，其词干还构成名词、携带者与形容词；前缀把同一词根扩展到「交换」与「不可变」。

latinIntro.en: Latin mutare gives mutate, mutation, mutant and mutable; com- builds commutation, in- builds immutable, trans- builds transmutation. All share the changing root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mutare 衍生 mutate、mutation、mutant 与 mutable；com- 构成 commutation，in- 构成 immutable，trans- 构成 transmutation。它们共享「改变」词根。

items.example: The root names the act of changing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名改变的动作。

items.example: The participle supplied the verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供了动词词干。

items.example: The suffix forms a verb from the stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀从词干构成动词。

items.example: The old dream was to transmute lead into gold.
items.exampleCN: 古老的梦想是把铅变成金。
