definition_zh: 尊重；敬重；好评；认为；视为
definition_en: to respect and value someone or something highly, or a feeling of high respect
core_image: 双手接过一件旧物，郑重地把它放到最高一层
scene: 毕业多年后，学生回到母校，把一本旧词典送还给老师。 Years later, the student still holds the old teacher in high esteem.
sceneCN: 这里 esteem 是「尊重、敬重」（第 1 个义项：对某人怀有很深的敬意）；句意：多年以后，这名学生依然非常敬重这位老师。

derivatives.zh: esteem 加后缀 -able 构成，值得敬重的；可敬的
由拉丁语 aestimatio 而来，判断；评价；估计
self 加 esteem 构成的复合词，自尊；自尊心

senses.title: High respect
senses.definition: a feeling of deep respect and approval for someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人怀有的深切敬意与认可
senses.example: The old coach is held in great esteem by his players.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老教练深受队员们的敬重。
senses.why: The Latin verb aestimare means to fix a value, so esteeming a person is setting a high value on that person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 aestimare 意为「估定价值」，所以敬重一个人就是给这个人定下很高的价值。

senses.title: Good opinion, standing
senses.definition: the good opinion that other people have of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 他人对某人或某物持有的好评与看重
senses.example: The school has risen in public esteem over the past decade.
senses.exampleCN: 过去十年间，这所学校在公众中的声誉提高了。
senses.why: Once a value has been assigned, the word can name the standing a person enjoys in the eyes of others.
senses.whyCN: 价值一经评定，这个词就转而指一个人在他人眼中的地位与声望。

senses.title: To regard as
senses.definition: to consider or judge something to be a particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 把某事看作或判定为某种性质
senses.example: I esteem it a privilege to speak at this ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 我认为能在这场典礼上发言是一种荣幸。
senses.why: The old appraisal sense survives in the pattern esteem something as something, where the mind assigns a value or a label.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「估价」义保留在「esteem 某物为某物」的句式中：头脑给事物贴上价值或名目的标签。

senses.title: To appraise, to value
senses.definition: to judge the worth or amount of something, an older use
senses.definitionCN: 判断某物的价值或数量，属于较古的用法
senses.example: In old ledgers the land was esteemed at a modest sum.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧账簿里，这块地被估为一个不大的数目。
senses.why: This is the original Latin sense of aestimare, a plain valuation, before the word narrowed to respect.
senses.whyCN: 这正是拉丁语 aestimare 的本义，平实的估价；后来词义才收窄为尊重。

intro.en: Esteem goes back to Latin aestimare, to value or appraise, through Old French estimer.
intro.cn: esteem 可追溯到拉丁语 aestimare（估价、评定价值），经古法语 estimer 进入英语。

items.en: Aestimare means to value or to appraise something.
items.cn: aestimare 意为给某物估价、评定价值。

items.en: Aestimatio names the act of valuation and the value set.
items.cn: aestimatio 指估价这一行为以及被定下的价值。

items.en: Estimer carries the verb into French with the sense of holding in regard.
items.cn: estimer 把动词带入法语，并带上「看重」的含义。

items.en: Estemen appears in English for valuing and for respecting.
items.cn: 中古英语 estemen 出现，兼有估价与尊重两义。

items.en: Modern English keeps esteem mainly as respect, while estimate takes over the counting sense.
items.cn: 现代英语里 esteem 主要保留尊重，而 estimate 接过了计量估价之义。

note.en: Esteem sits inside the Latin value family and beside the everyday words for respect.
note.cn: esteem 与拉丁语「估价」词族相连，也与日常表示尊重的词相邻。

entries.definition: worthy of respect
entries.definitionCN: 值得敬重的；可敬的

entries.definition: a judgement or opinion of value
entries.definitionCN: 判断；评价；估计

entries.definition: respect for oneself
entries.definitionCN: 自尊；自尊心

entries.definition: a feeling of admiration for someone
entries.definitionCN: 尊敬；敬意

entries.definition: attention or respect for someone
entries.definitionCN: 尊重；关注

entries.definition: a feeling of great approval
entries.definitionCN: 钦佩；赞赏

normalIntro.en: Esteem is a scale in the mind: a person is weighed and found valuable.
normalIntro.cn: esteem 是心里的一杆秤：把人称过之后，认定其价值很高。

normal.en: To hold someone in high esteem is to respect that person deeply.
normal.cn: hold someone in high esteem 就是深深敬重某人。

normal.en: Self-esteem is the value you place on yourself.
normal.cn: self-esteem 是你给自己定下的价值。

normal.en: A mark of esteem is a sign that others value you.
normal.cn: a mark of esteem 是别人看重你的表示。

normal.en: Esteem and estimate share one Latin root but have drifted apart.
normal.cn: esteem 与 estimate 同出一个拉丁词根，后来分道扬镳。

normal.en: The phrase esteem it a privilege keeps the old sense of judging something to be valuable.
normal.cn: esteem it a privilege 这个说法保留了「判定某物有价值」的古义。

abstract.en: Picture both hands receiving an old book and placing it on the top shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象双手接过一本旧书，把它放到书架最高一层。（对应第 1 个义项：把人放在心里的高处，就是敬重）

abstract.en: Imagine a name rising on a public list as neighbours nod in approval.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字在众人名单上往上走，邻居们纷纷点头称许。（对应第 2 个义项：声望就是别人眼中的位置）

abstract.en: Picture a judge setting a high price on a small object and calling it precious.
abstract.cn: 想象鉴定人给一件小物件定下高价，称它珍贵。（对应第 3 个义项：认为、视为就是给事物定名分）

examples.en: The students hold their teacher in high esteem.
examples.cn: 学生们非常敬重他们的老师。

examples.en: Her self-esteem grew after she finished the course.
examples.cn: 完成课程后，她的自尊心增强了。

examples.en: The village esteemed him as a fair judge.
examples.cn: 村里人把他视为公正的裁判。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一斯汀」——记成「一心一意把对方当尊长」，于是有敬重之意；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aestimare（估价、评定价值）→ aestimatio（评价）→ 古法语 estimer → 中古英语 estemen → 英语 esteem，核心义「给某人定下很高的价值」。

sensesIntro.en: Esteem starts as a valuation, becomes the respect a person commands, and keeps a formal verb sense of regarding something as valuable.
sensesIntro.cn: esteem 从估价出发，转为一个人赢得的敬重与声望，并保留「认为某物有价值」的正式动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of hands weighing something and setting it high.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手把某物掂量之后，放到高处。

branches.en: Respect is the value placed on a person.
branches.cn: 敬意是给一个人定下的价值。

branches.en: Public esteem is the standing others grant.
branches.cn: 声誉是他人给予的地位。

branches.en: To esteem as is to judge something to be valuable.
branches.cn: 认为、视为就是判定某物有价值。

branches.en: Both the noun and the verb keep the old valuation image.
branches.cn: 名词与动词都保留着古老的估价意象。

branches.en: A judgement repeated by many people hardens into public standing.
branches.cn: 许多人的判断反复叠加，就固化为公众声望。

intro.en: Esteem belongs to the Latin value family, and English builds estimable, estimation, and self-esteem around it.
intro.cn: esteem 属于拉丁语「估价」词族，英语围绕它构成 estimable、estimation 与 self-esteem。

latinIntro.en: Latin aestimare means to value, and aestimatio means a valuation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aestimare 意为估价，aestimatio 意为估价、评价。

items.example: Aestimare is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: aestimare 是整个词族的源头。

items.example: Aestimatio names the act of valuing.

items.meaning: to value, to hold in regard
items.example: Old French estimer carries both senses.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 estimer 兼有估价与看重两义。

items.example: Esteem keeps the noun sense of respect.
items.exampleCN: esteem 保留表示尊重的名词义。

items.example: The verb esteems a person or a plan.
items.exampleCN: 动词 esteem 可接人或计划作宾语。

items.example: Estimable describes a person worth valuing.
items.exampleCN: estimable 形容值得看重的人。
前缀 self- 构成 self-esteem。

items.example: Self-esteem is the value one places on oneself.
items.exampleCN: self-esteem 是自己给自己定下的价值。

definition_zh: n. 背痛；腰痛（通常为持续性钝痛）
definition_en: A pain in the back, usually a dull and lasting one.
core_image: 直不起腰时后背那条隐隐的痛线
scene: 搬了一整天箱子，他晚上直不起腰。 Lifting boxes all day left him with a bad backache by evening.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：backache 指背部的疼痛，常作不可数名词。

senses.title: Pain in the back
senses.definition: a dull lasting pain anywhere along the back, treated as an uncountable condition
senses.definitionCN: 背部任何位置的持续钝痛，作不可数的身体状况看待
senses.example: She has had backache since the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 她自从那次跌倒后一直背痛。
senses.why: Backache joins back with ache, an old word for continuing pain, so it names a state rather than a sharp blow.
senses.whyCN: backache 由 back 与 ache 组成，ache 是指持续疼痛的旧词，因此它指一种状态而非一次剧痛。

senses.title: A bout of that pain
senses.definition: countably, one spell of such pain, as when a person speaks of recurrent aches
senses.definitionCN: 作可数用法时指一次这样的疼痛发作，如谈到反复发作的疼痛
senses.example: He gets backaches after long drives.
senses.exampleCN: 长途开车后他就会背痛发作。
senses.why: Because the condition returns in spells, speakers began counting the spells, giving the plural.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种状况会一阵阵回来，使用者开始数这些发作，于是有了复数。

intro.en: Backache is back plus ache; back is Old English baec, and ache comes from Old English acan, to ache, a native verb long confused in spelling with the noun.
intro.cn: backache 是 back 加 ache；back 是古英语 baec，ache 出自古英语 acan「疼痛」，这个本族动词的拼写长期与名词相混。

items.en: Old English baec meant the back of a body, the native word still in use.
items.cn: 古英语 baec 意为「身体的背部」，是沿用至今的本族词。

items.en: Old English acan was a verb meaning to give continuing pain.
items.cn: 古英语 acan 是动词，意为「持续作痛」。

items.en: Middle English had the verb ake and the noun ache, with different sounds.
items.cn: 中古英语有动词 ake 与名词 ache，读音不同。

items.en: Dr Johnson fixed the spelling ache for both, following the noun form.
items.cn: 约翰逊博士按名词形式把两者的拼写定为 ache。

items.en: Backache is recorded in the nineteenth century as complaints of work posture grew.
items.cn: 随着劳作姿势引起的病症增多，backache 于十九世纪有记载。

items.en: Today it appears in occupational health as lower back pain of mechanical origin.
items.cn: 今天它出现在职业健康领域，指力学原因引起的下背痛。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the ache compounds; the near-meaning group lists other words for pain in the trunk of the body.
note.cn: 形近组保留 ache 复合词；近义组列出表示躯干疼痛的其他词。

entries.definition: Pain in a tooth.
entries.definitionCN: 牙痛。

entries.definition: Pain in the head.
entries.definitionCN: 头痛。

entries.definition: The spine, or firmness of will.
entries.definitionCN: 脊柱；骨气。

entries.definition: Exhaustingly hard work.
entries.definitionCN: 累断腰的劳作。

entries.definition: Pain in the lower back.
entries.definitionCN: 下背部疼痛。

entries.definition: Difficulty in moving a joint.
entries.definitionCN: 关节活动困难。

entries.definition: Tender pain after effort.
entries.definitionCN: 用力后的酸痛。

entries.definition: Injury from overstretching.
entries.definitionCN: 过度拉伸造成的损伤。

normalIntro.en: Backache is back plus ache: a continuing dull pain along the back, and the plural counts its spells.
normalIntro.cn: backache 是 back 加 ache：沿背部的持续钝痛，复数则数它一次次发作。

normal.en: Usually uncountable: have backache.
normal.cn: 通常不可数：have backache。

normal.en: The plural counts separate spells.
normal.cn: 复数指一次次单独的发作。

normal.en: Lower backache is the commonest kind.
normal.cn: 下背痛是最常见的一种。

normal.en: Ache is dull; pain can be sharp.
normal.cn: ache 是钝痛，pain 可以是剧痛。

normal.en: Toothache and headache follow the pattern.
normal.cn: toothache 与 headache 遵循同一构词。

abstract.en: Picture a line of dull heat along the spine.
abstract.cn: 想象沿脊柱的一条闷热之线。

abstract.en: Imagine standing up only halfway.
abstract.cn: 想象只能直起一半的腰。

abstract.en: Think of a chair that never quite helps.
abstract.cn: 想象一把怎么坐都不解决问题的椅子。

examples.en: Backache kept her from the garden.
examples.cn: 背痛让她没法去花园。

examples.en: A firm mattress eased his backache.
examples.cn: 硬一点的床垫缓解了他的背痛。

examples.en: Repeated backaches forced him to stop lifting.
examples.cn: 反复的背痛发作迫使他不再搬重物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：back「背」+ ache「持续作痛」——背上那条不断的钝痛，就是 backache；同法还有 toothache、headache。

root: 古英语 baec「背」与 acan「持续作痛」合成 backache；ache 的拼写在十八世纪按名词形式统一，十九世纪该复合词随劳作病症增多而通行。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same dull line of pain: the lasting condition, and one spell of it counted separately.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一条钝痛之线：持续的状况，以及被单独计数的一次发作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dull line of pain along the back when you cannot stand straight
core.cn: 核心意象：直不起腰时后背那条隐隐的痛线

branches.en: A back sore after lifting boxes.
branches.cn: 搬箱后作痛的背。

branches.en: Pain lasting since a fall.
branches.cn: 自跌倒后持续的疼痛。

branches.en: Spells brought on by long drives.
branches.cn: 长途开车引发的发作。

branches.en: Repeated bouts that stop the lifting.
branches.cn: 反复到让人不再搬重物的发作。

branches.en: One condition, counted or not.
branches.cn: 同一状况，可计数或不计数。

intro.en: Backache is back plus ache; the same ache ending builds toothache and headache, while -breaking gives backbreaking.
intro.cn: backache 是 back 加 ache；同一 ache 词尾构成 toothache 与 headache，而 -breaking 则给出 backbreaking。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are native; Latin lumbus, loin, gives lumbago and lumbar, and dolor, pain, gives dolorous beside them.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都属本族语；拉丁语 lumbus「腰」产生 lumbago 与 lumbar，dolor「痛」则产生 dolorous。

latinEntries.exampleCN: baec 产生 back。
acan 产生 ache。
lumbus 产生 lumbar。

definition_zh: n. 心绞痛（心肌缺血引起的胸痛）；咽峡炎
definition_en: Chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart muscle; in older medical use, a severe choking sore throat.
core_image: 胸口被一只看不见的手攥住
scene: 他爬到三楼就得停下，胸口发紧。 The doctor diagnosed angina after the stress test.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：爬楼时胸口发紧、休息后缓解，是心肌供血不足引起的心绞痛，医学上称 angina。

senses.title: Chest pain from a short of blood
senses.definition: a squeezing chest pain that appears when the heart muscle does not get enough blood, usually on effort
senses.definitionCN: 心肌供血不足时出现的压榨性胸痛，通常在用力时发作
senses.example: The angina eased once he sat down.
senses.exampleCN: 他一坐下，心绞痛就缓解了。
senses.why: Latin angina meant a choking sore throat, from a root meaning to squeeze; the heart sense keeps the same image of a tightening grip.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 angina 意为「令人窒息的咽痛」，出自意为「挤压」的词根；心脏义保留了同一幅「被攥紧」的画面。

senses.title: The older throat sense
senses.definition: a severe sore throat with swelling that threatens the airway, as in quinsy
senses.definitionCN: 伴肿胀并威胁气道的严重咽痛，如扁桃体周围脓肿
senses.example: The old texts use angina for a strangling throat infection.
senses.exampleCN: 旧文献用 angina 指一种令人窒息的喉部感染。
senses.why: This is the original sense: before cardiology borrowed the word, angina named any condition that felt like being strangled.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义：在心脏病学借用该词之前，angina 指任何感觉像被勒住的病症。

intro.en: Angina is Latin for a choking sore throat, from Greek ankhonē, strangling, from ankhein, to squeeze. Heberden added pectoris, of the chest, in 1768 and the modern heart sense was fixed.
intro.cn: angina 在拉丁语中意为「令人窒息的咽痛」，来自希腊语 ankhonē「勒紧」，后者出自 ankhein「挤压」。赫伯登 1768 年加上 pectoris「胸部的」，现代心脏义由此确定。

items.en: Greek ankhonē meant strangling or a strangling, from ankhein, to squeeze tight. The physical image is a hand closing on the throat.
items.cn: 希腊语 ankhonē 意为「勒紧、窒息」，来自 ankhein「紧紧挤压」。身体意象是一只手扣住喉咙。

items.en: Latin angina named a severe sore throat, especially quinsy, and belongs to the same family as angere, to choke, which gives anxious and anger.
items.cn: 拉丁语 angina 指严重咽痛，尤指扁桃体周围脓肿，与 angere「使窒息」同族，后者产生 anxious 与 anger。

items.en: William Heberden described the chest condition in 1768 and called it angina pectoris, angina of the chest, to separate it from the throat disease.
items.cn: 赫伯登 1768 年描述了这种胸部病症，称其为 angina pectoris「胸部绞痛」，以与喉部疾病区分。

items.en: English took angina in the sixteenth century for the throat sense, and the cardiac meaning spread only after Heberden named it.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 angina 指咽喉义，心脏义在赫伯登命名之后才传播开来。

items.en: In current medicine angina alone almost always means the heart condition, and the throat sense survives mainly in older texts.
items.cn: 在当代医学中，单独的 angina 几乎总指心脏病症，咽喉义主要保存在旧文献中。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the squeeze family angina, anguish, anger and anxious; the near-meaning group lists related conditions.
note.cn: 形近组保留「挤压」词族 angina、anguish、anger、anxious；近义组列出相关病症。

entries.definition: Severe mental or physical suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 极度的精神或肉体痛苦。

entries.definition: A strong feeling of displeasure.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的不快情绪。

entries.definition: Worried and uneasy.
entries.definitionCN: 担忧而不安的。

entries.definition: Relating to angina.
entries.definitionCN: 与心绞痛有关的。

entries.definition: A reduced blood supply to a tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 某组织供血减少。

entries.definition: Tissue death from a blocked supply.
entries.definitionCN: 供血受阻导致的组织坏死。

entries.definition: An abscess beside the tonsil.
entries.definitionCN: 扁桃体旁的脓肿。

entries.definition: A sudden tight muscle pain.
entries.definitionCN: 突发的肌肉紧缩痛。

normalIntro.en: Angina shares a root with anger and anguish: all three come from a squeezing grip.
normalIntro.cn: angina 与 anger、anguish 同根：三者都来自「被攥紧」这个动作。

normal.en: Angina pectoris is the full name; pectoris means of the chest.
normal.cn: angina pectoris 是全称，pectoris 意为「胸部的」。

normal.en: It is uncountable: angina, not an angina, though an angina attack is fine.
normal.cn: 它不可数：angina，不说 an angina，但 an angina attack 可以。

normal.en: Stable angina comes on effort; unstable angina comes at rest.
normal.cn: 稳定型心绞痛在用力时发作，不稳定型在静息时发作。

normal.en: Do not confuse angina with anguish, which is suffering in general.
normal.cn: 别把 angina 与 anguish 混淆，后者泛指痛苦。

normal.en: The adjective is anginal, as in anginal pain.
normal.cn: 形容词是 anginal，如 anginal pain。

abstract.en: Picture a fist tightening behind the breastbone.
abstract.cn: 想象一只拳头在胸骨后收紧。

abstract.en: Imagine a staircase that has to be climbed in stages.
abstract.cn: 想象一段必须分几次爬完的楼梯。

abstract.en: Think of a pipe narrowed until the flow slows.
abstract.cn: 想象一根被收窄到水流变慢的管子。

examples.en: He carries tablets for his angina in his coat pocket.
examples.cn: 他外套口袋里装着治心绞痛的药片。

examples.en: The scan showed no sign of angina at rest.
examples.cn: 扫描显示静息时没有心绞痛迹象。

examples.en: Angina pectoris was first described in the eighteenth century.
examples.cn: 心绞痛最早在 18 世纪被描述。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安绞痛」——安（an）绞（gi）痛（na）：安静下来才不绞痛，一用力就攥住胸口，就是心绞痛。

root: 希腊语 ankhein「挤压」生出 ankhonē「勒紧」，拉丁语作 angina 指窒息性咽痛；赫伯登 1768 年加 pectoris「胸部的」，遂指心肌缺血性胸痛。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one grip: the older strangling throat infection, and the modern squeezing pain of a heart short of blood.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一次攥紧：较早的窒息性喉部感染，以及现代心脏缺血时的压榨性疼痛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible hand tightening on the chest
core.cn: 核心意象：一只看不见的手在胸口收紧

branches.en: A tight chest on the third flight of stairs.
branches.cn: 爬到第三层楼梯时发紧的胸口。

branches.en: Pain that fades when the walk stops.
branches.cn: 停下脚步就消退的疼痛。

branches.en: A swollen throat that barely lets air through.
branches.cn: 肿到几乎不通气的喉咙。

branches.en: An old case note naming quinsy.
branches.cn: 一份写着扁桃体脓肿的旧病历。

branches.en: Both feel like being strangled.
branches.cn: 两者都像被勒住。

intro.en: Angina carries the squeeze root ang-, which also builds anger, anxious and anguish.
intro.cn: angina 带着「挤压」词根 ang-，这个词根还构成 anger、anxious 与 anguish。

latinIntro.en: Greek ankhonē became Latin angina; the same Latin angere, to choke, gives anxious and anger, so the family is easy to keep together.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 ankhonē 变成拉丁语 angina；同一个拉丁语 angere「使窒息」产生 anxious 与 anger，所以这个词族很容易一起记。

latinEntries.example: Angina first named the throat disease.
latinEntries.exampleCN: angina 最初指喉部疾病。
ankhone 是希腊语来源。
angere 产生 anxious 与 anger。

definition_zh: v. 逮捕；拘押；理解，领会；（正式或旧用）忧惧，预感不安
definition_en: To seize someone in the name of the law; in formal use, to grasp a meaning with the mind, or to look ahead to something with fear.
core_image: 伸手一把抓住：抓人、抓意思、抓住不祥的预感
scene: 警方在机场把嫌疑人抓住了。 Police apprehended the suspect at the airport.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：apprehend 在警务语境中指依法把人抓住、拘押，比 arrest 更书面。

senses.title: Seize in the name of the law
senses.definition: to catch and take hold of a person suspected of a crime, the formal police word for arrest
senses.definitionCN: 抓住并控制涉嫌犯罪的人，是 arrest 的正式警务说法
senses.example: Two officers apprehended him outside the station.
senses.exampleCN: 两名警员在车站外将他抓获。
senses.why: The root means seize, and the law simply supplies the reason for seizing, so the physical grip is still visible in the word.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「抓住」，法律只是提供了抓的理由，所以这个词里仍看得见那只手的动作。

senses.title: Grasp with the mind
senses.definition: to understand or perceive something, especially a difficult idea, in formal or academic writing
senses.definitionCN: 理解或察觉某事，尤指难懂的概念，用于正式或学术文字
senses.example: Few readers apprehend the full force of that argument.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有读者能领会那一论证的全部分量。
senses.why: The same seizing is turned inward: instead of a hand closing on a person, the mind closes on a meaning.
senses.whyCN: 同样是「抓住」，只是转向内部：不是手合拢抓住人，而是头脑合拢抓住意思。

senses.title: Look ahead with fear
senses.definition: to anticipate something with anxiety or dread, an older formal sense surviving mainly in apprehensive
senses.definitionCN: 带着焦虑或恐惧预期某事，这一较旧的正式义主要存活在 apprehensive 中
senses.example: She apprehended trouble long before the letter arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 信还没到，她早就预感到有麻烦。
senses.why: Here the mind seizes something that has not happened yet, so grasping ahead turns into fearing ahead.
senses.whyCN: 这里头脑抓住的是尚未发生的事，于是「提前抓住」就变成了「提前害怕」。

intro.en: Apprehend comes from Latin apprehendere, to seize, built from ad-, to, and prehendere, to grasp, which is itself prae-, before, plus hendere, to take.
intro.cn: apprehend 来自拉丁语 apprehendere「抓住」，由 ad-「向」与 prehendere「抓握」构成，而 prehendere 本身又是 prae-「在前」加 hendere「取」。

items.en: Latin prae meant before or in front. In grasping, the hand goes out ahead of the body.
items.cn: 拉丁语 prae 意为「在前、向前」。抓东西时，手总是先伸到身体前面。

items.en: Hendere meant to take or seize, a root also seen in the Greek khandanein, to hold.
items.cn: hendere 意为「取、抓」，这一词根也见于希腊语 khandanein「握住」。

items.en: The two parts fused into prehendere, to lay hold of, the source of English prehensile, as in a monkey's tail.
items.cn: 两部分合成 prehendere「抓住」，它是英语 prehensile 的来源，例如形容猴子的卷尾。

items.en: Adding ad-, to, gave apprehendere, to seize upon, used for both taking a thing and taking an idea.
items.cn: 加上 ad-「向」得到 apprehendere「抓上去」，既用于抓实物，也用于抓概念。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century, first for grasping with the mind and for dreading what is coming.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪吸收该词，起初指用头脑领会，以及忧惧将至之事。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the physical sense had narrowed to lawful seizure, which is why police reports still say apprehend.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，实体义收窄为依法抓捕，因此警方通报至今仍用 apprehend。

note.en: The look-alike group sets apprehend beside comprehend, which only understands, and apprentice, which shares the same Latin root; the near-meaning group gives the everyday verbs.
note.cn: 形近组把 apprehend 与只表「理解」的 comprehend、以及同源的 apprentice 并列；近义组给出日常说法。

entries.definition: To understand fully.
entries.definitionCN: 完全理解。

entries.definition: Anxious about what may happen.
entries.definitionCN: 对可能发生的事感到不安。

entries.definition: A learner bound to a trade.
entries.definitionCN: 绑定学艺的学徒。

entries.definition: To inform someone of something.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事告知某人。

entries.definition: To take into police custody.
entries.definitionCN: 交由警方羁押。

entries.definition: To take hold of suddenly.
entries.definitionCN: 突然一把抓住。

entries.definition: To hold firmly, or to understand.
entries.definitionCN: 牢牢握住；或理解。

entries.definition: To keep someone in custody.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人羁押。

normalIntro.en: Apprehend is ap- plus prehend, to seize: seize a person, seize a meaning, or seize a fear before it arrives.
normalIntro.cn: apprehend 就是 ap- 加 prehend「抓」：抓人、抓意思，或在恐惧到来之前先抓住它。

normal.en: Police apprehend; ordinary speech says arrest.
normal.cn: 警方用 apprehend，日常口语说 arrest。

normal.en: The noun apprehension carries all three senses too.
normal.cn: 名词 apprehension 也带这三层意思。

normal.en: Apprehensive today means anxious, not understanding.
normal.cn: 如今 apprehensive 意为不安，不是「理解的」。

normal.en: Comprehend only understands; apprehend can also arrest.
normal.cn: comprehend 只表理解，apprehend 还能表逮捕。

normal.en: The root prehend also gives prehensile, a gripping tail.
normal.cn: 词根 prehend 还产生 prehensile，指能卷握的尾巴。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing on a shoulder at a gate.
abstract.cn: 想象在登机口一只手扣住肩膀。

abstract.en: Imagine the mind closing on a difficult idea.
abstract.cn: 想象头脑合拢抓住一个难懂的概念。

abstract.en: Think of a shadow grabbed before it lands.
abstract.cn: 想象影子还没落地就先被抓住。

examples.en: The suspect was apprehended within an hour.
examples.cn: 嫌疑人一小时内就被抓获。

examples.en: A child apprehends a rule long before he can state it.
examples.cn: 孩子早就领会了规则，却还很说不出来。

examples.en: Investors apprehended a fall in prices.
examples.cn: 投资者预感到价格会下跌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：ap-「向」+ prehend「抓」——伸手抓过去：抓人是逮捕，抓意思是理解，抓未来是忧惧。

root: 拉丁语 prae-「在前」加 hendere「取」成 prehendere「抓住」，再加 ad-「向」成 apprehendere；英语 14 世纪先取「领会、忧惧」，16 世纪收窄出「依法逮捕」。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses are one act of seizing: a hand on a suspect, a mind on a meaning, and a mind on a fear that has not arrived.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项是同一种「抓住」：手抓住嫌疑人，头脑抓住意思，以及头脑抓住尚未到来的恐惧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand reaching out and closing, on a person, a meaning or a dread
core.cn: 核心意象：伸手一把抓住：抓人、抓意思、抓住不祥的预感

branches.en: Officers closing on a suspect at a gate.
branches.cn: 警员在登机口围住嫌疑人。

branches.en: A fugitive taken after two years.
branches.cn: 逃了两年后被抓的逃犯。

branches.en: A reader finally getting the argument.
branches.cn: 终于读懂论证的读者。

branches.en: Dread felt before the letter arrives.
branches.cn: 信未到就先感到的不安。

branches.en: Both seize something not yet in hand.
branches.cn: 两者抓住的都是还没到手的东西。

intro.en: Apprehend joins ap-, prae- and the seize root hend-/prehens-, which also builds comprehend, prehensile and apprentice.
intro.cn: apprehend 拼合了 ap-、prae- 与「抓」词根 hend-/prehens-，同一词根还构成 comprehend、prehensile 与 apprentice。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is hendere, prehendere and apprehendere; the same family gives the adjective prehensilis, able to grip.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 hendere、prehendere 与 apprehendere；同族还给出形容词 prehensilis「能抓握的」。

latinEntries.exampleCN: hendere 是 prehend 的来源。
prehendere 产生 prehensile。
apprehendere 变成 apprehend。
prae 是 prehendere 的开头。

definition_zh: 突变；变异；（一般意义上的）变化；语音换音
definition_en: a change in genetic material, the process that produces such a change, or a change of form in a broader sense
core_image: 复制过程中一个字母被换掉，整段指令的意思随之改变，纸带上留下一个明显的错位
scene: 复制过程中一个字母被换掉，整段指令的意思随之改变。 A single mutation can switch off a gene that controls cell division.
sceneCN: 这里 mutation 指「遗传物质中的一个改变」（第 1 个义项：基因序列的变化）；句意为一个突变就能关闭控制细胞分裂的基因。可辨识物件：复制纸带、错位字母、红色标记、基因示意图。

senses.title: A change in genetic material
senses.definition: an alteration in the sequence or structure of genetic material
senses.definitionCN: 遗传物质序列或结构的改变
senses.example: A mutation in the control region increased the plant's height.
senses.exampleCN: 控制区的一个突变增加了这株植物的高度。
senses.why: The technical sense is a change at the level of instructions, which is why it can be small in size and large in effect.
senses.whyCN: 技术义指指令层面的改变，因此它可以很小，却产生很大影响。

senses.title: The process that produces variation
senses.definition: the process by which genetic changes arise and supply variation
senses.definitionCN: 遗传改变产生并提供变异的过程
senses.example: Mutation supplies the variation on which selection acts.
senses.exampleCN: 突变为自然选择提供作用其上的变异。
senses.why: As a process, mutation is a source rather than an event, so it appears without an article in population genetics.
senses.whyCN: 作为过程，突变是来源而非事件，因此在群体遗传学中常不带冠词。

senses.title: An organism carrying a change
senses.definition: an organism or strain that carries an altered genetic sequence
senses.definitionCN: 携带改变后遗传序列的生物体或品系
senses.example: The lab keeps a pale-eyed mutation in its fly stocks.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在果蝇品系中保存着一个浅色眼的突变体。
senses.why: Laboratory usage shortens 'a mutant organism' to 'a mutation', especially when the change is the point of interest.
senses.whyCN: 实验室用法把「突变体生物」缩短为「一个突变」，尤其当改变本身是研究重点时。

senses.title: A general change of form
senses.titleCN: 一般意义上的变化、转变
senses.definition: a change in form, character or policy
senses.definitionCN: 形态、性质或政策上的变化
senses.example: The policy underwent several mutations before adoption.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策在通过前经历了几次变化。
senses.why: The older general sense survives outside biology, where mutation means transformation rather than sequence change.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的一般义在生物学之外存续，那里的 mutation 指转变，而非序列改变。

senses.title: Vowel mutation in linguistics
senses.definition: a change in a vowel caused by a following sound, as in umlaut
senses.definitionCN: 由后接音引起的元音变化，如日耳曼语变音
senses.example: The plural shows mutation of the root vowel.
senses.exampleCN: 复数形式显示出词根元音的换音。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century philology used mutation for sound change, a sense older than the genetic one.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪语文学用 mutation 指语音变化，这一义比遗传义更早。

senses.title: Mutation rate
senses.definition: the frequency with which genetic changes arise per generation or unit of time
senses.definitionCN: 每代或每单位时间出现遗传改变的频率
senses.example: Mutation rate depends on repair efficiency.
senses.exampleCN: 突变率取决于修复效率。
senses.why: Measuring changes turns them into a rate, which is why mutation appears in quantitative genetics as a number.
senses.whyCN: 测量改变使其成为比率，因此在数量遗传学中 mutation 以一个数字出现。

senses.title: Mutation breeding
senses.definition: the use of induced genetic changes to produce new varieties
senses.definitionCN: 利用诱发的遗传改变产生新品种
senses.example: Mutation breeding produced a shorter rice variety.
senses.exampleCN: 突变育种产生了一种更矮的水稻品种。
senses.why: Breeding treats mutation as a tool: changes are induced, then selected, without inserting foreign sequences.
senses.whyCN: 育种把突变当作工具：诱发改变后再选择，不插入外来序列。

senses.title: Neutral, harmful or beneficial
senses.titleCN: 中性、有害或有利的突变
senses.definition: a genetic change classified by its effect on the organism
senses.definitionCN: 按对生物体的影响分类的遗传改变
senses.example: Most mutations are neutral, a few are harmful, and a very few help.
senses.exampleCN: 多数突变是中性的，少数有害，极少数有利。
senses.why: The word does not build harm into its meaning; effects are added by the adjectives that surround it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本身不含「有害」，影响是由周围的形容词加上的。

intro.en: Mutation comes from Latin mutatio 'a change', from mutare 'to change'. English used it for general change before genetics gave it a technical sense.
intro.cn: mutation 来自拉丁 mutatio「变化」，源自动词 mutare「改变」。在遗传学赋予它技术义之前，英语已用它表示一般变化。

items.en: Mutare 'to change' is the base of mutatio. Its deeper origin is not established beyond Latin, so any pre-Latin root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: mutare「改变」是 mutatio 的基础。它在拉丁语之外的更深来源未得到确证，因此任何拉丁语之前的词根均属重构。

items.en: Mutatio 'a change' was formed with -tio, the action-noun suffix, from the past participle stem mutat-.
items.cn: mutatio「变化」由过去分词词干 mutat- 加动作名词后缀 -tio 构成。

items.en: Mutation entered English in the fourteenth century with the general sense 'change, alteration'; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: mutation 在 14 世纪以「变化、改动」的一般义进入英语；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Late nineteenth- and early twentieth-century genetics gave mutation the technical sense of a change in hereditary material; the genetic sense is recorded from 1894.
items.cn: 19 世纪末至 20 世纪初的遗传学赋予 mutation「遗传物质改变」的技术义；遗传义从 1894 年起有记录。

items.en: Nineteenth-century philology used mutation for vowel change, especially umlaut; the term i-mutation is recorded from 1874.
items.cn: 19 世纪语文学用 mutation 指元音变化，尤其是变音；i-mutation 这一术语从 1874 年起有记录。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin and sense dates): mutare has no established deeper etymology, and the boundary between general and biological use is not sharply dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（拉丁语之前词源与义项年代）：mutare 没有已确立的更深词源，一般义与生物学义的分界也没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one separates mutation from its family and from a dangerous look-alike; group two separates it from words for variation and change.
note.cn: 第一组把 mutation 与其词族及一个易混形近词分开；第二组把它与「变异」「变化」类词区分。

entries.definition: The verb meaning 'to undergo or cause a mutation'; mutation is the event or process.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「发生或导致突变」的动词；mutation 是事件或过程。

entries.definition: An organism carrying a mutation, or the adjective describing it; it is a noun of the changed body.
entries.definitionCN: 携带突变的生物体，或描述它的形容词；指被改变的身体。

entries.definition: Relating to a mutation; the adjective does not name the change itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与突变相关的；形容词不命名改变本身。

entries.definition: From mutilare 'to maim, cut off', not mutare: the act of damaging or removing a part. The resemblance is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 mutilare「残害、割去」，并非 mutare：指损伤或割除某一部分。相似是偶然的。

entries.definition: Difference among individuals; mutation is one source of variation, not variation itself.
entries.definitionCN: 群体内个体间的差异；突变是变异的来源之一，并非变异本身。

entries.definition: A change in something, often deliberate; mutation stresses a change in form or sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的改变，常为有意；mutation 强调形态或序列的改变。

entries.definition: The broad everyday word; mutation is narrower and often technical.
entries.definitionCN: 宽泛的日常用词；mutation 更窄，常带技术性。

entries.definition: A complete change of form, often dramatic; mutation can be a single small change.
entries.definitionCN: 形态的彻底改变，常较剧烈；mutation 可以是单个微小改变。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mutare 'to change' + -tion: the act of changing.
normal.cn: mutare「改变」+ -tion：改变的行为。

normal.en: The family runs mutate, mutation, mutant and mutational.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mutate、mutation、mutant 与 mutational。

normal.en: Mutation rate, point mutation and mutation breeding are fixed phrases.
normal.cn: 突变率、点突变与突变育种是固定搭配。

normal.en: Mutation is not automatically harmful: most changes are neutral.
normal.cn: 突变并非自动有害：多数改变是中性的。

normal.en: Linguistic mutation means vowel change, an older sense.
normal.cn: 语言学中的 mutation 指元音换音，是更早的义项。

abstract.en: Picture a single wrong letter turning a recipe into a different dish.
abstract.cn: 想象一个错字母把食谱变成另一道菜。

abstract.en: Picture a copying machine that occasionally drops a mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一台复印机偶尔漏掉一个记号。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour changing as it passes from mouth to mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻在口耳相传中改变。

examples.en: The mutation was traced to a single base change.
examples.cn: 这个突变被追溯到单个碱基改变。

examples.en: Mutation is the raw material of evolution.
examples.cn: 突变是进化的原料。

examples.en: The old word underwent a mutation in meaning over two centuries.
examples.cn: 这个旧词在两个世纪里经历了词义变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: mut（改变）+ ation（名词尾）——改变的结果 → 突变；一般义是「变化」。

root: 拉丁 mutatio「变化」← mutare「改变」；mutare 在拉丁语之外的更深来源不确定，相关原始印欧语词根均属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one changed unit: the change itself, the process, the carrier, a general alteration, a vowel shift, a rate, a breeding tool and a classification by effect.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个被改变的单位展开：改变本身、过程、携带者、一般变化、元音换音、比率、育种工具与按效果分类。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one letter replaced during copying, and the meaning of the whole strip shifts.
core.cn: 核心意象：复制时一个字母被替换，整条纸带的意思随之改变。

branches.en: CHANGE AND SOURCE: a change in the material, and the process that keeps supplying it.
branches.cn: 改变与来源：物质中的改变，以及不断提供改变的过程。

branches.en: CARRIER AND EFFECT: an organism that carries the change, and how its effect is classified.
branches.cn: 携带者与效果：携带改变的生物体，以及效果如何分类。

branches.en: GENERAL CHANGE: policy and form can mutate outside biology.
branches.cn: 一般变化：政策与形态在生物学之外也能改变。

branches.en: VOWEL CHANGE: philology used the word for sound shift before genetics did.
branches.cn: 元音变化：语文学在遗传学之前就用这个词指语音转变。

branches.en: MEASURE AND TOOL: a rate to count, and a breeding method to use.
branches.cn: 度量与工具：可计数的比率，以及可使用的育种方法。

intro.en: Mutation is a Latin action noun; its stem also builds the verb, the carrier noun and the adjective, and the same root appears in words for change and unchangeability.
intro.cn: mutation 是拉丁动作名词；其词干还构成动词、携带者名词与形容词，同一词根也出现在表示「可变」与「不可变」的词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin mutare gives mutate, mutation, mutant and mutable; com- and in- build commutation and immutable, trans- builds transmutation. All belong to the same changing root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mutare 衍生 mutate、mutation、mutant 与 mutable；com- 与 in- 构成 commutation 与 immutable，trans- 构成 transmutation。它们都属同一「改变」词根。

items.example: The root names the act of changing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名改变的动作。

items.example: Mutatio is the direct source of mutation.
items.exampleCN: mutatio 是 mutation 的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix makes an action noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成动作名词。

items.example: Commutation of a sentence reduced the penalty.
The transmutation of elements was once alchemy.
items.exampleCN: 元素转变曾属于炼金术。
